name: Taste
desc: She poured strange ingredients into the pot, mixing in the purest love and care.
memoryDesc: Beneath its bitter, inedible peel lie the sweet and sour grains of memory.

dialogues.content: There we go. Try this, Berry.
Hmm, okay...
So, why were you so eager to take the ladle from me earlier?
Because you were about to add pomegranates to the fish soup!
What's wrong with that? I remember you used to love pomegranates when you were little.
Remember last year when we walked past that big pomegranate tree? You picked a whole bag of them. Too bad they all rolled down the hill when you slipped. You said it was such a waste.
So this time, I picked some just for you... Don't you like them anymore?
It's not about the pomegranates. It's just that pomegranates and fish might not taste good together, don't you think?
But you like berries dipped in milk... It's hard to buy milk here on this island, so I thought soup would work just as well.

{性别:It's not really the same|It's really not the same}. Fish soup has a strong salty, fishy taste, so it doesn't go well with sweet fruits. Plus, fruits are best eaten fresh; they'd lose their crunch if boiled.
And even if you were to cook pomegranates, you should at least peel them first...
Uh... this is way more complicated than I thought.
It is. "The interplay of ingredients is a culinary art. Only the right combinations bring out the best in each" — That's what they say in "The Art of Cooking".
So, the funny sour taste in that stew last time was because I added berries?
...I think so.
And the time you said the shrimp was too rich, was it because I used honey instead of salt? I thought honey was better since it's more expensive...
...That's right.
Ah... So I messed up all those times...
I've heard that honey is sweet, and sweetness is good; while bitterness, like in chicory, is bad. But I can't really tell what sweet or bitter tastes like.
I was taught very young that food is just a means of filling the stomach; tasty food is a distraction from what's important and might lead to indulgence, so I wouldn't need a sense of taste.
They made me drink a potion; and ever since then, I haven't been able to taste anything.
Berry...
Sorry, I've made you eat so much awful food...
...Not at all. Your cooking is usually great. Those were just minor hiccups — everyone has off days.

I always look forward to trying whatever new dish you've invented... And you know what? It's the author of "The Art of Cooking" who has no taste! They don't appreciate innovative ingredient combinations.
You really think so? Or are you just saying that...
Have I ever lied to you?
...Right.
Well, can you tell me what a pomegranate tastes like?
It's a bit sweet, a bit sour, and — well, let's keep that a secret for now.
Why?
Tasting is something you should experience yourself.
If it's the potion that made you lose your taste, there's got to be something that can bring it back, right?
Alright, starting today, I'm going to earn as much as I can, so that I can soon get off this island to find that cure!
Once your sense of taste is back, we'll try all the delicious food out there in the world... and buy loads of your favourite pomegranates!
...The world beyond this island, mm.

name: Wounds
desc: You are the reason I must be strong.
memoryDesc: A broken feather, tinged with the salty tang of the sea and a faint trace of blood — evidence of a young girl's naivety and courage.

dialogues.content: Home at last. Quick, Berry, take a seat!
Huh?
You got hurt, didn't you? Let me see your hand... I'll bandage you up.
It's okay. Just a scratch.
Don't fight me on this.
...Okay.
How many times have I told you? Always protect yourself first when there's danger.
Like with that sea eagle just now — why didn't you just dodge? Why did you have to confront it head-on and get scratched... Does it still hurt?
You were right behind me. If I had dodged, it would have hurt you.
I could have dodged it too!
I'll be more careful next time.
*sighs* You always say that.
When we were kids, some bad grown-ups often picked on us. But you'd rather fight them head-on than back down with smart words, and you always ended up bruised and battered.
You'd always promise to be more careful next time, but every "next time" turned out to be another "Sorry, I'll be more careful next time."
I'm not like you. You're good with words and always know what to say to different people. But I can't do that... People are too complicated. I never really understand what they really mean.
For me, the only way to solve problems is with what I have in my hands. If not weapons, then fists or teeth.
It's okay. If you're not great with words, I'll speak for you, just like you've always protected me like a shield.
But you have to promise me to break this charging head-on habit, okay? You're strong now, you don't have to put yourself in danger anymore — it must hurt a lot.
Pain is nothing; it'll pass if I just bear it for a while. "Those who don't fear pain have no weaknesses"... This way of fighting is the most efficient.
...Fine! If it works so well, guess I should learn it too. Next time there's danger, I'll just charge right in.
You... No, it's different for you!
What's the difference? Just saying that worries you, doesn't it? You should know how your habit worries me, too.
So, at least for my sake — take good care of yourself, okay?
Breaking a habit isn't easy... but I'll try.
Mm-hmm. Let's really make it stick this time!

name: The Beyond
desc: This shore is my whole world, a cage forged just for me.
memoryDesc: Even from within a cage, there are still those who gaze upon the horizon.

dialogues.content: {nickname}, are you scared?
I'm not scared when you're with me. If anything, I'm a bit... excited. This could be our <H>chance</>.
I've been thinking... maybe we can leave Purgatorio Island someday. What do you think?
Leave? Why, aren't you happy here?
It's not that. It's just... this island is so small — you can circle it in less than a day.
The people here think this tiny island is the whole world. They believe the ocean and the cosmos just revolve around this rock, day after day.
But I know that's not true! Remember that book, "Betwixt Leaves And Branches"?

Yeah, it was brought back from Hyperborea by the fishermen. The kids took all the snacks, and that book was tossed aside in the cabin like rubbish. You picked it up and brought it back like it was treasure.

Right. That book was a real eye-opener. It showed me that Purgatorio Island isn't the centre of the world — it's merely a speck on the map, tinier than an ant. Across the sea, far beyond the Heaventree, lies a vast continent...
And its name is "Atlasia."

North of us is the Hyperborean Empire, where the ancestors of the villagers come from. It's a vast land that stretches from the southern coasts to the northern snowfields, all connected by long trains.
Even further north, beyond Hyperborea, lie endless mountains and seas of floating ice, home to countless small settlements, each with its own fascinating customs.
To the south is the Elysian Church, the oldest civilization. It's a divine realm where gods live in a tower high above the sky. And to the east—
What's wrong, Berry? Are you alright?
I'm fine, just a bit tired. Let's not talk about this for now, okay?
Right, you must be exhausted, and here I am going on and on. Let's go to the cave and have some rest.
...You're right. This island is a prison, and we've shut the world out.
But what if the world outside isn't as wonderful as you imagine?
{nickname}, {nickname}?
Phew... you're okay.
Berry! You're covered in blood... What happened?! Did those monsters hurt you?!
It's Filthoid blood, not mine. They've attacked the village.
I figured as much. I was hiding here and heard those beasts charging like mad down the mountain.
It's weird... Those Filthoids usually keep to the deep woods. We barely see them. What drove them to suddenly come out and attack people?
It didn't make sense to me. I wanted to come find you right away, but then I thought with your combat skills, you might handle things better on your own.
Mm, you did the right thing staying put and waiting for me.
The village is crawling with Filthoids. Thankfully, it's still safe around here. Let's hole up for now. I've brought enough food to last a few days.
What about the villagers?
They were heading to the docks when I left, probably trying to escape by boat. No time to worry about them now, we need to find shelter quickly.
Let's go back to the cave I was hiding in.

name: Tomorrow
desc: All has ended, and all begins anew.
memoryDesc: The fleeting moments of happiness are forever gone. But thankfully, there is always tomorrow.

dialogues.content: Ugh, those Filthoids have found us... {nickname}, hide behind that tree!
Berry, Behind you!
What?!
{nickname}! Are you okay?
Berry, I think I might...
I've patched up all your wounds. It should be all right for now.
No fever, your breathing's steady... looks like you're just worn out and fast asleep. Right, you've really been through a lot these past few days.
You always lecture me when I get hurt.
Now the tables have turned, and here you are, sleeping like a log... not giving me a chance to lecture you.
You always wonder why I feel the need to protect you... Hmm, why is that?
You're right, I'm just like you — sand in my eyes makes them itch, a tickle on my palm makes me laugh, and a cut on my hand hurts and bleeds.
There's no real difference between us. So why do I always feel this deep need to protect you... as if it's simply part of who I am?
I think I'm starting to understand now... maybe it's because you taught me these things—
Growing up with you, I learned that this is how people should live — we're not machines built for fighting and killing; we laugh when we're happy, and cry when sad.
When we're scared, it's okay to shout out; when in pain, we should find comfort in someone's embrace.
There's <H>her</> — don't know if I have the right to call her "mother" — and then there's you...
The two of you made me feel like I could live like a real person.
...Sleep tight, {nickname}. I'll keep watch over you tonight.

name: Point of Attack
desc: A playwright once told me that to drive a protagonist into action, you must first strip away all their hope. How I wish reality didn't work that way.
memoryDesc: Meticulously crafted in both size and form to perfectly conceal broken horns, allowing a Charon boy to pass as an ordinary Sola.

dialogues.content: Who are you?
Tell me, Parsifal — what happened? Who broke your horns?
I don't care what anyone outside this troupe thinks or does. Bullying of any kind is absolutely forbidden in Magic Flute. We will not let ignorance, prejudice, or hatred defile the sanctity of art!
Don't be afraid, Parsifal. Just tell the truth. I promise you, the troupe will handle this fairly and remove any bully from our ranks.

"We will not let ignorance, prejudice, or hatred defile the sanctity of art"... If the troupe didn't have the unspoken rule that "Charons cannot perform on stage," Ms Violetta, I might actually believe you.
That's because—!
...Forgive me, Ms Violetta! I didn't mean it that way.

I wasn't questioning your intentions. I know that, as our mentor, you never care whether we're Solarians or Charons. It's only the narrow-mindedness and bigotry of certain audience members that fosters this divide.
Everyone in the troupe has been kind to me. No one bullied me. As for the horns... I cut them off <H>myself</>.
...Parsifal...
I want to stand on that stage, Ms Violetta. I want to sing the lyrics with my own voice, see the audience with my own eyes, step into that world illuminated by the spotlight...
As long as these "demon horns" are gone, I'll finally be able to go on stage, right?
Parsifal... you poor child...
It's just... cutting off a part of my own body hurts more than I imagined. Please, give me a little more time. I promise I'll remove what's left of the broken horns and—
Stop it! And don't ever do anything to your horns again.
...I've made up my mind. In the next performance of Children From the Snowfield, you'll take the stage alongside Susanna and Fane. You'll be the lead — you'll play the "Nameless Fairy."
...What did you just say?
Violetta! I could hear you spouting nonsense from all the way across the room — you're making Parsifal the lead!?

Are you out of your mind? By tomorrow, the entire city of Icelake will be buzzing with the news that the Magic Flute troupe cast a Charon as their lead! Do you have any idea what that will do to our decades-long reputation?
Don't worry, Ms Putsch. It's a fairy role. Some extravagant headgear will fit the character perfectly. We'll have the props master design something dramatic. No one will notice Parsifal is a Charon.

And don't fret about the rest of the cast. I'll speak to them personally — I'll do my best to minimise any trouble for you. If things really turn messy, just say it was my idea and that I forced the entire troupe into it.
Besides, we both know Parsifal is the finest singer in the troupe. His talent surpasses even mine at his age. Otherwise, you wouldn't have kept him singing behind the curtain for so long.
I refuse to watch such a rare and precious gift remain buried in the shadows, never given the chance to grow. Parsifal deserves the opportunity to shine in the spotlight.
But Children From the Snowfield is one of our most celebrated productions in recent years. If we suddenly cast a newcomer as the lead, people are bound to be curious about his identity.
You know how ruthless Icelake's tabloids can be. How exactly do we keep his identity under wraps?
Well... In Icelake, is there any story more riveting than a headline about the beloved local star Violetta's latest romance?
Wait... Are you saying you plan to...
I've been feeling rather bored lately. Perhaps I'll ask Baron Andrew out for a stroll, maybe a cosy afternoon tea date... Hehe, I wonder what headlines the reporters will concoct this time.
*sigh* Fine... But I can't let you shoulder this alone. Like I've always said: once you're in the troupe, you're family. Whatever comes our way, we face it together. I'll handle the props.
Ms Violetta, Director Putsch, thank you for your kindness. But if my identity is exposed, I'll bring disgrace to the troupe...
Parsifal, look me in the eye and tell me — do you believe in your own performance?
...Yes, I do.

Then that's all that matters. You're my most talented student. Your only task is to use your voice and your craft to help the audience immerse themselves in the story. Make them fall in love with the character — not obsess over who's playing the role.
...I understand. I'll give every rehearsal my all. I'll make them see... a real fairy brought to life from the script and score.

All right, all right, don't overthink it. Just perform like you always do — that alone is more than enough. Though... Hehe, I must admit, even I'm getting a little excited. Who knows? This might just become our greatest production of Children From the Snowfield yet.
It will be. I'll give a performance so remarkable it'll make you — and my mother — proud of me.
I'm looking forward to it.

Ladies and gentlemen, today marks the debut of Parsifal Snowfield, the newest performer in the Magic Flute troupe. Let us shower him with flowers and applause — and look forward to the brilliance this rising star will bring in the future!
What are you doing?

Wow... The lead's performance tonight was absolutely stunning! I could've listened to him forever. Parsifal, right? How have I never heard of him before? Could he be a visiting star from another city?
Though his voice sounds a lot like the previous lead's. Is it some sort of imitation show?
Lady Violetta—!! Oh, my radiant rose, my tender moonlight, the horticulturist of my soul, the goddess of my dreams!
—What...?
Please, tell me! What the papers wrote — it can't be true, right? You would never lower yourself by dating a playboy like that Baron! You wouldn't tarnish your purity like that — Lady Violetta!!!
Ms Violetta, watch out!
Get out of my way, you little twerp— Wait... you... you're a Charon!?
That boy — that new performer is a Charon!
A Charon on stage? Have they lost their minds!?
How dare you deceive us! Let a demon like that set foot on stage and defile our eyes! Where's the troupe's director? Show yourself!
This is all my fault! I lied to the director and Ms Violetta — it has nothing to do with anyone else! Please don't—
Shut it! How disgusting... a Charon soiling Children From the Snowfield! Ugh, and now you've dirtied my clothes too! Get off the stage already!
BOO! Off you go! Beat it!
Argh!
Please calm down! Ms Violetta, Parsifal... ah!
No...! Don't hit him! Stop this at once! Someone, go to the Security Bureau and bring the city guards — hurry!
BOO! Away with you! Beat it!
You dirty liar! You nasty fraud! <W>Demon's Child!</>
No... I'm not...
I just wanted to get on the stage. That's all.
But what fell from the stage wasn't flowers — it was blood.
I am a wretched prisoner, offering up evidence of guilt with my own hands.
And then... I await my judgment.

name: Lock In
desc: When hope is shattered and every path of retreat is severed, the protagonist can never return to the life they once knew. I once tried to delay that moment for as long as I could.
memoryDesc: A journalist, with an abundance of flowery language, tells the tale of a wealthy merchant's legendary life, extolling his wisdom, elegance, and generosity — as though tantalisingly waving a golden straw before the world.

dialogues.content: Who are you?
I was told you wished to see me, Mr Young Performer.
...Good evening, Mr Glenville.
My name is Parsifal Snowfield, a performer with the Magic Flute troupe. On hearing of your presence, our director asked me to deliver her greetings, along with a small token of appreciation.
This is a commemorative pin to mark the theatre's 200th anniversary. We'd be honoured if you would accept it.
Oh? I don't attend the theatre often, so this is quite unexpected. What an honour. Do extend my gratitude to Ms Putsch.
We consider it only right to express our gratitude to distinguished patrons like yourself. I hope my unannounced visit hasn't caused any inconvenience.
Not at all. My wife and children haven't arrived yet, so I happen to be free. You mentioned you're a performer — are you performing tonight?
...No, I'm not on tonight's programme. In fact, beyond delivering the troupe's greetings, I came with some... personal matters I'd like to discuss with you.
Oh? By all means — please go ahead. I'm always happy to lend an ear to a young friend's concerns.
Before I begin, would you mind taking a look at this old letter and this pocket watch? Perhaps they might remind you of certain... past events.

This pocket watch is rather valuable, engraved with the Glenville family crest — yes, it must have been one of my custom orders. And this letter... hmm, it's unmistakably my handwriting. "To Herzeleide"...
That's right. It's a letter you wrote twenty-two years ago to a woman named Herzeleide Snowfield. She was my mother... She passed away a few years ago due to illness.
My mother never mentioned my father's identity. But while sorting through her belongings, I found a collection of letters the two of you exchanged. This is one of them.
According to the letter, you and my mother met over twenty years ago at a viscount's banquet. It was love at first sight... and that banquet took place exactly ten months before I was born.
...Are you suggesting that you're my son?
I believe... yes, I am.
What are you looking for?
Wait... that thing on your head... it's... You're a Charon!?
Huh? Yes, I am. Don't you remember? My mother, Herzeleide, was a Charon—

You truly are a marvellous "performer," aren't you? Dressing the part, spinning your tales so convincingly, making me let my guard down — I welcomed you, listened to all your drivel, and all along, you were nothing but a fraud!
No, I'm not a fraud!
Ridiculous! A Charon woman bearing my child? Don't make me laugh! Who are you, really? What's your game?
Ah, I see how it is — you must be one of those stooges from the Icelake Daily! That bald hack running the paper takes money from my rivals to invent absurd scandals and tarnish my name.
I—I'm not! Everything I said is true! Didn't you just say you remembered my mother and how much you loved her?
Enough! I was never short of ladies back then! How am I supposed to know which one you're talking about!?
Ahem, Master Glenville, the show is about to begin.
...Hmph. Listen, Mr Came-Out-Of-Nowhere, I don't recall saying any such nonsense, and my butler here can attest to that. Perhaps your hearing is defective.
I've heard that hearing loss among Charons is considered a bad omen. Perhaps you should take better care of your health. Now, if you'd kindly leave my box, or else I'll be forced to summon security.
Forgive me for not seeing you out, but I need to remind my staff of their responsibilities — apparently, they've forgotten not to allow riffraff of questionable origins inside.
"Riffraff"...?
...I see. My apologies for wasting your time. I'll take my leave.
Ha... hahahaha! What a marvellous surprise! Who would have imagined I'd have such a refined and talented son?
If only my two little rascals at home had half your poise and manners, I might have fewer wrinkles on my forehead!
I owe it all to my mother. Though we lived a modest life, she was always strict about how I carried myself.
After all, your mother was the epitome of grace and elegance.
You remember her?
Of course, I remember her vividly! In those days, she was utterly captivating — wherever she went, admirers flocked around her, drawn like moths to a flame.
That evening, I had the privilege of dancing with her. I was so exhilarated I couldn't sleep a wink! And to think she chose to spend the night with me... it felt like a dream come true.
She wore a deep crimson gown that night, her skin glowing like fresh snow in the moonlight. Her cheeks were flushed — perhaps from the wine — shining like roses in bloom.

You becoming an opera performer — surely that was her influence, wasn't it? We used to attend the opera together often. She knew every lyric by heart and would sing them around the house all the time.
Yes...! When I was little, she used to teach me to sing whenever she had a moment. She was my very first mentor.
But then, one day, she left me. Disappeared without a word. I searched high and low for her, but she was nowhere to be found.
I must apologise, my boy... I wasn't honest with you earlier. Losing her was why I stopped going to the opera. It was my fault... If I had looked just a little longer, perhaps she wouldn't have—
From my earliest memories, my mother's health was always fragile. You know how proud she was — maybe she didn't want you to see her in that condition, so she just...
Oh, my silly girl... How could she think I'd care about something like that? Not giving me a chance even to say goodbye — how could she be so cruel?

It's all in the past now. Please don't let it weigh on you. I'm just glad you still remember her. To be honest, until a moment ago, I was still worried that my sudden visit might seem too abrupt or inappropriate.
How could I? With a son as exceptional as you, I couldn't be happier!

In fact, the Glenville family has long considered investing in the Galea Theatre. It would be mutually beneficial, after all. This time, I'm here specifically to discuss the matter with Ms Putsch. It'd be wonderful if someone from the troupe were willing to help make the connection...
Speaking of which, my boy, which roles have you played? With your talents, you must always be cast in the lead, surely?
I—I've played many roles. Most recently... I was the lead in Children From the Snowfield.

Good heavens, you don't mean the production from earlier this month, do you? A business associate invited me to see it, said it was incredibly popular and that tickets were practically impossible to get. Unfortunately, I was out of town on business and couldn't attend.
What a pity! Had I known the lead was my son, I'd have cancelled everything to be there — then proudly boasted about you to my friend.
Will the play be staged again soon?
...I doubt it will be put on again in the near future. But I'm well-versed in many other productions, and I'm keen to explore new roles going forward.
That's the spirit! A young man should always be eager to try new things. You may look like your mother, but I'd say you've inherited a bit of my adventurous streak. So, when's your next performance?
Actually... that's why I wanted to speak with you. I've run into some difficulties.

After my last performance, there was a confrontation with a few audience members who forced their way onto the stage. It drew the attention of the Security Bureau, and since then, the troupe has faced a wave of protests. As a result, I'm temporarily barred from performing. I was hoping... perhaps you could help me navigate this situation.
Ha! That's how it is, isn't it? The moment you taste success, jealous vermin crawl out of the shadows, desperate to drag you down.

In all my years of business, I've faced more rumours and slander than I could count — both openly and behind my back. But don't you worry — from now on, I'll handle these nuisances. You just concentrate on your craft and leave the rest to me.
Here's what we'll do — tell me who those troublemakers are. I'll make it clear to everyone in Icelake that if they dare lay a finger on Morris Glenville's son, they'll pay dearly for it!
Thank you, Mr Glenville! But truly, there's no need to go to so much trouble. All I want is the opportunity to keep performing.
Haha, shouldn't you be calling me "Father," my boy? From today on, we're family.
Come and have a seat, and let's talk properly... Oh, and why are you still wearing a hat indoors? Take it off and hand it to the butler.
It's fine. I'll hold onto it myself.
Ha...
What a farce.
I am a gambler consumed by despair, casting my last chip onto the felt.
And then... I lose everything I'd been looking for.

name: Twist
desc: Audiences love twists and surprises, so the stories playwrights weave must ebb and flow. But my story... it seems to have but one direction — downward, ever deeper, an endlessly spiralling descent.
memoryDesc: The cold metal bears the engraved number "47" — so worn it is barely legible. The name this soul once held has long since been erased, never to be known again.

dialogues.content: Who are you?
What do you wish to say?
Hmm? Are you trying to say something? What is it?
Wh... Where...
What ha...ppened... to... me...
What? I can't make out what you're saying.
Where... am I? What... happened to me...?
Um, this is the 6th Legion's lab...
The 6th Legion... That's right. I passed the recruitment tests. But why... why am I in a lab?
I feel awful... What did you do to me?
You... you don't remember? This is the third time you've asked me that. You underwent alchemical augmentation.
Augmentation?
What... is this...?
...It's my hand?
This monstrous claw... is my hand!?
W—Well, it's not so bad, is it? Your body's stronger now. For Charons like you, having a chance to serve the Empire in this way is... is the highest... honour...
A—And you're lucky. You know, many of the earlier subjects didn't even survive the grafting process...
"Lucky"? Is that what you just said?
This is your idea of "lucky"?
...Sorry.
I am a savage beast, commanded to tear apart every last prey.
And then, silently bury myself in the dark.
(After that... who knows how many days passed.)
(In such endless darkness, time itself had become meaningless.)
Hmm... The sedative concentration in his blood is dropping. Should I increase the dosage?
It's you... again.
Ah—! How come you're awake again?
What's going on? Why is the sedative concentration so low?
S—Sorry, Professor! I'll increase the dosage right away!
Will I...
Hmm? What's that thing mumbling?
Will I... ever go back to the way I was?
Go back? Hahaha! What are you talking about? I don't think we have done anything to your brain. Was it the fire that damaged it, or were you born this stupid?
What we need is a monster, a vessel, a reliable weapon — anything but you. How could we possibly turn you back?
Why... WHY!?
"Why"?
Would you explain to an ant why you're crushing it underfoot? Would you justify to a cherry why you're chewing it to a pulp?
Oh, wait — I forgot. A wretched thing like you has probably never even tasted a cherry.
Why is the injection taking so long? Hurry up and get it done.
It's done, Professor.
...I have.
Hmm? You have what?
I have tasted a cherry. The first time my mother and I were taken in by the theatre, the director treated us to a hearty meal. For dessert, we had cherry pie.
I still remember when it was cut open — deep red syrup spilling from the golden crust, its sweet aroma filling the dining hall at once. It was so much richer than any cheap candy could ever be.
The director said she couldn't eat sweets at her age, but I knew... she just wanted me to have her slice. She could see how much I loved that cherry pie.
In those days, Ms Violetta — my mentor — was a bright young woman. She took dainty nibbles of her portion, all the while checking a compact mirror to ensure she hadn't gotten crumbs on her face.

And then there were little Susanna and Dennis, bickering over who'd get the last slice. They decided to settle it with a line-reading contest, but both messed up so badly that Ms Violetta nearly choked from frustration.
Ha... I wonder how they're all doing now. Without this "lying fraud" around, the troupe can finally perform properly... right?
Is there a problem?
Nothing serious, Professor. The subject's mental state is unstable — he's been rambling nonsense again. I was just about to increase the sedative dosage.
Good call. You've shown considerable progress these past few days.
Thank you, Professor!
(Ugh... My mind... it's slipping again. My throat... it's failing me...)
That's more like it. Just keep quiet.
(Ah... I see.)
(You — have become a monster too.)

name: False Resolution
desc: Perhaps I was never destined for a beautiful story — but even so, I have the right to choose how it ends.
memoryDesc: Bright, warm, and tender, they beckon to the children lingering in the night, guiding them home. Yet for a beast lost to the shadows, such lights will forever remain out of reach.

dialogues.content: Who are you?
Where are you off to?
I am a proud performer, delivering my swan song.
And in the end, I take my bow and leave the stage.
If we had met as humans... would it have been the four of us leaving the theatre together, laughing and chatting?

Susanna wouldn't let you off the hook as her free accompanist. And knowing you, you'd agree without hesitation. Before we knew it, we'd all be out there, rehearsing on the freezing streets just to humour her.
Oh wait... you had family. Your no-nonsense big sister would probably show up to drag you home. Or maybe... maybe you'd convince her to join us instead — yes, that's more like how it would end up.
No. That's never going to happen. What am I thinking, now that things have come to this?
That stage, those scripts, those friends... they belong to Parsifal. I no longer have them.
But—
Here, there's one final performance. One only I can deliver.
I've gathered paints and oils, enough to make myself look almost identical to you. I've seen your secret hideout. And with the harmonica chain you left me...
The performer, the costume, the props, the set — all ready. Now, all that's left is for the curtain to rise.
Don't worry, Blues. I'll keep my promise and see it through.

name: Death is Gentle
desc: Sometimes, false hope is more cruel than despair itself, as it prolongs yesterday's suffering into a future where closure should have already been found.
memoryDesc: The dark crimson liquid inside had long since solidified, clinging to the transparent shards. It was once a miracle desperately sought by a young girl.

dialogues.content: Thank you for having me, my child. It's been many years since I've had the pleasure of sitting down and conversing with a friend like this. I must admit, I do miss it.
"Many years"? How long are we talking about?
Hmm... It has probably been over a decade, I would say. And before that... perhaps a few centuries.
Huh...?
Hehe, I must have caught you by surprise. In truth, my age stretches far beyond the land beneath our feet — older than even the Hyperborean Empire itself.

options.content: That's incredible.
What's your secret? Please teach me.

dialogues.content: I didn't realise you had so many years of wisdom, Lady Nifle... It's truly an honour to speak with you.
The magic powers of Daimons differ greatly — most are innate or passed down through bloodlines. I'm afraid it is not something that can be easily taught.
There is no need for such formality. Think of me simply as a friend, someone with whom you may share your thoughts.
That's alright. I was just joking around. But seriously...

But tell me, what would you like to discuss? I have long distanced myself from the fleeting trends of the world. However, if you seek stories from distant lands or times long past, I would not mind sharing what I know.

options.content: Yes, please!

dialogues.content: I recall you saying that you were a "Ferrywoman of the Misty Sea." I must admit, I'm still not entirely clear on what that means.
Hmm... Perhaps you've heard of the Charon lore.

In the beginning, the world was a chaotic sea of mist. From this mist arose the sacred tree, its branches adorned with pure white flowers. These flowers gave birth to our primordial ancestor — the goddess of life, Mother Embla, from whom all living things came.
All life emerged from the Misty Sea. After drifting through the river of the "Mortal Realm," all things eventually return to the Misty Sea.
The role of the Ferrywoman is to guide wandering souls back to the Misty Sea. Thus, I spend most of my time listening to the murmurs of the departed, responding with whispers.
That sounds... rather unsettling.
Hehe, yes. To most, death is indeed a terrifying notion.

options.content: Don't you think so?

dialogues.content: Hmm... Since the topic has arisen, allow me to share with you a tale about "death." It is the story of a girl and her ailing younger sister.

The girl and her sister were born into poverty in Elysium. Orphaned at a tender age, they had no choice but to fend for themselves, enduring both hunger and cold. Alas, one harsh winter, the younger sister succumbed to a fatal illness.
Desperate to save her sister, the girl searched far and wide for any possible cure, yet none came. It was then she heard a tale from an old man — the legend of the "golden blood."
It is said that a woman, blessed by the gods, was once revered by the nobles of Elysium. Her blood, believed to cure ailments and preserve youth, was as precious as gold.

Countless nobles offered vast sums of gold for but a single phial of her blood. Yet, before long, war descended upon Elysium. During the Great Migration, she was taken by rebels, and her whereabouts were lost to history.

Driven by her resolve to save her sister, the girl set out on a long and arduous journey. Eventually, much to her astonishment, she discovered that the woman was still alive — over a century old — and living in Aethyrie, the Woodland Kingdom.

So, the girl carried her dying sister through mountains and rivers, and finally they found the so-called "blessed woman." Cradling her nearly lifeless sister, the girl tearfully begged for just a drop of her miraculous blood.

But the "golden blood," once believed to be a divine gift, turned out to be nothing more than a myth — a tale spun by the greed of the nobles to conceal their own sins. In truth, the woman had been imprisoned for her healing powers, enduring great suffering before finally escaping Elysium.
She had long since decided never to use her abilities again, lest they cause even more pain and suffering.
So the girl went through all that for nothing...?
No... wait. Since you've spent so much time telling the story, surely it's not over yet?
Hehe, you're perceptive. After much hesitation, the woman eventually agreed to help.
Why would she do that?

Because, you see, the woman had not fully closed her heart to the idea of healing others. Twice before, she had tried to use her blood to extend the life of others — once for her closest friend, and once for her daughter.
Her friend was a valiant warrior, fatally wounded on the battlefield. Her daughter, a respected scholar, was peacefully nearing the end of her days.
Although their circumstances were vastly different, their decisions were the same: both refused to accept the woman's blood, choosing death over a life prolonged by such a means.
The sorrow in the girl's eyes reminded the woman of her own past, and her thoughts turned to a question that had long lingered:
What could have been, had she been able to save her friend and daughter? What might the path she did not take have offered?
She needed to know the answer. So, she cut her own arm and gave her blood to the girl.
The ailing little sister drank the "golden blood" and soon regained consciousness.

options.content: That's wonderful news.
It's not that simple, is it?

dialogues.content: You are a kind child... but the so-called miraculous blood is, in truth, but an illusion. It is a fantasy people have chosen to believe in.
Indeed. The so-called miraculous blood is, in truth, but an illusion. It is a fantasy people have chosen to believe in.
The woman's blood did possess a unique power, but it neither cured disease nor halted the process of ageing. Instead, it preserved the body in a state of mere "existence."
Like an insect trapped in amber — unspoiled, yet not truly "alive."
So, after drinking the blood, her little sister did not die, but her body was still in an irreversible decline.
She could do nothing but lie in bed, struggling even to swallow water. She could not taste her food, nor understand the words on the pages, nor hear clearly her sister's voice.

The girl took on various odd jobs, hoping to have enough time to stay by her sister's side and take care of her. To make ends meet, she had no choice but to take on the most gruelling work — the kind that others would avoid.
Her will was indeed unwavering, desperately clinging to the hard-won "miracle." Yet her frail body couldn't withstand the constant strain, and each day she came closer to collapse.

options.content: What happened next?

dialogues.content: Eventually, the younger sister chose to end her own life. With the last of her strength, she pushed the small phial of "miracle" — the one her elder sister had so desperately begged for — to the ground and shattered it.
Perhaps, in the end, she realised that this so-called "miracle" was but a pair of heavy shackles — for both herself and her elder sister.
It was I who guided her soul to the Misty Sea. Would you care to guess what she said to me?
From the look on your face, I imagine she said something gentle, like "Thank you"?
...You are quite perceptive. I may have been too subtle, and perhaps not as sincere as I should have been.

She expressed her gratitude to her elder sister, and to that woman as well. Though her life ended in suffering, it was through this very suffering that she found peace and the strength to accept her passing.
Upon hearing this, the girl wept, breaking into profuse apologies. Yet, in the end, she spoke but a single word of thanks — directed at the urn carrying her sister's ashes as it drifted away.

The girl later journeyed to Aethyrie, where she became a skilled physician and settled there. After starting her own family, she visited the woman, sharing with her that she had found happiness in her life.
It was then, in that moment, that the woman finally understood why her friend and daughter had refused to let her "save" them.

In the grand design of life, death is not always an unwelcome guest. At times, it arrives with quiet grace — like petals drifting from a flower as fruit begins to ripen, marking not just an end, but the birth of something new.
To resist death is to remain in stasis. It may actually cause them to miss out on the beauty life has to offer.

options.content: But I still don't want to see the people I care about pass away like that. Maybe if I try harder, I can find a real miracle to save them.
You're right. Perhaps accepting inevitable death is the better choice.

dialogues.content: You're a strong and compassionate child.
You're a brave child.
However, this story reflects only the perspective of that woman. Do not let it weigh heavily on your heart. You are free to carve your own path, should you choose.
I believe that, no matter the path you take, as long as you remain clear of mind and not led astray by falsehoods, you will find the right way in the end.

name: A Gleam Of Sunshine
desc: Though the winds of tomorrow will one day erase every trace we leave behind, the moments of glory we once shared will forever glow in the memories of those who remain.
memoryDesc: A scroll holding the unfulfilled dreams of a young man and woman. It is a legacy, timeless and pure, that they have entrusted to the generations that follow.

dialogues.content: Greetings, my child. You seem weary. Has something been troubling you?

options.content: So much has happened lately. I'm feeling exhausted.
I feel like I can't make a difference no matter what...

dialogues.content: Since leaving my homeland, I've been through so much and experienced many regrets. At times, I feel so powerless, as though all my efforts will be in vain.
Lady Nifle, as someone with centuries of wisdom, do you have any advice for me?
I see... Well, let me share another story with you.
This is a story about a young man and a young woman — one filled with hope, courage, and dreams of the future.
The story takes place a millennium ago, when Elysium was the only nation on the continent. One was a commoner, the other a noble.

The young man, born a commoner, developed a profound love for books from an early age, particularly history and mythology. Even as a youth, his vast knowledge became widely known, and many expected him to become a great scholar.

But the more he read, the more he learned, and the deeper he thought, the more he came to realise that this land was rife with injustices. What people had come to accept as normal was not always right.

The commoners toiled endlessly, barely scraping by, while the priests dined in excess. Beneath the loud chorus of hymns, the cries of the innocent could be heard — condemned as heretics and executed beneath the gallows.
—Of course, one of those cries belonged to a young girl, said to possess the "golden blood."
By day, she trembled as she slit her arm, offering her blood to those who came to worship her; by night, she curled in her cell, weeping in pain and praying for mercy from the gods.

One day, the young scholar ventured into the temple and delivered an impassioned speech to the gathered crowd, all of whom sought the so-called "golden blood." In response, however, all he received was the sharp point of the guards' spears.
He was thrown into a cold, damp cell, where, by a twist of fate, he encountered another key figure in the story — the noble young woman, who had arrived with her father for an inspection.

The young woman had a deep passion for riding and martial arts, and beneath her spirited nature was a kind and compassionate heart. When she came across the "misguided" young scholar — one of her own age — she couldn't help but feel sympathy for him. In secret, she visited his cell, hoping to persuade him to confess and earn a lighter sentence.
But the scholar insisted on his innocence. He even urged the young noblewoman to awaken from her own ignorance.

He revealed to her that the girl, said to possess the "golden blood" whom people revered, was in fact a poor soul held captive by a powerful nobleman — the noble young woman's very own father — who sought to profit from her.
At first, the young woman dismissed his words as absurd. Yet, the fervour in his bright eyes lingered in her thoughts, refusing to fade.

She saw sincerity in those eyes. And so, with a heart moved by his words, she took the first step toward uncovering the truth. Stealing the key from her father, she ventured into the deepest chamber of the temple, where she found the pale, emaciated girl — shackled and imprisoned.

After learning the truth, the noblewoman returned to the scholar's cell and stood before him once more. Seeing her grave and sympathetic expression, the scholar understood that she was now ready. And so, he shared with her the dark truths of the nobleman.

The young man's words struck like a blade, tearing through the delicate fabric of the young woman's privileged life, exposing the grotesque reality beneath. In that moment, she began to see the dark corners of her world that had once remained hidden.

She confided in her father, hoping he would release the young man. Instead, she found herself placed under house arrest, constantly watched. It was then that she realised — her father had always been complicit in their suffering.

options.content: That sounds... so hopeless...
It's almost impossible for one person to make a difference.

dialogues.content: Yes. There were times when they, too, despaired. Exhausted, much like you are now, they questioned the very meaning of their struggle. Yet, despite it all, they chose to persevere.
Even in prison, the young man continued to develop his theories, tirelessly sketching a vision of a new world rooted in justice and freedom.
Without the support of her family, the young woman rejected the temptations of wealth, dedicating herself to uplifting the downtrodden and seeking out those willing to contribute to the cause.
At first, their efforts were as subtle as the flutter of a butterfly's wings. Yet, over time, their actions stirred a storm, cracking the seemingly impenetrable structure of Elysium.
Together, they became the leaders of the legendary Great Migration, leading a resistance that freed the oppressed from the grasp of Elysium.
The Elysium resistance... the Great Migration...
I've read about it in books. But they never truly achieved their vision of equality, did they?
...Indeed, fate is a cruel force. It can stir a storm in the calmest of seas or extinguish flames with the power of a tidal wave. As you've said, often, our efforts yield nothing in the end.
However, those glorious moments were real, and they will be eternally etched in memory.

The Great Migration shed the light of courage and freedom across the Atlasia Continent, piercing through the veils of deceit woven by the gods. For the first time, people were allowed to confront their own desires and emotions.
Even after centuries, that spark of light endures in the weighty tomes of history, continuing to inspire those who strive toward the world envisioned by the young man and woman.
Mmm...
You asked for my advice earlier, but having lived in seclusion for so long, I find it difficult to offer concrete guidance.

What I can share with you is: the longer I have lived, the more I've come to realise that what's truly precious in life lies in those fleeting moments. The moments you've fought for what you cherish will remain timeless, regardless of the outcome.
{nickname}, do not fear, nor hesitate — within you lies extraordinary strength, and I have no doubt that you will leave an indelible mark upon the course of time.

options.content: Can I really do it...?
I will try my best.

dialogues.content: I have faith in you.
For now... let us set aside the weight of our thoughts and savour this rare moment of peace together, over a pot of tea.

name: The Scenery Along the Wrong Path
desc: We choose to walk the path that leads to the cliff's edge, for along the way, we will be greeted by beautiful wildflowers.
memoryDesc: Made from fresh game meat and vegetables, this stew once warmed a heart that had briefly ceased to beat on a cold, unforgiving winter night.

dialogues.content: Greetings, my child. You seem much improved since last time.

options.content: The credit all goes to the story you shared with me, Lady Nifle.
I've tried to live in the present moment, as you advised last time.

dialogues.content: I am pleased that my story was of some help to you. Now, is there anything on your mind today that you'd like to discuss?
I've been wondering... What are your thoughts on "mistakes," Lady Nifle?
I... I've been through so much, and lost even more. At times, I wonder if I've made the wrong choices. If I had taken a different path, would things have turned out differently?
But I can't go back in time, and so, I'll never know the answer.
Mmm... I can see your confusion. Well then, allow me to share a tale about "mistakes" this time. It is the story of a couple.
They lived on the outskirts of Elysium. He was a hunter, and she, a maid in the city. For years, they yearned for a child, yet fate remained unyielding to their prayers.
Then, one day, while hunting in the forest, the man stumbled upon a wandering child — battered, bloodied, and trembling in the cold. A pitiful sight indeed. Without hesitation, he brought her home.

His wife bathed the child and found no visible wounds upon her frail form. Yet, the child seemed to have been deeply traumatized. No matter what they asked, she simply stared at them, unblinking and silent.

Still, the couple took her in, tending to her with patience and care. In time, the girl, like a frost-laden bud beneath the warmth of spring, began to open herself to the world once more. And one day, at long last, she spoke.

She told them she had lost her birth parents. After some deliberation, the couple chose to adopt her as their own. They showered her with kindness, and in return, she blossomed into a sweet and well-mannered daughter. Thus, beneath their humble roof, a family found its quiet harmony.

options.content: That sounds like a story with a happy ending, doesn't it?

dialogues.content: On the surface, yes. But beneath it all, the girl carried with her a terrible secret.
She was born into a family of heretics, followers of the ancient Charon myths. As a result, her parents were executed, and yet she survived — saved by a mysterious healing gift that she possessed.
With hands horribly mutilated, she dug herself free from their graves and fled into the wilderness, seeking refuge in the forests.

In Elysium, nothing was deemed more sinful than heresy. Had her secret been revealed, even if her adoptive parents did not have the heart to hand her over to the executioners, they would have undoubtedly abandoned her.

Having at last found a place she could call "home," the girl could not bear the thought of losing it. Thus, she chose to conceal her true identity, clinging to the fragile hope that the truth would remain undiscovered.

Time passed, and under the care of her adoptive parents, the girl grew. Her secret remained well-guarded, and as the years went by, she even forgot it herself. She began to believe that, with her new family, she could live a happy, peaceful life forever.

When her adoptive mother suggested they travel to the city, to work and experience the world beyond, the girl did not hesitate. After all, they would merely be lowly maids in the houses of the nobility, unnoticed and insignificant.

One day, while cleaning, her adoptive mother accidentally broke a valuable artefact. According to her employer's house rules, such a mistake would result in a flogging. Unable to bear the thought of her mother enduring such a punishment, the girl decided to take the blame herself.
As the flogging began, the whip tore into her skin, leaving a gaping wound. Yet, within moments, the wound healed, as though no harm had been done.

This "miracle" soon reached the ears of the house's master — Lord "Generous." He rushed to the scene, and with a swift motion, plunged a knife into the girl's chest. She fought through the agony for minutes, only to rise again, alive.
Lord "Generous" took her away. Upon investigation, he discovered that she was the daughter of the two heretics from years past.

At first, he was enraged. But then, a "brilliant" idea crossed his mind: if he could exploit her power, which had never been seen in Elysium, masking it as a "divine miracle," it would not only be profitable but would also thrust him into the spotlight.
To achieve this, however, he needed to conceal her true identity. So, he imprisoned her, created a new identity for her, and secretly had her adoptive mother executed.

options.content: How could this happen...?

dialogues.content: The girl was filled with deep regret. Had she not hidden her true identity in her desperate search for the warmth of a family, her kind, innocent adoptive parents would never have suffered such a fate.

Though the girl was rescued by the resistance during the Great Migration, she never sought out her adoptive father again. Their encounter had been a mistake from the beginning, and she did not want to bring any further misfortune upon him.

For decades, she could not rid herself of the burden of the past, constantly worrying about her adoptive father's well-being. In time, as my journey took me through Elysium, I visited him on her behalf.
By then, her adoptive father had grown old, his hair streaked with silver. He had spent much of his life in hiding, and when I showed up, he was astonished that anyone still remembered his name.
Honouring the girl's wishes, I did not reveal the true purpose of my visit. Instead, I simply sat with him as a Ferrywoman, reminiscing about days long past.

He remembered everything vividly — the night he lost both his wife and daughter, the moment his life unravelled, casting him into a fugitive's existence, wandering from place to place in perpetual flight.
And yet, to my surprise, he told me he had no regrets in choosing to take the girl in.
He then handed me a small box — a keepsake containing his wife's ashes. He told me he had long been waiting for a Ferrywoman, so that her soul might finally find peace.
With quiet astonishment, I performed the long-overdue farewell ritual for his wife. To my surprise, even after all these years, I could still hear the whisper of her soul...
She spoke the same words as her husband: "Thank you for becoming our daughter."

He then told me that, from the very beginning, they had known the girl's true identity. On the night her parents were executed, they watched as the executioners, torches in hand, marched into the forest.
And the next morning, when they saw the wandering girl, they recognized her at once. Fully aware of the consequences, they made their choice to take her in.
For them, meeting the girl, protecting her, and raising her brought great joy. Though it was a joy shadowed by danger, they embraced it without hesitation.

The old man confided that his only regret was lacking the courage to leave sooner. Had he taken his wife and daughter away from Elysium earlier, perhaps they might still have been living a peaceful life together today.
And so, in the years that followed, the once wronged hunter became a true "heretic." For decades, he quietly aided Elysium's oppressed, guiding them across the border to freedom.

options.content: Did you tell him his adopted daughter was still alive?

dialogues.content: ...I did not say it outright. Yet, from the quiet relief in his eyes, I believe he had already understood.
Though they may never meet again, knowing that their loved ones are safe is, perhaps, comfort enough.
This story's ending doesn't seem so tragic after all.
Indeed. Hearing his words, I found myself reflecting...
As long as we live, mistakes are inevitable. Some stem from a narrow vision, others from misplaced hope, and at times, even willful ignorance.
However, a misguided choice does not always yield a misguided outcome. The taste of its sweetness or bitterness is known only to those who have lived through it.
What truly matters, more than the mistake itself, is the future that lies before us.
It grants us the opportunity to make amends, to bring about change, and to transform what we've endured into something more meaningful.
Perhaps that is why, when the old man spoke to me of his past, there was neither regret nor sorrow in his eyes — only the quiet contentment of one who has made peace with his journey.

options.content: I think I understand now...

dialogues.content: Thank you for sharing this story with me. I've learned so much today, just like before.
Hehe, it is I who should thank you.
Perhaps it's my age, but I do tend to be long-winded. I appreciate your patience — for keeping this old lady company and listening to my endless ramblings about the past.

name: Her Story
desc: Countless tales intertwine, weaving the endless journey that is her life.
memoryDesc: In this dream, there is neither the cruelties of life nor the sorrows of death. Regrets remain unwritten, mistakes yet to unfold — she is simply there, cradled by the warmth of sunlight and the soft murmur of the stream.

dialogues.content: Ah, you've arrived, my child. Tell me, what is it you wish to speak of today?

options.content: You've shared many stories of others, yet you have never spoken of your own.

dialogues.content: Lady Nifle, today... I'd like to hear your story.
My story, hmm... You are an insightful child. I suspect you have already caught glimpses of it, have you not?

options.content: Yes, I believe I have.
Huh? What do you mean?

dialogues.content: The stories you've told me... they are all your own experiences, aren't they?
The truth is, my story is interwoven with the very tales I have shared with you.
Indeed.
They are not merely events that happened; they are, in truth, fragments of my own past.

I am the woman who bore a gift yet failed to ease people's suffering. I am the helpless girl once imprisoned in the temple's cold embrace. I am the child whose very existence became the harbinger of misfortune for those who took her in.
Right... but still, I wish to hear it from you directly — not as an observer, but as you, Nifle, the protagonist of your own story.
Ah... I see. Very well. Since you wish to hear it, I shall, albeit uncharacteristically, recount my past.
I was born in Elysium, into a family devoted to the ancient Charon myths.

When I was ten, my parents were executed for heresy. I was meant to perish alongside them. Yet, in that moment, I unexpectedly awakened as a Daimon, gaining the power of immortality. And so, I survived.
Orphaned and adrift, I wandered the forests until a passing hunter found me. He took me in, offering the quiet warmth of a home I had lost.
At eighteen, my true nature was inadvertently exposed. Word soon reached Lord "Generous," who bestowed upon me the title of "the Blessed One" — a crown woven of thorns.
For years, my world was confined within the walls of a small temple, while Lord "Generous" reaped immense wealth from selling my blood.

It was not until two brave souls — the young scholar and noblewoman from my second tale — rescued me from that lasting nightmare. They were my saviours, my dearest friends, and the ones who first cast light upon my path ahead.

Later, Erika fell in battle during our journey north. As for Lexis, though he escaped, he never found the answers he sought for his ideal world. In the end, he faded away amidst stacks of unfinished manuscripts, his vision left incomplete.
During my years in Aethyrie, I adopted a child. It was my first experience as a caretaker, witnessing a life unfold before my eyes.

I watched her grow — from a tiny infant wrapped in swaddling clothes to a radiant young woman, and later into a figure of calm wisdom. I remember her first cries, her first words, the first time she recited the ancient verses...
I recall her endless debates with Lexis, and the solemn moment when she accepted the key to his library as he lay upon his deathbed.
Each change in her filled me with joy and pride. Yet, I remained painfully aware that, like Erika and Lexis, she too was bound by the limits of mortality. She could not stay by my side forever.

In the end, they all left me. Once, I mourned their passing. But after meeting the two sisters who sought my blood, and bearing witness to countless partings between life and death, I came to accept the impermanence of this world.

I have let go of both joy and sorrow, renounced desire, and no longer grieve or rage at the suffering woven into the fabric of existence. For the past nine centuries, I have wandered across Atlasia, guiding the souls of the departed.

Now, I remain in Hyperborea for a time, drawn here by a child whose face is strangely familiar. Yet, I do not seek to meddle in conflicts or alter the course of fate. I wish only to bear witness to her story.
Soon enough, I will resume my journey. Nothing in this world will ever truly bring my wandering to a halt — unless, at last, death itself chooses to embrace me.
—And that is my story. Tell me, my child, does it sate your curiosity?

options.content: No, this isn't the full story.

dialogues.content: I would still like to know... before you assumed all these roles, before you gained immortality — what was Nifle like, back then?

You are the first to ask of my childhood. Many have been curious about my past, but none have sought to know the life I led before fate wove me into grander tales. Compared to what followed, it was quite unremarkable.
Let me think...

My first home — the one of my birth — lay deep within the northern forests of Elysium. There were no churches, no nobility — only the soft rustle of hares darting through the underbrush, and the fragrance of wild berries.
My earliest memories are of dappled sunlight filtering through the leaves, and the gentle murmur of a stream winding its way through the quiet woods.
In those days, I was no different from any other child. I would beg my father to take me into the forest to play, and I would ignore my mother's gentle warnings, splashing carelessly in the stream.
My mother, too, was a Ferrywoman. Strangers would pass through the forest, entrusting her with small caskets. Under the moonlight, she would dance, letting them drift down the river's current.
Once, I asked her what lay within those caskets. She told me they carried what people cherished and missed dearly.
So I asked, "Why would people cast away what they held dear?" She said, "Because to move forward, one must learn to let go."
I did not understand. Sensing my confusion, my father only smiled, ruffled my hair, and said, "One day, when you are older, you will understand."
But they never lived to see that day. The moment they were executed, the carefree days of the young Nifle came to an end.

options.content: Do you miss those days?

dialogues.content: At times, memories of that distant past resurface. But unlike most, I do not cling to them with longing or nostalgia. I simply let them drift through my thoughts, like fallen leaves carried by the wind.
To me, the past — like all that has come and gone — is simply another thread woven into the fabric of my existence, neither weighted with sorrow nor imbued with special meaning.
And yet, as I recount these tales to you, I sense the faintest of ripples stirring within me...
...I find myself weary. If you do not mind, I shall rest here for a moment.
(As Lady Nifle speaks, she closes her eyes, her head gently coming to rest against your shoulder.)
(Her breathing slows, steady and serene, and a faint smile graces her lips. It seems she has drifted into a peaceful dream.)
(A dream laced with the sweet scent of wild berries, bathed in the golden warmth of sunlight, where perhaps, a hare flits playfully through the underbrush in the distance...)

name: Deepwood Duo — Blades at Play
desc:
In the heart of the deepwood, every soul seeks to leave a tale behind — most are woven with vengeance and love.
Yet, the truly awakened leave no shadow in their passing.
memoryDesc: A sword can kill — yet it may also serve a different purpose.

dialogues.content: A hero wanders with blades keen, hearts unbound, and rights the world's wrongs.
The righteous roam free, untethered and unfettered. To keep a curfew is to be a guard, not a hero. For true grace lies not in the blade, but in the freedom it brings.
So you're leaving.
So I am.
You're really going, after all.
So indeed.
You weren't supposed to go.
And yet I must.
Why do you have to go?
To spare a life.
Whose life?
Yours!
Whoa, so cool! This time let's swap — I'll say: "Yours!"
So lame. I only agreed to do this once.
Hey you two... what are you doing?
You don't get it? We're acting out a scene from Drifter!
This is the most famous dialogue from the most popular Drifter novel. Every time I read this part, I wish I could jump into the book.
If Mom didn't drag me by the ear to study every day, I'd have gone to Outer Peaks already — learned real skills, fought for justice!
If you finished your homework early like I do, Mom wouldn't bother you.
She's biased. She lets you use her sword to chop wood and clean fish. But when I try to spin it just once, she says that I'm wasting my spirit on trifles.
Of course. I'm doing real work — helping Mom. You'd hurt yourself just swinging that thing around.
I'm telling you, if Mom had ever read Drifter, she wouldn't let you use this sword for chores.
She should've given it to me. Let me practice from the manual. Then once I'm grown, I can protect you and Mom.
You've read too many novels. With the Nine Chapters of Dafeng now, no one needs a Drifter anymore.
She's right. These days... there aren't many drifters left.
Ah, sorry, mister! I was too busy talking with my brother and forgot you were still here.
Did you... come for Mom? She said she isn't receiving guests.
Well, I can see that. She used to never let this blade leave her side. Now that you two have it... I understand what she means.
You know Mom? Can you tell us about her young age? I've always thought she must've been a great hero — why else would she have a sword like this?
Whenever I ask, she just stays quiet.
I was asked to come to her. But since she doesn't wish to meet... it's not my place to say more.
Aww, boring. With that outfit and that sword on your back, I thought we might get to see her draw it again.
Haha, in time, perhaps you will. Well then... I take my leave.
Seriously?! Hey, sis — you hear that? Stop using Mom's sword on chickens! She might need it again someday. What if it rusts?
Don't be so dramatic. We'll worry about that later.
How about you, mister? Won't you sit and rest a while before you go?
Can't do that. There's always a pack of little hounds on my tail — can't stay in one place too long. I won't trouble you further.

name: A Drifter's Regret — Beyond Mountains and Rivers
desc: Behind every peak lies a hope — and behind every hope, a fading light. Yet looking back, the finest view remains the one he left behind.
memoryDesc: Between dream and memory, echoes of a wandering free; Amidst joy and sorrow, a wistful smile for a world gone by.

dialogues.content: Heroes live by love and vengeance, storms of passion and conflict. And where there is drama, there are those who eagerly write it all down. Their tales are devoured by all.
Everyone dreams of galloping through the world of dust — yet those who truly ride it know only the weight of the wind and the loneliness of the road.
You're back, Mingluan.
I'm back, Kezhou.
And the results?
There were some, naturally.
I set foot in five kingdoms... comprehended five new types of kung fu.
First, I went west out of Huaxu, into the great desert of Khemet.
I'd heard it was a burning sea of sand, endless and scorching. So I decided to travel by night, under the stars.
But I hadn't expected the desert cold to bite so deep. Had I done nothing, I would've frozen — just another nameless skeleton under the dunes.
Just as I wondered how to survive… I saw flickers of green on the horizon. Small at first, then growing.
Those green lights came in pairs, cold and fierce — like the Greedywolf Star in the old texts. Then I realized… they weren't stars. They were eyes.
How pitiful.
Who's pitiful?
Certainly not you.
Then you misjudge me. Those pups are fine. I just knocked a few out, dragged them into the lee of a dune, and used them as blankets. Their warmth got me through the night.
Killing them would've been easy. But had I done that… I wouldn't have lasted the first night.
Wolves are nothing to you, I know. But your palm strikes have always been fierce — they call you "Dragon-Subduer". I'm surprised you held back enough to spare them.
That must be the first kung fu you comprehended.

As sharp as ever, Kezhou. You see right to the heart of it. Every night after, I did the same, knocked out wolves for warmth. And from that I grasped a new palm technique. I call it the Wolf-Slumber Palm.
Impressive, the Wolf-Slumber Palm. That calls for a drink.
The second one must've been in the Hyperborean Empire. Let me guess... something swift, like a rapier? Or a heavy fist, solid as the city of Icelake?
I'm surprised you've heard of Icelake, stuck here in Huaxu as you are.
Made a friend lately who lives there. Picked up a thing or two.
I see, but wrong guess. I was in a hurry. Went straight to Luca.
On the way, I met a legendary creature of the sea. A beast they call a Siren. Beautiful as the moon... but its song steals your mind.
So it's like Master Mo Baoqin, a century ago? Using secret tone arts to shatter one's focus?
Just like that. But in the moment, I didn't think — just dove deep, held my breath, and grabbed onto a passing whale. Barely escaped with my life.
But because of that, my breath control improved. I hardly fear poison or petty tricks like that anymore. I call this method the Whaleheart Art.
And then?
And I didn't stay long either. Then I went to Yashnia, home of the Elysian Church... there I—
Wait. Let me interrupt.
Of course, but you owe me a drink.
Fine. But just tell me... what about her? Did you find her in the end?
You said you wouldn't return without finding her.
I'm tired.
She's on my mind all the time. In the sand, the waves, the forests, by the Sacred Tower, on Whisper River. I searched... but never found a trace.
So I wondered, maybe she returned to Huaxu, to all the pain here. But, still, no one's ever seen her.
How pitiful.
Who is?
All who love in vain.
Heh...
If we're talking pitiful... you're no different. I wander free, beyond the reach of the Nine Chapters. But you probably just crossed blades with Magistrates before coming to see me.
Obviously. But I'm used to it by now. Just as you're used to life abroad.
You interrupted me. Drink your penalty. Once you finish, I set out again to look for her. This time I'll try the reverse. Start by sea to Aethyrie.
I already drank it.
When? I didn't see.
Just when you spoke of the Sacred Tower and Whisper River.
Really? I didn't even notice. Maybe I just want to see her too much.
Not really, I haven't drunk yet.
You little... you've loved tricking people since we were boys. Some things never change.
And you still fall for it every time.
Hahaha...
Well then, I'm off. Till we meet again.
Till we meet again.
And so the second one departs... now for the third.

name: Of Jade Flutes and Nightspent Wine
desc: Scents stir the soul's deep-seated memories; perhaps this is why every heart treasures a different fare, for no two journeys share the same road.
memoryDesc: Its pages are tinged with age, yet with a collection boasting dishes of rare craftsmanship, seldom encountered in this mundane world.

dialogues.content: Ah! Hot, but so savory
Whew—
The outside is fried crisp — it crackles when you bite, but the inside is tender, smooth, yet firm enough to hold together. That takes serious skill and control.
You've got taste. Uncle Maojin's tofu puffs are famous all around. I'd say they're no worse than that "Untamable Loong" nonsense.
Wait, could it be…
Talkative little rascal. Stop pestering the customer. Another batch of tofu puffs is ready — serve them.
Right away!
You taste it?
Yes. Your skill lives up to its reputation. No wonder my master could never forget it.
Enough with the flattery. You eating for yourself or for your master? Speak your own mind.
It's delicious!
There, see? So if it's good, what should you do?
Seven more!
Now you're talking.
Well, now that you're fed — who's your master?
Yan Shanting.
Oh, him. Here for the Art of the Sword, then? Didn't think he'd remember.
He never forgot. Will you be participating, Master Liu?
"Master Liu" isn't here anymore. I put down the blade long ago. Here is only Uncle Maojin.
Enough questions. You want seven more tofu puffs? I'll make them.
Make it seven to go. I'll let my friends try them.
Fine. But remember, tell them Uncle Maojin made it. One extra word, I'll cut out your tongue and braise it.
Understood. Then I take my leave, master.
A true hero is, above all, a connoisseur of fine living. A noble steed, a peerless blade, and elegant robes are the rightful marks of the righteous.

But none are pursued with more fastidious care than food and drink. So much so that the very image of a hero is steeped in vintage wine and generously roasted meats. Should a swordsman refuse wine, one feels the edge of his blade is blunted — lacking that seasoned cunning.
One catty of yellow wine, seven fried tofu puffs, and extra chili paste!
Right away, sir! I'll put the order in.
One catty of yellow wine, seven fried tofu puffs, and extra chili paste!
Thanks. By the way, have you heard of a Drifter named Liu Weifu, the Iron Palm? He'd be in his sixties or seventies by now.
Can't say I have. Never met a Drifter in my life.
Well, you're looking at one right now.
You're a Drifter?
Obviously. What, I don't look the part?
Not really. I heard Drifters drink wine by the bowl and eat meat by the chunk. Never seen one order tofu puffs.
What kind of nonsense is that? We're not wild dogs tearing into raw meat. When we eat with purpose, we have our own refinements.
Well, dogs eat more than just meat, actually…
That's enough. Are my tofu puffs ready? Hurry them up, will you?
You got it! Uncle Maojin, hurry with those tofu puffs!
No rush. Almost done.
Right. Sir, it'll just be a moment. But since you mentioned that Drifters "eat with purpose," could you tell me more? The place is empty — I'd love to hear.
Fine. The master I'm looking for today was also famous in his day for his cooking. They called him the "Gourmet Knight."
His most legendary dish was called "The Untamable Loong Beyond Reach." Rumor was, he slew the Argent Loong that guarded the Nine Chapters and served it at a feast.
In truth, he used his palm strength to tenderize meats from all kinds of birds and beasts, ground them fine, and reshaped them. One bite released manifold flavors — so he called it "Loong Meat."
Then he'd stir-fry incredibly silken tofu with marrow from various animals, letting their richness soak in. He called that "Loong Marrow."
You're having a laugh, sir. It's just tofu. How could anyone call it Loong Marrow? By that logic, our fried tofu puffs could be called "Fried Loong Marrow."
Ah, I only know what my master told me. They say the Iron Palm retired long ago. No one knows where he is now.
All this talk is making my mouth water, and you've never even tasted it? Enough fantasy — try these. Our signature fried tofu puffs.
Let me taste it.

name: Of Youth's Vigor Frosted by Time's Snow
desc: Youth in pursuit of the sword ever climbs toward the peak. On and on, until companions grow few. At the summit, none remain, only endless snow upon bowed heads.
memoryDesc: A chapbook of half-truths, once all the rage. Who now can parse the strife sealed in these characters? The book holds its silence.

dialogues.content: Following Kezhou deep into a remote stretch of mountains — the site of the contest, it seemed.
Before lay slopes lush with new growth, cascading springs — a fine arena for a contest, yet... it felt too still, too quiet.
Why is it just us? I thought you said every Drifter with a name would be here.
A shame to say it, but there aren't many left worth the title these days. We Drifters grow fewer with each passing year
Even last time, only four showed up.
The first was my master, Yan Shanting. Though he's passed, his last wish was for me to stand in his place here.
So then, I sought out the other three masters who fought.
First, a swordswoman of great skill — the one who won last time, unmatched among Huaxu. But I didn't even see her.

My master told me she loved the sword too deeply — often she wouldn't even draw it, fighting with the sheath instead. However, she left the world of blood and dust, hid herself away, so the Nine Chapters never caught her.
Now, interesting enough, she lets her children play with her prized blade. She wants no part of the clash of blades — only peace behind closed doors, so I didn't disturb her.
My master called her the wisest of them. I never understood. Well, now I know his reasons even without seeing her this time.
I think... I would've done the same.
The next was Mingluan, a little older than me. A prodigy since childhood — he became famous young, fighting in this contest before he'd even come of age.
He had a beloved once, a master of the sword herself. They roamed together, righting wrongs. Everyone thought they were destined.
But even a righteous life wears on you. She grew tired — always drifting, always hiding from Magistrates.
So, they promised to leave Huaxu together, find a quiet life elsewhere.
But the day they set was the same day as the contest. Chained by his pride, Mingluan insisted on fighting one last time to win the title, then leave with her.
But the fights between masters isn't decided quickly. They fought for three days and nights. When he finally went to meet her, only empty mountains looked back over the river.
She must have seen that he couldn't let go of his fame, and left alone.
At first he didn't mind. But soon, longing became sickness. He realized something mattered more than being "First in the Realm".
So he too left Huaxu, searching for her even now. Still hasn't found her.
So of course, he won't be coming.
The last was called the Gourmet Knight — a master of the kitchen. His "Untamable Loong Beyond Reach" was a legend.
But once, at a feast he prepared, someone poisoned the dishes. Blue-and-white porcelain that should've held delicacies... was stained with blood.
Though it wasn't his doing, the food had passed through his hands. The Nine Chapters declared him guilty.
He could've fought the Magistrates — but resisting would've been like admitting guilt. So he surrendered. They broke his leg, and his spirit.
When he was free again, he'd lost all heart. He left the Drifter life behind, and now he just cooks. Makes the best fried tofu you'll ever taste.
Wait, the tofu you brought me the other day, was it...?
No, absolutely not. I didn't answer questions and you didn't ask.
Oh... I see.
So then... that means only you are here for your master?
Yes. It's just me this time, representing my master.
This is what's become of the Drifters. Once, we gathered freely — no code to follow but our hearts and our blades.
Our stories were written in flashes of steel.
But under the Nine Chapters, no one draws a blade for justice anymore. Everyone fears breaking rules, drawing the eyes of the Magistrates.
Even those who call themselves free can't escape the Nine Chapters' grasp.
Is that the reason you want to overthrow it?
It's one reason. There are others — old grudges, new wounds.
Sometimes I wonder, if it keeps peace for most, is fighting it really right?
