But meeting those masters, seeing how they've ended up… I wonder how many unseen injustices lie beneath this "peace".
As a Drifter, I can't stand aside. Yes, our numbers thin — but just as it is said, new storms rise from our generation.
A sword in hand, a heart in the world. Even a lone Drifter can lead the way, see further than others. That's not a bad fate.
Walk the path you must; finish what others could not. I think I understand now why Drifters never truly fade away.
And I believe, next time, you won't be the only one here.
Haha! Well said!
But don't think I'm sad about no one showing up. In fact — it's perfect!
I now declare: due to the absence of the other three participants, I, Kezhou, disciple of Yan Shanting, is hereby number one among Huaxu's Drifters!
Just like that?
Why not? My master told me to. He said if the others didn't want to fight, don't force them.
After all, fewer fighters means a better chance to win. Maybe only one match to victory!
Though my master was too conservative. I didn't even have to fight one! Now that's what I call unrivaled!
I thought you'd be more upset.
Moping and sighing? Not for me. Let others play the mournful hero.
What I'll do, is cut down the Nine Chapters — the thing that weighed on my master, my seniors, the Drifters... all of them!
When it's done, maybe I'll retreat to the mountains like in those old tales.
With your personality? I doubt you'll stay retired.
True. I'll figure it out then.
Today, I've won. I should live joyfully — leave tomorrow for tomorrow. Come, friend! Let's s drink! And sing! And sing 'til we drink again!
All that once was — the gleaming blades, vows sworn in life and death, righteous passions — had long faded to dust on the wind.
All that remained was hair iced by time, and a soft sigh: so youth is lost to the world's wear.
It's early in the morning, where are we even going?
The Grand Blade-Meet. Happens once every twenty years.
Now I'm awake. Who's fighting?
Any Drifter in Huaxu with a reputation ought to come. They've held this seven or eight times already — up on the mountain peak, they spar until only one stands victorious.
How many will show up this time?
You'll see when we get there.

name: The Wish for Magic
desc: She whispered her magical wishes to her friends.
memoryDesc: A pile of spent casings, which, with a touch of imagination, transform into pistols, cannons, airships, and mighty robots — keys to unlocking a world of dreams.

dialogues.content: Hello, {性别:Mr|Miss} Unicorn. I've just got this amazing gift from the Great Magician. Would you like to see it?

options.content: What is it?

dialogues.content: It's a box of building blocks.
Look at these blocks — they might look similar at first glance, but if you look closely, you'll see that each one has a unique shape, colour, and pattern!
I've counted — there are over a dozen different types here!

options.content: Aren't these actually spent casings?

dialogues.content: Spent casings... Is that what they're called? Wow, you know so much! Thanks for telling me. Now, let me show you how to stack them up — it's really fun!
Watch this! If you put them together like this, it becomes a tiny pistol.
And like this, it turns into a big cannon — BOOM!
Now, look — it's an airship!

options.content: It's Outsider who taught you all these, isn't it?

dialogues.content: Yes! He showed me lots of cool ways to put them together, like making a giant robot that can shoot missiles from its shoulders and has wings on its back—
Oh! And the fists — they can launch too! I'll show you!

name: The Wish for Stars
desc: She sent her long-lost dreams skyward upon the stars.
memoryDesc: Fairy tales don't always end in happiness. After the bird turned into a burning star, does she still weep in the night sky?

dialogues.content: My second wish is for {性别:Mr|Miss} Unicorn to secretly take me out of the city to see the real stars.
The sky is so vast and distant, and the stars are so bright... it's all so beautiful...
In the city, even on clear nights, you can only see a small patch of the sky because of the buildings and city walls.
The star lamp Outsider gave me is pretty, but there's nothing like the real starry sky... achoo!

options.content: Be careful not to catch a cold.
Stand behind me, I'll shield you from the wind.

dialogues.content: I'm okay, really. You can feel my palm. It's quite warm! I'd like to stay out a little longer...
Look! Those stars over there, they look like a bunny together, don't they?

options.content: Yes, they do.
They look more like a big drumstick.
They look more like a dolphin wearing pants on its head.

dialogues.content: Hehe. Then I'll make up a story about a little bunny's marvelous adventures among the stars tonight.

options.content: Why do you like seeing the stars so much, Fina?

dialogues.content: Huh? ...I don't see it. Are you hungry?
Huh? Wh—What's that?! I can't picture it...
A long time ago, my mom told me a story about a little bird that turned into a star... It's my favourite, and I'd love to share it with you.
Just kidding. Anyway, I'm curious—

options.content: Why do you like seeing the stars so much, Fina?

dialogues.content: Just kidding. Anyway, I'm curious—

options.content: Why do you like seeing the stars so much, Fina?

dialogues.content: This bird wasn't like the others: she had ugly feathers, a jarring song, and her claws and beak were not sharp. The other birds didn't like her, always bullying her, trying to chase her away.
Yet, this little bird yearned for the starry sky. She prayed to the stars, wishing for a chance to join them, even if it meant perishing in their fiery glow.

options.content: So the stars answered her prayers?

dialogues.content: No... Some stars ignored her, while some mocked her for overreaching: a plain little bird dreaming of soaring through the beautiful starry sky, how ridiculous.

options.content: What happened then?

dialogues.content: She decided not to pin her hopes on others. Bidding farewell to her family, she flew toward the night sky alone.
The higher she flew, the colder the sky became; eventually, she froze, never to flap her wings again.

options.content: ...That's quite a sad ending.

dialogues.content: No, that's not the end. As the little bird lay frozen, she suddenly realised something: her plain body began to quietly burst into radiant flames, just like a shining <H>star</> in the sky.
That's right — she became a star herself!
And that's my story. Do you like it, {性别:Mr|Miss} Unicorn?

options.content: I love it. It's a beautiful story.
I didn't like it. It's too sad.

dialogues.content: I love it. That little bird was much braver than I expected.
The little bird shouldn't have had to sacrifice herself... It was an evasion of real injustice. She should've fought back.
I see... well, that would indeed be a completely different story.
Do you think I can be like that little bird someday?

options.content: ...The little bird's family would be devastated.

dialogues.content: Ah... I hadn't thought of that.
I always imagined her family would be proud and happy for her because she would always shine so brightly in the night sky.
If they missed her, they could simply look up at the starry sky on cloudless nights and say hello, just as we have done.
But you've made me realise that as a star, she could no longer speak or move. Her family would never be able to reach her, no matter how far they trekked.
Would that make her family sad? I need to think about it...
Thank you for taking me out to see the stars tonight, {性别:Mr|Miss} Unicorn. Let's go home.

name: The Wish for a Bird's-Eye View
desc: She buried her memories in distant lands.
memoryDesc: Though the cold rains of the past have yet to cease, she still feels warmth from another's palm.

dialogues.content: My third wish is for {性别:Mr|Miss} Unicorn to take me up on the town walls of Icelake.
Huff... huff... huff... huff...

options.content: Take it easy, Fina.

dialogues.content: I'm fine, look! We're now at the highest point of the outer city! It feels like we're birds soaring in the sky!
Hello, Sun! Hello, Clouds! It's so nice to see you! I'm Fina, and this is {性别:Mr|Miss} Unicorn, my dear friend!
Hehe...

options.content: Keep it down, Fina — you wouldn't want Outsider to find out about this, would you?
Hello, Sun!

dialogues.content: Ah... sorry!
Haha, you're full of energy today, {性别:Mr|Miss} Unicorn!
I've never seen Icelake from such a high point before! Oh, do you know Icelake well by now? Let me show you around—
See that brass-coloured, round thing with a spiky tip? That's the Silverpeace Monument! It's been there for hundreds of years.
And do you see those cramped rows of houses down south? One of them is my home! The neighbours are loud but friendly.
And to the west...

options.content: What's wrong? If you don't know that place, I can tell you about it.

dialogues.content: ...I know that place.
That's the inner city... where I grew up. That house over there... that's where I used to live.

options.content: Oh, so you came from a rich family. That's nice.
Do you miss it there?

dialogues.content: No, it wasn't nice at all.
No, not at all.
Because that place was just a house rather than a home.
My parents were taken to a faraway place. It all happened on a stormy night in August.
Dad was taken by a "bad hunter," and his body was left hanging in the sky with a noose around his neck.
Mom was killed by a savage "beast," and her blood, red as roses, was washed away by the pouring rain, leaving nothing behind.
They've gone to a faraway place... and there's no home for me there anymore.

options.content: (Pat her head gently)
(Give her a hug)

dialogues.content: Your hands are as warm as you, {性别:Mr|Miss} Unicorn...

options.content: Remember the story you told me? The one about the little bird and the stars?

dialogues.content: Maybe your parents have become stars in the sky... Though they can't speak, they're still quietly, gently watching over you.
So, whenever you miss them, just smile at the night sky.
Thank you... I'll do that.
It's okay, don't feel bad for me, because I have a new home now.
I have the Great Magician, and I have you. I am more than content now.

name: The Unfinished Wish
desc: She entrusts her hopes for tomorrow to the blank pages.
memoryDesc: How far must she journey before she pens a beautiful ending to this tale?

dialogues.content: There you are, {性别:Mr|Miss} Unicorn!

options.content: Only one wish to go. Where do you want to go this time, Fina?

dialogues.content: This time, we're not going anywhere because my last wish is already here with us.
Look, I've brought my new storybook!
Oh, it's a collection of stories by Fina... wait, why are all the pages blank?
Because I want to write a new storybook with you — that's my fourth wish.

options.content: Oh, that's a rather simple wish... Absolutely, we can do that.
But I'm not good at writing stories.

dialogues.content: Let's start the first story with a simple adventure~
That's okay, I'll teach you!
One day, Little Nightingale and {性别:Mr|Miss} Unicorn embarked on an adventure together...
No pressure, we'll figure it out together.
Was it just the two of them, or were there other friends?

options.content: Just the two of them.
Plus the Great Magician.
Plus Miss Butterfly.

dialogues.content: Then it'd be their very own secret adventure.
Right, with the Great Magician along, it'd surely be a wonderful trip.
Hehe, Miss Butterfly and Little Nightingale could fly in the sky together then.
Alright, so they set off together. They arrived at...

options.content: A frozen land covered in ice.
A cluster of small islands at sea.
A faraway realm in the east.

dialogues.content: Hmm, sounds a lot like Icelake.
Right, so they set sail in a magical boat, carried away by playful waves.
Hmm... Perhaps then, they'd meet the elegant Lady Dragon there?
After that, they...

options.content: Discovered a mysterious treasure chest.
Made new friends in a foreign land.
Revelled in the spectacular scenery.

dialogues.content: A chest...? What could be in it? Silver coins, pretty flowers, or finely made building blocks?
That means more companions for the journey — the more, the merrier!
Right, going on an adventure is about seeing all those wonderful places in the world.
In the end, they...

options.content: Returned home with a wealth of treasures.
Settled down in another prosperous land and lived happily ever after.
Defeated the evil Demon Lord and became celebrated folk heroes.

dialogues.content: Right! So this is how the story...
Hmm...

options.content: What's wrong?

dialogues.content: I just feel like... there's something missing from our story...
It's such a perfect story, with a happy ending for everyone... What could possibly be missing?
I think I know.

options.content: The problem with this story is just being "perfect."
What's missing from the story is "regrets."

dialogues.content: Everything in this story goes perfectly, doesn't it? Without any real challenges or regrets, it all feels almost unreal.
Right... When I was little, the stories my mother told weren't just about happiness and laughter. There would also be bad things and tears:
Beautiful princesses fell into deep slumbers, enchanted princes turned into beasts, children were taken by evil sorcerers, and little birds froze in the night sky...
Even though the endings were normally good... why must they experience sadness first? Why couldn't they be happy all the time?

options.content: Because that's just how life is.

dialogues.content: Well, take your favourite marshmallows for example: They come in different flavours — some are sweet, some are sour, and some are even a bit bitter.
Right! I love those sweet ones, and hate the bitter ones... no, the mustard flavour is the worst. Why would anyone put mustard in marshmallows!?

Every time I had one of those by mistake, it'd bring tears to my eyes, and I had to find a sweet one to get rid of the mustard taste in my mouth. What's funny is that the sweet taste would seem stronger—
Ah, I get it now... It's precisely because of the bitter and mustard-flavored ones that the sweet ones taste so good.
And it's the same with the stories, right? If there's no sadness or regrets, then happiness wouldn't feel as precious...
So that's how it is... I see.
The story we just wrote stands for our fondest wish. But a real story, like our lives, has both laughter and tears...
Thank you, {性别:Mr|Miss} Unicorn. I think I'll need more time...
To grow, to live, to learn, and to travel — before I can finish this storybook.
So, {性别:Mr|Miss} Unicorn, you still owe me that wish!

options.content: Sure, whenever you feel ready.
Oof, I walked right into this, didn't I?

dialogues.content: Hehe, let's fill this book with wonderful stories in the future!

name: Nurturing Love
desc: Thump, thump, thump — did you hear that? It's the sound of love flowing through.
memoryDesc: Drink it down. Swallow the bitterness in the glass, and embrace the sweetness of love.

dialogues.content: Finally received your invitation. Much time has passed since I arrived at this place, and I'd been wondering how long you were going to keep this poor wandering perfumer waiting.
You should know even the most passionate heart cannot burn forever. Indifference will extinguish those flames, leaving it hard and cold.

options.content: Indifference? What have I done?
...That's right, that's what I am, cold and uncaring.

dialogues.content: You left me out in the cold. Fate is so cruel for giving me a romance that begins with the coldest of shoulders.

options.content: Romance? Between whom?

dialogues.content: *sigh* Never thought your words could be even colder than your actions. Are you truly blind to the romance that is about to blossom?

options.content: Romance? Between whom?

dialogues.content: Between you and me, of course. Who else's eyes are looking deep into each other at this very moment?
Don't be so surprised, hehe. You might treat me as a temporary guest staying over at your place. But for me, every encounter is a story waiting to unfold, especially when it's you.
Don't look away. Your wine-red eyes reflect possibilities of our future. Within this intoxicating haze, we shall share a duet of love or a walk in my aroma garden.
You will eventually sway to my passions, and every inch of you shall bear my scent. When that moment comes, fate shall reveal if you are indeed the destined one.
You don't even need to make your own move for all this to happen. Just submit and follow my lead, and I shall let you experience a love of utmost purity and sweetness.

options.content: Calm down. We've just met.
I get it now. You're rehearsing poetic literature for a theatre show.

dialogues.content: Hehe, I understand your concerns. But you should know that no law or tradition dictates the number of days one must wait for love to sprout.
Ahem... What a cute and lovely guess. Perhaps I shall rephrase my words: I'm about to ascend the stage called Love, and I'm seeking a suitable partner.
Of course, if you wish to refuse, then just treat today's encounter as a scented dream that I have carefully concocted for you.
But I want you to know that I, Rebecca the wandering perfumer, am always seeking my destined life partner.
When I finally find the one, I shall share countless moments and sweet words with them, and we will never be apart.
I know it is difficult, for I am enshrouded in a warm layer of sweet venom. Though the coating protects me, it renders me incapable of receiving intimate hugs or loving kisses.
But I never give up. I strongly believe that if this land gave birth to a freak like me, it must have given birth to another who can withstand my venom and accept me for who I am.
And you, my darling with wine-red eyes, you showed me the potential in this.
So, let's consider this very moment as our very first date, a sweet little gift for your sincerity.
You can refuse, but then my venom will seal your tongue to safeguard my secret forever. Which one do you prefer?

name: One of a Kind
desc: Love is meant to be tested. Rather than sweet nothings, a drop of poison feels like a far more honest trial. Whether forever apart or happily ever after — why not find out now?
memoryDesc: The jellyfish twirls in the glass under the light, sinking silently into the depths, failing to find a companion before it dissipates upon reaching the sea floor.

dialogues.content: Another occasion of us alone. It's rare that someone hasn't fled screaming in terror after discovering that side of me.

options.content: That side of you?

dialogues.content: You must have sensed it already.
Stretch out your arms and take a look. Aww, such clean and lovely arms. Though callused and scarred, they remain pure and immaculate. And when tired, they only weep with salty sweat—
They differ from mine, which solely exude and bleed deadly venom.
The uncontrollable venom is like a wild old friend of mine. I rely on it to ward off Filthoids pouncing on me in forest trails or to send pursuing soldiers to an eternal sleep.

But the venom is the vile and vicious repellant of anything and anyone that I wish to get closer to. Merely washing my face in a pond paralyses and suffocates any fish that tries to give me a friendly peck.
I once detested it. If not for my venom, I would be like many other girls of my age. I would be picking out my favorite clothes at the market, or stealing a glance at my crush.

options.content: Never thought you'd dream of that.
You said once... Does that mean you've grown used to it?

dialogues.content: They're not dreams. Just occasional notions that never linger. I laugh at myself for having had those thoughts.
Not exactly. It's more like I've subdued the venom. I found a more fitting way to coexist with it.

Now, I no longer peep at someone I like, nor waste time on hours of useless talk to test their sincerity. A moment of sweet embrace is all I need to determine if this one is suited for a long-term commitment with me.
The venom serves as my most valuable touchstone. If I meet someone capable of withstanding my embrace, I would immediately know that I've met the destined one.
It's just that this person has yet to appear — perhaps they never will. But don't you find this far more romantic than the inane love talks between worldly people?
At least for me, it's a gift. Those who fear me, intimidate me, care for me, or obey me are all subject to this fair and equal trial.
Although I remain the same as I was and my wanderings continue, I no longer envy others, because my unique venom will help me find the special love that will be wholly mine.
Now, I intend to open my arms and ask you one question: Will you embrace me?

options.content: It's too dangerous. I refuse.
Try it if you dare.

dialogues.content: Hehe, don't be scared. You're the first to hear me divulge this much about my past. You get only one chance, but perhaps you're indeed the one I've been searching for.
And then you'll pierce my throat with that sword in your hand, right? Hehe, don't be so on guard. I can feel it. We're kindred souls, you and me, fated to lead lives not shared by any other.
*sigh* I didn't expect that this date, iniciated by you, would actually end with your rejection of my advance. What a pity.
But we still have time, and you'd better be careful. A day might come when I decide to appear right behind you and hold you tight.

options.content: You won't get a chance like that.

dialogues.content: Oh, how cute, just like a little kitten baring its tiny fangs. Perhaps I should keep my distance, then. Goodbye, I look forward to our next rendezvous.
Only a few seconds have passed, yet we meet again.
Hehe, it seems you're not that wary of me, which is nice. Don't worry, I don't intend to embrace you right now, but I have a word of advice:
Turn around and look at me once you hear my voice the next time we meet, and do not shift your gaze elsewhere, or something dangerous might happen.
Now, this is goodbye for sure. Arrivederci.

name: The Heart of a Monster
desc: Even monsters have vulnerabilities. They aren't heartless demons — just lonely misfits lost among the crowd.
memoryName: Drink: A Song of Ice and Fire
memoryDesc: Relationships often mirror this drink: starting with warmth, followed by bitterness, and ending with a chill. Like water and fire, some things were never meant to blend.

options.content: You won't get a chance like that.

The "Unspoken Bond of Love" has called me here today. Every drop of my venom yearns to see you.
Interested in seeing how in tune we are with each other? Guess what I'm about to say next.

options.content: I don't like guessing what others are thinking.
Matters of your past?

dialogues.content: And being so straightforward happens to be one of your charms.
That's right. See, we are so in sync with each other. Seems I've made the right choice in deciding to do this.
Then let's just skip the senseless prattle and focus directly on matters of the past.
I'm about to share a certain secret with you, which also means danger is approaching.
I once met someone like me. She was born with fiery-red skin. Her temperament is the same, a blazing firebrand with little tolerance for the impure.

Unlike me, a monster despised and abandoned since childhood, she carries the legacy and hopes of her family, and ultimately becomes the righteous warden. No criminal she sets her sights on can ever escape her.
However, like my venom, her flames tend to drive away or scare off anyone who tries to approach, be it with good or ill intent.

options.content: Is she after you?

dialogues.content: Yes. You know, a monster like me, who's born with lethal venom, can't help but leave a few bodies behind, whether by accident or willful intent. It shouldn't surprise you that I'm wanted.
During her long and persistent chase, I realised something — she's just like me, we're both lonely monsters. So, I took advantage of this.
I offered a seemingly sincere confession to confuse her, making her realise that she wasn't the only freak in this vast land and think that her pity and clemency would get me back on track.
But then, I just ran away right after she destroyed the evidence of my crimes.

You can hardly imagine how furious she became, how her fires burnt as she gnashed her teeth and swore to throw me in prison. However, you should know that by granting me refuge, you will be seen as an accomplice.

options.content: I'm already wanted by the Empire anyway. Being listed for another crime hardly matters to me.
Perhaps we should keep an appropriate distance.

dialogues.content: Is that so? Now I understand why I always feel an intoxicating aura of danger whenever I see you.
How cunning. How do you come up with these ambiguous lines of rejection that subtly lead people on?
Since you showed no sign of displeasure or rejection after I told you about a potential threat, does that mean we're growing closer?
Appropriate... how am I supposed to interpret that? For me, shadowing you around is the appropriate distance... But what about you? I'm not sure what's the appropriate distance for you.
I confess that I did struggle a bit when I was deciding if I should tell you about my dangerous past. I was worried that I would end up wandering this world on my own again.
Is it like secret lovers who frolic only when alone and pretend to be strangers in the presence of others? Or should we just go our separate ways and never, ever see each other again?
But I cannot bear to see you menaced by other threats. My venom alone is dangerous enough as it is.

But these two extremes might just offer the easiest solutions. Instead of just saying "I do" or "I hope you find someone who actually deserves you," you chose the option that paves the way for future dialogues and tests.
Yet your answers have strengthened my belief that I shall find my destined one by staying here.

options.content: Destined one?

dialogues.content: I can't get too close and risk putting you in danger, nor can I stay away from you and let us become strangers.
Yes, someone that I've yet to find as I travelled from Luca to Hyperborea. I thought that person only appeared in my dreams as a shiny yet indistinct figure.
This is like crafting a perfume formula without precise measurements. I can only keep fiddling with the weights and measures as I work towards the perfect result.

options.content: Why do I get the feeling that you're enjoying this?

dialogues.content: {性别:His|Her} body is strong enough to withstand every drop of my venom... whose heart is pure enough to take in all my love... and whose hands are gentle enough to wipe away all my sorrows...
Of course I am. I've never had a problem like this before, and I believe that by solving it, I will get the answer I've been looking for and find my destined one.

options.content: Destined one?

dialogues.content: Do you think {性别:he|she} has heard all that?

options.content: Every word of it, I believe.
Who would that be? I can relay your words if you want.

dialogues.content: Yes, someone that I've yet to find as I travelled from Luca to Hyperborea. I thought that person only appeared in my dreams as a shiny yet indistinct figure.
Oh... Hahahaha...
{性别:His|Her} body is strong enough to withstand every drop of my venom... whose heart is pure enough to take in all my love... and whose hands are gentle enough to wipe away all my sorrows...
You are so cute, weird, and interesting that I just can't get enough of...
As for whether the destined one is you, who is so cute, weird, and interesting that I just can't get enough of...
I really want to embrace you with my venom now... But I'm 100% serious when it comes to love.
Please give me some time to ponder over it.
So, let's give us some time to ponder over it.

name: Love's Edge
desc: Love is a blade that cuts through all barriers, whether across mountains, seas, or a single drop of lethal poison.
memoryDesc: This drink is simple in appearance and straightforward in flavour, for true love requires no embellishments — it exists in the gaze of the beloved.

dialogues.content: *sigh*...

options.content: Something troubling you?
Guess I didn't invite you at the right time.

dialogues.content: Yes, a most vexing matter, and the person who is in front of me is the very source of that trouble.
No, it's not about the timing, it's the person. My troubles began the moment I received your invitation.
Despite your pure, flawless appearance, you can suffocate people with your own "venom."
You did not announce your danger like I did at our first encounter, but instead cautiously wove a web of words.
Perhaps you didn't mean to, but it makes people more accustomed to staying here subconsciously, being imperceptibly influenced and changed by you.
After leaving Luca, I hardly stayed at any place for long or met anyone worthy of my attention.
I thought it would be the same this time — that I would bid farewell to the one with my embrace when I was tired of the journey.
But I hesitated this time. The venom within my body keeps whispering that I can never leave this place.
I can't take this, and this is the source of my troubles. So, I've decided to conclude this journey today.
Simply put — I want to wrap you in my venom and bid you farewell.
So, any last words for the last seconds?

options.content: You're running away from who you really are.
Your acting is terrible.

dialogues.content: Running away? No, not at all. I know exactly what I want, and I yearn to see the terror on your face.
Really? That didn't scare you at all? I was so hoping to see terror on your face. What a pity.
But you don't seem scared. What a pity.
Then I'll have to settle for the next best thing, and tell you about my real thoughts.
Days I shared with you are unlike the others I had before. I would say romantic things and we would test each other's sincerity during these afternoon dates...
And when the date ended, I would take my umbrella and find a deserted alley. There, I would mull over the conversations we had while dancing and swaying all on my own.
Hehe... Isn't that romantic as well?
I had always wanted to find the destined one who was capable of surviving my embrace. But today, I finally realised that all I want is love that belongs to me.
My embrace used to be my touchstone. But when my heart skipped a beat, I started to know that true love, the kind I can call my own, does not need to be tested.
The kisses and hugs are not necessary. I prefer the lingering aftertaste that does not fade.
It doesn't seem bad to have daily routines like morning greetings, smelling my latest perfume, and continuing my work on other perfume recipes...

I will try to make a perfume that can neutralise my venom, or search for a spell that can cleanse the toxins. Like some little mermaid in those fairytales, I'll do whatever I can to change for my love.
Perhaps a day will come when I can finally hold you in my arms.
Not for any test, but only to express my love for you.

name: Master of Disguise
desc: Camouflage offers protection; mimicry punishes the wicked.
memoryDesc: Down it goes! The tart sweetness pops on your tongue like children's laughter, crackling and bursting on the porch.

dialogues.content: ...Hey! Didn't you see I suddenly vanished after finishing my drink? How could you just act like nothing happened?!
Right in broad daylight, Demon Tabethe the Red Hand mysteriously disappeared! Aren't you at least a bit curious or worried?

options.content: There was an extra chair here... It was you, wasn't it?
Why would I be worried? If anything, I appreciate that you turned into a chair just to entertain me.

dialogues.content: What?! You saw through my awesome disguise?!
Pff, get over yourself — I was just trying to spook you! BOO! Get it?
Hmph, I slipped up this time. But next time, I'll turn into something you'd never expect!
What to turn into next... Maybe a barrel? A chandelier? Or even a big hammer?
Wow, you're really good at this.
Of course! I heard this trick of mine is called... caramel... camel... camel-something... Ah — camouflage! That's it!
So you can turn into anything?
Hehe, you bet! Watch this—
I'll make an offer you can't refuse. Think it over before you respond.
What wakes me is business; what about you?

options.content: Haha — what wakes me is the blinding brilliance of Demon Tabethe the Red Hand!
Haha — I'm going to tell on you to Camilla!

dialogues.content: Hehe, you're so sweet — sweeter than this drink you made!
I'm not scared of her! No one can catch Demon Tabethe the Red Hand!
But I can't turn into anything too big or too small. I can do a cat, but not a mouse; a barrel, but not a lamppost.
That's enough to fool most people, though. I can just turn into a bin or a crate, and those rotten thieves won't know what hit them!

options.content: ...Oh boy, this might be a problem someday.
Sounds impressive; good thing you're not a baddy.

dialogues.content: What are you mumbling about?
What do you mean?
Nothing, I just meant you are awesome.
I mean, imagine if someone smart but nasty had your skills — the whole town would be in chaos.
But maybe avoid turning into bins or crates next time. Wouldn't want someone accidentally smashing you while looking for something useful...
Mm-hmm, I thought so too! I'm nothing like those bad grown-ups. Wait, are you saying I'm not smart?
Who would do that?
Of course not, Tabethe is very smart. Anyway, I've been curious about these "bad grown-ups" you always talk about. Who are they?
Er... some overly curious passersby, perhaps?
Any bullies who pick on the weak! The first time I met bad grown-ups was at the orphanage. Those caretakers... well, calling them "caretakers" is a stretch — they were more like jailers.
Always taking what's useful and tossing the rest — typical bad grown-ups!
Back then, when they caught me sneaking food in the kitchen, they'd beat me. Ugh, those monsters! I only did it because they never fed me enough!
Those passersby wouldn't mean to hurt anyone! Anyway, who are those "bad grown-ups" you always talk about?
If I ran into them now, I'd hang them upside down from the ceiling and make them watch as I eat up all the food in the kitchen!

options.content: There, there. Those bad grown-ups can't hurt you anymore.
Sounds great! Those baddies so deserve that.

dialogues.content: Hmph! Exactly!
Alright, I've finished my drink. I'll tell you more about those bad grown-ups next time. Now, let's go play outside!
Hehehe, wanna play hide and seek? I bet you won't find me so easily this time!

name: Escaping the Orphanage
desc: Others may define good and bad, but it's up to you to decide right from wrong.
memoryDesc: Sweet and salty aren't opposites, just as innocence and mischief can coexist.

dialogues.content: Mmm, this drink's a bit salty but so yummy — like sea breeze-flavored cotton candy!
It kind of reminds me of something I drank long ago... back when I was still with my mom and dad, before our ship sank and I ended up at that orphanage...
But honestly, I'd choose wandering on my own over staying with those bad grown-ups! They were stingy with food, not to mention anything as nice as a drink.
At least being on the streets, I could scavenge for something to eat — beats starving under the watch of those bad grown-ups!
When I got a bit older, groups of rich visitors would come by now and then, taking away some unwanted kids with horns like me. People at the orphanage said they were adopted by rich families.

I didn't want new parents, but I thought being in a rich home meant I'd never go hungry again, so I wanted them to take me. But those bad grown-ups said no rich people would want a naughty troublemaker like me.
Hmph! As if I'd ever behave just to be chosen! I couldn't stand that awful place for another day, so during their visit, I transformed into one of their suitcases.

Turns out those rich folks weren't too bright — they just picked me up and walked away, completely clueless. It was rough on my ears, though — they were pulled as the handles, and I almost got dropped along the way!

options.content: Oof, that must've hurt a lot! I'll take extra care of your ears from now on!
Managing to escape from that place proves Demon Tabethe the Red Hand was awesome even as a kid!

dialogues.content: ...Thanks, sounds a bit weird though...
Hehe, you bet! Too bad I wasn't as skilled back then, or I wouldn't have turned my ears into the handles.
Actually, I was planning to sneak in with those kids getting adopted, hoping I'd never starve again with a rich family.
But those rich people reeked of disinfectant — it stung my nose! And the way they looked at those kids... I don't know why, but it gave me the creeps...
It was like... a chef sizing up fish or ducks!
I've seen too many bad grown-ups to trust them — I might be better off on my own. So I didn't join those kids, and ended up running away by myself.
And that was my first step towards becoming Demon Tabethe the Red Hand!

options.content: I think you're not a bad kid, Tabethe. You're just... very special.
Those rich visitors sounded really sketchy; you made a smart call, Tabethe.

dialogues.content: Not bad, just special? No one's ever put it that way before... A special kid, special... Hehe!
Exactly, you got it!
Getting out safely on your own was already something. Congratulations on earning your freedom, Tabethe.
Back then, I was just focused on getting away. If I were as good at my disguise tricks then, I would've secretly followed them to see what they were really up to!

Yeah, I did great! Breathing fresh air again was so awesome. For the first time, I realised the night sky wasn't always so dark, and the dim stars I'd seen through dirty glass were actually bright and beautiful.
I slept under the stars that night, right on the grass — and woke up to a beautiful sunny day! Since that day, I've been living in that little seaside town, free from those bad grown-ups!
And I met someone there...
Did you finally meet someone kind?
Yep, a really, really kind person! But I'm a bit tired now... even Demon Tabethe the Red Hand needs her rest!
Next time you whip up a new drink, I'll tell you all about it!

name: The Line Between Good and Evil
desc: Once you open your eyes, a broader world unfolds.
memoryDesc: The initial sourness knits your brow, but as your taste buds adjust, a smooth sweetness blooms — much like understanding the world: hope always follows the storm.

dialogues.content: Yum-yum! This drink's so good — just like all the other drinks you've made! Hehe, you know exactly what I like.
I fell asleep on the grass under the stars last night. The sky turned from bright blue to dark navy, with stars twinkling like frosting on a blueberry smoothie!
Except for the night I escaped the orphanage, I almost never had such a sound night's sleep on the grass.
...Because when I first got to the town, I did a lot of bad stuff...
The grown-ups there hated me for that. They called me a "demon"...

options.content: Did you maybe go too far with your pranks?
Did you polish off all the fish in town?

dialogues.content: They could've handled it if they were smarter! Well... you're right, it was my fault.
I'm not that big of an eater! Well, you got part of it right though...

I had been living off stealing food from the street stalls. The vendors were so mad they tried to beat me, but I just mimicked their angry faces to piss them off. I didn't think what I did was wrong back then.
"I just took a little, it's not like you'd starve! Tightwad!"
Until I met her...

She was the fishmonger's daughter. She caught me stealing from her dad's stall but didn't tell on me; instead, she gave me fish to fill my belly, asked if I was separated from my family, and even offered me a place to stay for the night. She was the first truly kind person I'd ever met.
A lot happened after that... She ended up without a home and had to go to the orphanage — like I'd let her go through what I had! I decided I'd be her family!
We'd giggle under the hot sun, splash each other by the sea, and race down muddy paths together. I'd turn into little animals just to make her laugh.
She was like a little sister to me — she'd call me Big Sis Tabethe. Even though we didn't always have enough food, she always said she was happy.
It was because of her that I decided to stop stealing from good grown-ups. From then on, Demon Tabethe the Red Hand would only target the bad ones!

options.content: Is it because you care about what she thinks?
Big Sis Tabethe!

dialogues.content: Yeah. I didn't wanna break her heart.
Wha... Stop it! You're embarrassing both yourself and me!
At first, I didn't listen — how could those vendors be good people? I was starving, and they just yelled at me, never giving me anything to eat.
I just wanted to see if you'd also take me in if I called you that...
But then I realised — some vendors actually saw me stealing, but they looked the other way.
...Are you an eight-year-old? Come on, act your age.
And those who chased me never really followed through... Of course, they couldn't catch me if they tried — I was fast...!
Just kidding. So, was it because you really care about what she thinks?
And some vendors even left unsold food out for me. But back then I thought they did it because they were scared of me and were paying protection money.
She once asked me, "Is it right to steal from good people?"
I held such a grudge against the bad people I met, that I was completely blind to the kindness of those good people.
When I realised all this, I felt so bad that the food I stole tasted off.
I guess I'd been taking out my hate for the bad grown-ups on those vendors.
I really was a demon...

options.content: There's no need to beat yourself up, Tabethe. A lot of people fail to own up to their mistakes in a whole lifetime. You already did great.
You will grow up someday. Wouldn't bullying good people just make you one of the bad grown-ups?

dialogues.content: Thank you... but you don't need to sugar-coat it for me. I know what I did was wrong.
You're right... Go ahead and let me have it. I won't talk back — I deserve this.
Ever since then, I'd only take stuff from bad thieves and mean grown-ups. It felt great, and it wouldn't hurt good people.
And guess what — those bad guys are loaded! I hardly ever go hungry now. Plus, I get to play tricks on them and watch them fume, hehe, it's so much fun!

options.content: It's more about the fun of playing tricks on them than finding stuff to eat, huh?

dialogues.content: Exactly! Er, I mean, not really! This is about "serving justice." All I did was teach them not to mess with the good folks.
Whew, that was a lot of talking today — my throat's literally smoking!
Hehe, can I get a refill of that blueberry drink?

name: Tabethe's Tentacle 6
desc: Even in chaos, there is warmth to be found.
memoryName: Drink: Demon Tabethe the Red Hand

dialogues.content: You both chug Tabethe's special concoction. A bizarre sweetness overwhelms your taste buds; soon after, you black out.
Aaaare you alright?! Oh no... it wasn't the drink, was it...?
...I drank the same thing! It was so good that it knocked me out for a moment, but I'm perfectly fine now! Hey, wake up! Don't even think about trying to scam me by pretending it's food poisoning...!

options.content: Will you keep it down...? I'm fine... just heard some tentacles talking, that's all...

dialogues.content: Doc! Help!!!
You're still feeling awful, but you seem to see Tabethe's tentacles cheerfully quivering, as if they are nodding at you.
This is so good! I could never get enough of this drink! I don't often say nice things, but thank you for always making these for me.
Hehehe, since you've made so many good drinks for me, it's time I return the favour!
Before you is a suspicious dark drink, bubbling and giving off a strange scent. Upon closer inspection, you recognise various dried fruits and candies settled at the bottom.
Ta-da! Behold my special creation — Demon Tabethe the Red Hand — named after my own title! Just so you know, this glass is filled with my thanks, hehe!

options.content: Refuse the drink
Accept the drink

dialogues.content: Come on! This is the one and only "Demon Tabethe the Red Hand" in the world!
Excellent choice!

I've put all the good food that good grown-ups gave me into this drink. I've been saving the ingredients bit by bit — tried so hard not to eat them right away! I can't even imagine how yummy this drink will be with all that good stuff put together!

I've put all the good food that good grown-ups gave me into this drink. I've been saving the ingredients bit by bit — tried so hard not to eat them right away! I can't even imagine how yummy this drink will be with all that good stuff put together!
How about we share it? Not that I want to try it myself! I'm just setting an example for a coward!
Who else but you deserves such a precious drink, right? But could you share a little with me? Hehe, I'm curious what the best drink in the world tastes like!
Cheers!
Alright, I'm done getting all mushy! Cheers!
They're still breathing. Both of them are fine — just passed out.
Waah... I was so scared... I've warned Tabethe not to put just anything in that drink — it's not safe...
Hehehe, maybe it'll mess up their brains and cause some weird side effects!
Knock it off! You ghoul!

options.content: ...Who's there?

dialogues.content: You see several tentacles extending from Tabethe gently swaying in front of you.
Did you hear that...? {nickname} is talking to us.
To my knowledge, only Tabethe can hear us speak.
...Oh no... This is bad, really bad! I knew it — every time 5 says something bad, it always happens for real! Could you zip it next time? I'm begging you!

options.content: Are those tentacles talking...?

dialogues.content: Um... hello? Yes, we're Tabethe's tentacles. Never thought we'd be having a conversation like this! Life's full of surprises, huh? Haha...
Um... it might be that drink that caused this situation... We're so sorry... didn't mean to make you chug down something weird...

options.content: Is Tabethe okay?
Am I okay?

dialogues.content: Based on my observations, you're both just reacting to some... special ingredients. A good sleep should fix it!
Ahem, just so you know — it was under my leadership that we concocted this beverage for Tabethe's unprecedented get-together with you!
Hmm? I thought it was because Tabethe knew nothing about making drinks, so she just threw in some pretty mushroom slices, which led to this.
Hehe, keep acting all smug, 3, and you might find yourself part of the next drink, hehehe.
Ah, that sounds horrible! Waah!
Please, you guys are too loud... Aren't you tired? And don't scare {nickname}...

options.content: Got it — this is a dream. A really weird one.

dialogues.content: That's one way to see it. Though no one knows how long the drink's effects will last... Actually, there's quite a lot we'd like to talk to you about! Maybe this is the chance... 1, you go first!
...My sentience came into being on the ocean, right after the shipwreck. I kept Tabethe company during those dark times in the sea. She got through it by talking to me.

I... I woke up when Tabethe had just been taken in by the orphanage. The staff there were mean to her; she was scared, but wouldn't show weakness in front of anyone. At night, she'd cling on to me, shivering...
I myself joined this esteemed group in the orphanage's kitchen. In a dire moment, it was under my command that we managed to evade the patrolling guards and secure half a loaf of bread!
And as for my manner of speaking, it's a perfect impersonation of the head of the orphanage.
Yawn... I awoke the night we escaped the orphanage. The sense of relief was so heavy... that once we were safe, I fell asleep right away on the grass with her...
And then there's me, hehehe! I'm Tabethe's best partner in crime! The thrill of all sorts of heists is just the best! Woo-hoo!
Get ahold of yourself! Sorry, this kid is a bit of a wild card. Ahem, I'm the youngest, and only recently became sentient.

Actually, I woke up once a long time ago. But then that little fish vendor girl got separated from Tabethe, which made her very sad. She didn't talk about it, but it hit her really hard and even affected me — I fell back into slumber, immersed in those memories.
Until she met another person who also truly cherishes her — yes, it was because of you that I woke up again.
Thank you for taking care of Tabethe. Your kindness woke me from my dream. And it was on my suggestion that she decided to make this drink as a thank you.
But I didn't expect her to go this overboard! She knows nothing about mixing drinks and just tossed in whatever looked good — and you two, 3 and 5! You two egged her on!
We're so sorry...

options.content: Haha, it's okay.

dialogues.content: Tabethe's waking up. How do you feel?
Ah, already?! I haven't finished my speech...

options.content: What a weird dream. Better wake up ASAP...
They're adorable. I hope this could happen more often.

dialogues.content: That odd taste hits you again. Even though you've experienced it before, it still overwhelmingly floods your senses.

Before blacking out again, you seem to hear a cacophony of voices: "Gods bless the kind-hearted," "What doesn't kill you makes you stronger," "I'll take the lead with the head," along with many voices murmuring, "Thank you."

name: Sleeplessness
desc: A healer who once slumbered for a century now offers to treat your sleeplessness.
memoryDesc: A compendium cataloguing 1,890 medicinal substances — nearly half of them herbs. The author's name reads: Fufeng.

dialogues.content: Spring vetch, summer amaranth; autumn citrus, winter ganoderma...
Where no sun shines, Ashless Wood thrives; in hearts of frost, Dewiolet blooms. Beneath thick grasses, Verdawort coils; from hidden scents, Vesperleaf stirs.

options.content: They sound like plant names. If they're listed in that book you're reading, I figure they must be useful for something.
That sounds like something from a medical text. Is it about herbs?
Am I interrupting? You seemed deeply absorbed in your reading.

dialogues.content: Indeed. Each one bears medicinal properties — a few are even edible.
Hehe... I didn't know you were so well-read. You're right — it's from Essentials of Medicinal Herbs.
Not at all. There's no need for such formality between us. You're always welcome here.
I've been reading for quite some time now... A short respite may be in order.
Though this Hall of Ephemerality lies long deserted, I've no fine tea to serve... I fear I've made a poor host.

options.content: Is it hard, living here all on your own?
It's nothing.
Oh no — there goes my free meal!

dialogues.content: It was, at first. But my ties to this place run deep... and in time, I came to embrace the solitude.
Thank you for your forbearance. I suppose this is what they call "a friendship as calm as water".
Feeling hungry already? But it's still a touch early for a proper meal. Bear with it a while longer, if you can.
Since fate has granted us this rare encounter, allow me to speak plainly. There is... something I wish to ask of you.
Go ahead. I'm listening.
The other day, I treated the young lady wounded by that Sable Bi'an using a remedy I found in one of my sister's old notes. It stirred in me... an interest in pharmacology.

My clan has long practised the Art of Ephemerality. But pharmacology — as a formal discipline — has only emerged in the past century. My sister excelled in it. As for me... my grasp is but fragmentary.

I've never wavered in my wish to carry forward our family's calling. Yet my return from a long slumber — that miracle was wrought by the lifelong efforts of my sister and her disciples. Such devotion... cannot go unanswered.
That's why I've begun studying modern medicine. But books alone can only take one so far.
What I truly long for is practice — to observe, to examine, to diagnose... To understand what illness means in the living body.
But a century has passed in the blink of an eye. I have no kin left... no companions in this era.
And if I were to err in treating a stranger... it would be malpractice, no different from harm.
So I searched my thoughts for someone who knows me — who might be willing to take that risk for me. In the end... there is only you.
That said, health is a deeply private matter. If you are unwilling, I shall not press you.

options.content: If it helps you rely less on the Art of Ephemerality, I'd be glad to help.
Free check-ups? Count me in! How do we start?
That's it? I thought you were going to ask me to fight Zhuyin or something!

dialogues.content: My thanks... It may seem a small kindness to you, but I shall carry it close to heart.
Eh—? Y—You trust me that much!? Wait, there's no need to take off your cloak just yet...
Heavens, I'd never ask anything so perilous! But... was that a yes?
Then... you have my deepest thanks. I'll give it everything I have.
Fushu conducts a thorough and meticulous examination.
Hm... You're in good health overall — at least, from what I can observe. However...
It doesn't show in your face, but... you've been without proper rest for quite some time, haven't you?

options.content: I've just been on the move a lot lately. Haven't really had the chance...
I've been chasing Proprietress Zhiliu's sky-high allowance — who has time to sleep with that kind of reward dangling in front of you?
Bah, sleep's overrated. Who really needs it anyway?

dialogues.content: If this keeps up, it could take a real toll on your health. Please take care. And if you've nowhere else to rest... the Hall of Ephemerality is open to you — for as long as you need.

Seeking fortune is only natural... but pushing yourself to exhaustion is far from wise. If this persists, your next check-up won't be complimentary. I might even have to levy a rather steep consultation fee.
Hm... If the patient proves especially noncompliant, I may have to prescribe a more... hands-on remedy.
Your level of sleep deprivation is quite severe... Have you been struggling with insomnia? Or difficulty falling asleep?
Nooo... I take it back!
Like what?
Maybe I'm just someone who doesn't need much sleep by nature... But I do dream a lot. Sometimes I wake suddenly and can't fall back asleep.
I trained in martial arts from a young age. For ordinary sprains or fractures, I can manage treatment even without the Art of Ephemerality.
I see. I had assumed it was merely the pace of life since arriving in Huaxu... but this runs deeper. You've carried it with you far longer.
But if a patient thrashes in pain, it could aggravate the injury... In such cases, a strike here may render them unconscious. Come — allow me to show you.
In any case, I've prepared a formula. I can't promise immediate results, but with consistent use, it should gradually ease the symptoms.
N—No, thank you! I'll take the conservative treatment!
That said... the key ingredient is Oneirowort — and the Hall of Ephemerality is currently out of stock. It's normally sourced from EverSpring, but procuring it may take days.
Our best chance may be to search the nearby area. With luck, you might sleep soundly as soon as tonight. What do you think?
Sounds great! I'd appreciate that.
Come — no sense in lingering.

name: Haunting Dreams
desc: A single blade of grass may veil the eyes — and all that lies before them becomes a waking dream of what is long past.
memoryDesc: Nearly identical in appearance to Oneirowort, yet known to induce hallucinations. If hallucinations are waking dreams, then their likeness begins to make sense.

dialogues.content: Liltfern sways where waters stream; Eclipta blooms where ripples gleam. Where fungi root beneath the tree, Oneirowort and Echowort be — Which is which, none e'er could see.
I heard you reciting something earlier — what do those lines mean?
A rhyme from the appendix of Essentials of Medicinal Herbs — a simple mnemonic verse describing where certain plants tend to grow. It was written to help folk find remedies in times of need.
These days in Huaxu, most people know at least a few lines. It's become something of a common chant.
Once committed to memory, it teaches you where to search — should you be bitten by a snake, stung by an insect, or fall ill far from aid.
The part I was reciting says Liltfern grows beneath the stream, Eclipta Grass by the water's edge, and Oneirowort by tree roots — often where fungi thrive. However...
There's another plant, Echowort, that so closely resembles Oneirowort it's near impossible to tell them apart, unless you're a seasoned herbalist or physician.
My sister left behind some comparative sketches in her notes, but...
(Fushu opens a weathered tome before you. You glance at the illustration — it wouldn't look out of place in one of Luca's avant-garde exhibits. You and Fushu exchange a helpless look.)
...Is there any other way?
There is.
You can actually make sense of this? And you still say you're not good at pharmacology?
I meant what I said. My knowledge barely scratches the surface.
Which is why... I plan to taste it.
Right now?
Right now.
You're really going to eat it?
I am.

Don't worry — Echowort's toxins are exceedingly mild. Some feel nothing at all. At most, you may glimpse a fleeting vision. Its name stems from an old saying: "to leave one's echoes and smiles in another's memory" — a poetic way of remembering the departed.
...You do know that doesn't exactly make me less worried about you, right?
There's no need for alarm. In most cases, whether a plant is poisonous or not lies in the dose.
A single sliver of Echowort may bring on a vision — but it fades swiftly.
Most physicians discourage this method... yet for many herb gatherers, it remains the surest test.
Besides — I practise the Art of Ephemerality. Even if a reaction occurs, I can recover at once. Truly, there's no need to worry.
(Fushu plucks the tip of the grass and places it on her tongue. Before long, her gaze dips low — and she begins to murmur softly beneath her breath.)
Mmh...
Why... forsake...
You... the Art of Ephemerality...
...Fushu? Fushu!? Do you still know who you are?
Of course. I am Fushu, the Zhuyou therapy user.

Endowed with divine power by the Nine Chapters of Dafeng, I must heal the sick and tend the dying — to uphold my duty without fail, even at the cost of my last breath. That is the path passed down through generations of my bloodline...
So why do you, Fufeng... defy that path without shame? You spurn Heaven's order above, disregard life below... abandon your healer's oath, and stray from our family's creed...
Hold on! I'm not your sis—
After what you did... could you still call yourself my sister?

options.content: I'm not your sister. I'm your friend — {nickname}. We're here gathering herbs, remember?
I AM your sister. I've realised how wrong I was.
Actually, I'm your mother.

dialogues.content: What sort of ridiculous tale is that supposed to be...? Although... {nickname}... that name... it does feel... familiar...
You... truly regret it? This is... unexpected. I... I wasn't ready to forgive you...
Mother...? But... you passed long ago... I must have failed so deeply that you've come to chastise me yourself...
No... no, this isn't right... I'm not the Fushu of a century past.
And my sister... she's long gone too...
...Please. Leave me be. I need a moment alone.
An incense's time later, Fushu returns to where you parted.
Feeling better?
Mm. I'm all right now. Forgive me... I lost my composure.
Did I startle you?

options.content: You ate that herb just to help me sleep — how could I blame you?
First time someone a century older than me mistook me for their big sister. Weirdly exhilarating.

dialogues.content: Then I'm relieved.
In that vision, I glimpsed an argument with my sister — a memory more than a century old. I thought I'd long made peace with it... but perhaps not entirely.
Still... there was something unexpected. It seemed to hint that Echowort is more than a simple hallucinogen — it's also a rare culinary herb.
Some say it absorbs the memories of the places it grows. Those who consume it may glimpse echoes of the past — stories rooted in the soil beneath it.
This isn't noted in the current edition of Essentials of Medicinal Herbs... likely a scribal omission. I should make a record — and see it restored.
Come. We may still find Oneirowort nearby.
I don't know... that looked like a serious case of food poisoning.

It's not my nature to leave things half-done. Truly — I'm quite well. If you're curious, I could even demonstrate the full Five-Animal Frolics sequence. It's excellent for circulation... assuming you can keep up.
Uhh... maybe teach me after we find the Oneirowort?
Heh. It's a promise.

name: Echoes of the Past
desc: You saw her, plain as day — a healer, a nonconformist, and a sister.
memoryDesc: Bizarre in appearance, yet in Huaxu, it's a cherished symbol of longevity.

dialogues.content: Here's one.
I'll try it. Should the effects prove unpleasant, you may step aside and return once they pass.
Wait!
How about we switch — let me try it this time?
I cannot allow you to bear this in my stead. When I offered to treat you, I never intended to subject you to harm — however slight.
Exactly — you're the doctor here. So it should be me.
If something goes wrong, I know you'll be able to save me. But if you collapse... I wouldn't know where to begin. I'd be helpless.
I... I can't agree to that. But I see your reasoning — I didn't consider it carefully enough. Perhaps we should find ano—
(Before she can finish, you pinch off a sliver of the herb's blade and place it on your tongue.)
Ah—!
What are you—!? No... this isn't the time to—
How do you feel!?
Mmm... not bad. Kinda minty. It's got this clean, cooool...
(Her face begins to blur before your eyes. One thing becomes clear: you are not naturally tolerant to Echowort.)
Ugh... my head... This place — is this the Hall of Ephemerality?
And is that... Fushu?
Ugh... what a nuisance. Truly, what a wretched nuisance!
Told myself again and again this morning — don't snap, don't prod her. And yet what happened? Didn't even get through our breakfast before I provoked that stubborn mule again!
Fufeng, honestly... must you always rise to it? Prickly as she is, she's still your little sister. It's not as though you can simply turn your back on her. So why keep needling her?
But I can't help it! That solemn little face — it's infuriating. And now, the smile's gone from her lips... and somehow ended up on mine.
Human nature, isn't it? Just plain human nature...
F—Fushu? Is that you?
Ah — I'm afraid not. I'm Fufeng, her twin sister. You wouldn't be the first to mix us up.
You're looking for Fushu? How curious. She's not one to mingle — closed up like a little clamshell, that one. Didn't think she had anyone she'd call a friend.

options.content: Fushu treats everyone with sincerity. She's a good physician — and a good friend.
I'm actually one of her patients. She charged me a fortune last time — I'm here to get my money back.
Hello, pretty lady! I'm not here for Fushu — I came for you!

dialogues.content: Huh... Someone your age, speaking so earnestly of her quiet ways? That's rare. Well, if you're a friend of hers, then you have a friend in me.
What, here to swindle my little sister now? Please — shake her upside down and not a single coin would fall. If you're going to lie, at least pick a more plausible mark.
Ugh, smooth talker. If you're neither sick or wounded, best run along and try your luck elsewhere.
So... what brings you to the Hall of Ephemerality?
I accidentally ate some Echowort. My head's spinning and I'm seeing strange things. I thought Fushu might know what to do, so I came looking for her.
Unlucky timing — she's sulking right now. Best not to poke the beehive. But I'm a physician too, you know. I could help.
Let me have a look...
Hmm... your footing's steady, eyes still sharp, speech coherent — I'd wager it was a small dose. Half a blade, perhaps?
Nothing serious. You'll feel fine before the antidote even finishes steeping. Just sit tight — it'll pass.
If it grows unbearable, I've some tangerine tonic on hand. Chew a few — they ought to ease the discomfort.
Let me guess — trouble sleeping? Too many dreams? Went hunting Oneirowort and picked Echowort instead?

If it's true relief you seek, you'd do better with a decoction of Creeping Tendrils and Crackblooms. Oneirowort may lull you to sleep, yes — but the memories it stirs will cling to your dreams, and weigh upon the heart.
...Looks aside, you and Fushu really are quite alike.
Now that's a rare remark. We may be twins, but I've always been the unruly one — ever toeing the line of Dafeng's Ninth Admonition.
Fushu may seem cold and distant, and you blaze like fire — but when you're tending the sick, you're the same. Meticulous, gentle... utterly sincere.
You... hah. Now I believe you're truly close to her.
That girl... so hopelessly stubborn. Bottles up every thought. And when she tries to speak from the heart, the words twist themselves into knots.
Takes someone patient and perceptive to understand her... Like you.
I've always had the sharper tongue — no wonder I rub her the wrong way. Some big sister I turned out to be.
Now then, friend of Fushu — I have a small favour to ask. And I trust you won't turn me down. Not when it's for her sake.
Sure. What is it?
May I trouble you to help me prepare an apology gift?
There's a stretch of water not far from here where Shouxing Squid tend to gather. Could you catch a few for me? It shouldn't prove too difficult.

name: Returning to Peace
desc: The Hall of Ephemerality stands empty — and yet, so long as memory endures, it remains the home she holds dear.
memoryDesc: Though the silver lamp yet burns, I fear our reunion was but a fleeting dream.

dialogues.content: Well now... you actually caught some? Impressive. As for me — jack of all trades though I claim to be — I could sit here all day and still come up empty...
"All trades" might've been a stretch.
Fushu showed me your paintings. Very... avant-garde.
...She showed you those? Just how close are the two of you?
Well... not close enough to know she had a thing for Shouxing Squid.
Not quite.
She loathes them. When we were little, just seeing one would have her bawling her eyes out.
We've been at odds a lot lately. I imagine you know why.
Simple, really — I want to explore new ways of healing. But she insists on clinging to the Art of Ephemerality.
And truthfully? I can't entirely fault her. My methods are untested, uncertain... and they stray far from the Nine Chapters of Dafeng.
What lies ahead for me — or my work — I can't say.
But one thing I do know: if she keeps pushing herself like this, the Art of Ephemerality will consume her.
And that... I couldn't bear. So no — I won't back down, which means we'll probably keep clashing, again and again.
That little sister of mine... never realises just how much I worry. Hmph. Even if I'm the one who has to apologise — I'm not making it easy on her!

She won't even let me near her right now. So, I'm counting on you to deliver these little "sweethearts." She trusts you — won't suspect a thing. Might even shriek like she did as a child — wouldn't that be amusing?

options.content: Shouxing squid...

dialogues.content: This is actually your way of saying, "May you live a long and healthy life," isn't it?
Ehh—! Must you spoil it by putting it into words? Sentiments lose their charm once spelled out. I was hoping to see that flustered little face of hers!
Now go on! Shoo, shoo!
Ah... you've come to!
Only three or four minutes passed, yet I was already fretting... I even began to question the texts — could the toxin have been more potent than I thought?
I nearly invoked the Art of Ephemerality — but feared you'd recover before the spell was done...
Haha — you two really are twin sisters...
You saw my sister...?
I did. You two had a fight. Then she tried to make peace — with Shouxing Squid, of all things.
...I'd forgotten. That was long, long ago.
Did you accept her apology?
No... we argued once more. I do not regret my words — and yet...
Perhaps now, I might bring myself to accept the offering.
Only perhaps. My aversion to multi-legged creatures remains wholly undiminished.
I shouldn't have let you glimpse such things. The past is long buried... to unearth it only invites old sorrow.
But this place — the Hall of Ephemerality — was where we came of age. I suppose every blade of Echowort here bears a sliver of our story.
So next time... allow me to be the one to taste it. Would you?

options.content: Sure — it's your memory. You should decide what to do with it.
But I was really hoping for some juicy drama...

dialogues.content: Thank you.
Hehe... Then next time we meet, I'll recount the whole tale myself.
Come — take this. Let's move on.
Here's one.
Care to guess — is it Echowort, or Oneirowort?

options.content: It's Oneirowort.
It's Echowort.

dialogues.content: It appears nearly identical to what we found before — but in the hand, the texture feels subtly different. I believe this is Oneirowort.
Had we not failed twice before, I might never have caught the difference.
How did the first person ever tell them apart? Trial and error, like us?
Heh... how did she do that, indeed?
She must've endured countless perils, sleepless nights, tireless study... Misunderstood, perhaps even hurt — yet never once losing heart.
All for the sake of an ancient vow — to mend, to soothe, to care — carried forward by healer after healer through the ages.
There's something I forgot to mention. Fufeng said Creeping Tendrils and Crackblooms work better for insomnia and restless sleep.
Oneirowort may help one sleep, but it also stirs old memories that weigh upon the heart.
So I don't really need it anymore. But... do you still want to try it?

Fushu does not reply. As before, she places the grass blade upon her tongue. But this time, there is no tension, no reproach — only the rhythm of her breath, and a faint murmur from the depths of a dream.
... Next time, pick a more fitting gift of apology, would you?

name: Visitor from the Legion
desc: Life is simple — eat to live, not the other way around. Keep that straight, and you'll be fine.
memoryDesc: A fiery, bold drink for those who crave a stronger kick. The first sip sparks your appetite, the second ignites your mood — a perfect icebreaker.

dialogues.content: Assessing your drink mixing skills? You got the wrong person. I know nothing about this.
All drinks are the same to me — If it tastes right, I'll drink it. When it comes to these bottles and flasks sounds, they are just noise to me.

options.content: Seems like the Legion has better food and drinks.

dialogues.content: The Legion's built for war, not picnics.
Wait, you mentioned the "Legion"...
...What do you want? What are you planning? Who are you? Who sent you? What intel are you after? Spill it.

options.content: I heard the Legion got a treasure called "No. 0".
You're overthinking it. I just want to offer you a drink.

dialogues.content: You're too well-informed for a mere Phoxhunter.
…I should've known. No one offers gifts without wanting something in return.
Guess I was too on edge. Ahem, sorry about that.
Time to take you to the Legion for questioning. Cooperate, and don't make me tie you up — it won't look good for either of us.
It's just there have been some audacious Phoxhunters who, seeing that I was one of them, tried to get close to me and fish for the secrets of the legion.

options.content: So you were a Phoxhunter before?
So you're originally from Icelake?

dialogues.content: (The following quickly flashes through your mind: Lynn takes out her gun immediately, and the dark muzzle is pointed straight at your forehead.)
Yeah, that was years ago. Wait, should I reveal this to others?
(This outcome is predictable. You shook your head and dismissed the risky idea to keep fishing out intel from her.)
...Never mind. The Legion doesn't say we have to hide who we were.

options.content: You seem to be so careful of what you say.

dialogues.content: You've got it wrong. I just saw you and thought I'd invite you for a drink.
Ugh, you have no idea what it's like in the Legion.
Legion camps are surrounded by electric fences powered by Phoxichor. They crackle with sparks, detering deserters, as well as discouraging thieves and spies.
But at least you can see those fences. It's the invisible ones you have to worry about — if you slip up, say the wrong thing, one zap, and you're gone.
My supreme officer has something personal against traitors. I don't want to end up dead over some accidental leak.

options.content: The Legion must have made you feel repressed.
I wouldn't have guessed — you seem to thrive on the status and prestige it brings.

dialogues.content: You think? I never wanted to be in the Legion.
Status and prestige? Sure, if you think risking your neck daily is worth it.
...I was happier as a Phoxhunter. It wasn't an easy gig, but at least I was free.
Not all commissions were about cheating death. Sometimes you'd get to walk dogs or hunt deer. And after a big score, you could enjoy a pint at The Asphodel.
You can do it on your own. No need to explain to anyone about your plans or worry about dead weight.
Most importantly, you didn't have to deal with commanders who can't stop their yapping.

options.content: Is this something I can know?

dialogues.content: I thought bad-mouthing your superiors can be considered as something wrong. Wouldn't that get you zapped?
A...Absolutely! I'm no noble — those thick-skinned aristocrats can definitely survive a zap. But if my superiors heard this, they'd fry me, or worse.
If you go around telling people what I just said, I'll put a bullet in your head. Understood?

options.content: I was just joking.

dialogues.content: Anyway, I find you quite... different.
I thought as a Hyperborean officer, you would have some... belief in the Empire. Like, talk about honour, loyalty, stuff like that...
Pfft, that kind of crap might work on the noobs.
Many would sacrifice everything for those invisible and untouchable things like sense of faith, but I am not one of them. I know exactly why I became a Phoxhunter and why I joined the Legion.
...I just needed a job that brings food to the table. I got that figured out from the start. The Legion needs my skills and I need their paycheck. Simple exchange.
All that talk of "glory" and "faith" — it's not why I'm here.

options.content: Um... Again, zap-zap warning~

dialogues.content: D**n it! I knew I shouldn't have had this drink. Can't keep my mouth shut when I'm a bit tipsy.
I'm done here! And don't you dare let today's conversation out!

name: Zap? Zap!
desc: There's something almost magical about high voltage — it dares you to flirt with danger and uncover its risky secrets.
memoryDesc: What's shared over drinks stays at the bar — an unspoken rule of any good drinking session.

dialogues.content: ...Hit me with another.
Hey, how do you usually pick up your gigs? Still at The Asphodel?

options.content: Yep, at Ms Camilla's tavern.

dialogues.content: Hmm, just like old times. The Asphodel is a neat place... At least Camilla doesn't suddenly throw in jobs where you have to kill people and rob their stuff.

options.content: You mean there are commissions that involve killing and robbing people!?

dialogues.content: Hah, never underestimate Icelake. It's teeming with tougher nuts than the capital, especially with the Security Bureau ignoring the outskirts. But don't worry — Camilla's gigs are clean, unless you're dabbling in the sketchy ones.
Speaking of which, how is Camilla these days? Still got that edge?

options.content: Nah, she's a very kind lady now.
Yes, still being fierce and sharp-tongued.

dialogues.content: That's good to hear! Ugh, time flies, even turned Camilla sweet, but it still couldn't soften up my iron-fisted supreme officer.

options.content: ...Who's your supreme officer?

dialogues.content: Okay, so Camilla hasn't changed at all... Ugh, she's just like my supreme officer — pretty but goes around acting like a pissed volcano.

options.content: ...Who's your supreme officer?

dialogues.content: Her name is... Sorry, can't tell you. I'd rather not end up on the electric fence getting zapped to ashes.
She's always got this long face like the entire Legion owes her money or something.

options.content: You give me the same vibes...

dialogues.content: Ugh, and her quirks! Like, who doesn't use a gun these days? But she insists on using her electrified whip and claims it works better.
(Your heart skipped a beat. Her descriptions reminded you of someone you're looking for — Sibylle.)
And people usually prefer peace and quiet when they have something to think about, right? Not her — she always blasts a loud recording and says it pumps her up and helps her think better.
She even keeps crows in her office. Hasn't she ever worried about bird droppings on her reports to His M—um, her higher-ups?

And then there's this: normal people go to the riverside to unwind and enjoy the breeze and scenery, right? My boss? She goes there only to watch anglers come back empty-handed, says it's funny and stress-relieving.
I mean — who does that!?

options.content: ...Your superior officer sounds like an interesting person. Can you tell me more about her?

dialogues.content: She's nuts. Trust me, she's far less interesting in person. Oh, and that's just the top boss. My direct superior? Even nuttier.
Now this dude rambles in circles and thinks he's all classy. Honestly? He sounds like a wishy-washy wet goose.
That guy's always babbling about efficiency and energy saving. Ugh, everyone knows that he's just making excuses for his laziness.
But I'll give him this — he's sharp. Slacks off, sure, but somehow still manages to get the job done. No one can really fault him for that.
Not long ago, he cracked the location of treasure with just a few clues. That's something my supreme officer had been chasing for years. But, well, there was... a little hiccup.
(If I guessed correctly, the "treasure" that Lynn mentioned could very well be Berry.)

options.content: Keep going. Did they finally find the treasure? Where is it now?

dialogues.content: Don't ask me... The two of them handled that mission together. It's all top secret — how would I know?
Crap. I really said a load of stuff I shouldn't be saying at all... It must be this lousy booze! You didn't spike it with a truth serum or something, did you?
Sheesh. I'm outta here. Ugh — thank goodness I don't drink in Dismania, or I'd end up zapped by my superior's whip... Argh, better stop talking now...
Assessing your drink mixing skills? You got the wrong person. I know nothing about this.
All drinks are the same to me — If it tastes right, I'll drink it. When it comes to these bottles and flasks sounds, they are just noise to me.

options.content: Seems like the Legion has better food and drinks.

dialogues.content: The Legion's built for war, not picnics.
Wait, you mentioned the "Legion"...
...What do you want? What are you planning? Who are you? Who sent you? What intel are you after? Spill it.

options.content: I heard the Legion got a treasure called "No. 0".
You're overthinking it. I just want to offer you a drink.

dialogues.content: You're too well-informed for a mere Phoxhunter.
…I should've known. No one offers gifts without wanting something in return.
Guess I was too on edge. Ahem, sorry about that.
Time to take you to the Legion for questioning. Cooperate, and don't make me tie you up — it won't look good for either of us.
It's just there have been some audacious Phoxhunters who, seeing that I was one of them, tried to get close to me and fish for the secrets of the legion.
