options.content: So you were a Phoxhunter before?
So you're originally from Icelake?

dialogues.content: (The following quickly flashes through your mind: Lynn takes out her gun immediately, and the dark muzzle is pointed straight at your forehead.)
Yeah, that was years ago. Wait, should I reveal this to others?
(This outcome is predictable. You shook your head and dismissed the risky idea to keep fishing out intel from her.)
...Never mind. The Legion doesn't say we have to hide who we were.

options.content: You seem to be so careful of what you say.

dialogues.content: You've got it wrong. I just saw you and thought I'd invite you for a drink.
Ugh, you have no idea what it's like in the Legion.
Legion camps are surrounded by electric fences powered by Phoxichor. They crackle with sparks, detering deserters, as well as discouraging thieves and spies.
But at least you can see those fences. It's the invisible ones you have to worry about — if you slip up, say the wrong thing, one zap, and you're gone.
My supreme officer has something personal against traitors. I don't want to end up dead over some accidental leak.

options.content: The Legion must have made you feel repressed.
I wouldn't have guessed — you seem to thrive on the status and prestige it brings.

dialogues.content: You think? I never wanted to be in the Legion.
Status and prestige? Sure, if you think risking your neck daily is worth it.
...I was happier as a Phoxhunter. It wasn't an easy gig, but at least I was free.
Not all commissions were about cheating death. Sometimes you'd get to walk dogs or hunt deer. And after a big score, you could enjoy a pint at The Asphodel.
You can do it on your own. No need to explain to anyone about your plans or worry about dead weight.
Most importantly, you didn't have to deal with commanders who can't stop their yapping.

options.content: Is this something I can know?

dialogues.content: I thought bad-mouthing your superiors can be considered as something wrong. Wouldn't that get you zapped?
A...Absolutely! I'm no noble — those thick-skinned aristocrats can definitely survive a zap. But if my superiors heard this, they'd fry me, or worse.
If you go around telling people what I just said, I'll put a bullet in your head. Understood?

options.content: I was just joking.

dialogues.content: Anyway, I find you quite... different.
I thought as a Hyperborean officer, you would have some... belief in the Empire. Like, talk about honour, loyalty, stuff like that...
Pfft, that kind of crap might work on the noobs.
Many would sacrifice everything for those invisible and untouchable things like sense of faith, but I am not one of them. I know exactly why I became a Phoxhunter and why I joined the Legion.
...I just needed a job that brings food to the table. I got that figured out from the start. The Legion needs my skills and I need their paycheck. Simple exchange.
All that talk of "glory" and "faith" — it's not why I'm here.

options.content: Um... Again, zap-zap warning~

dialogues.content: D**n it! I knew I shouldn't have had this drink. Can't keep my mouth shut when I'm a bit tipsy.
I'm done here! And don't you dare let today's conversation out!
And I trust you won't go blabbing about what I said.
I know exactly why you chose that extra-strong drink. You had your own reasons for coaxing intel from me — but I chose to act the fool and play along.
Let's stop here. Don't push any further. I can't cross the Legion — everyone's gotta live, right?
And I don't want to... lose someone that I can actually talk to.
Alright, that's it. I'm off!

name: The Forever Lost Hometown
desc: More sorrowful than losing one's home is seeing it intact but forever out of reach.
memoryDesc: Icelake may be small — a tiny speck on the Empire's map; yet Icelake is vast — memories of it linger no matter how far one travels.

dialogues.content: Hey, do me a favor. I'll pay you.
I'm off to the capital tomorrow and I've got a package here that needs to be delivered to No. 48, Oak Street in the west suburbs. It's for a lady named Riola Baker.

options.content: What's in the package?

dialogues.content: You're asking too many questions.

options.content: I need to know if there are any hazardous materials.
I don't want to end up delivering something illegal and get zapped for it.

dialogues.content: Fair point. Alright, I'll spill it. There's a gun and a mask in there.
Don't be nervous. It's just a toy gun. If you don't believe me, feel free to test it on me.

options.content: Try it out!

dialogues.content: (BANG—)
Ow! Fake bullets hurt too! And why aim at the head!? Get over here, I'm gonna give you a thrashing! D**n, that friggin' hurt.

*sigh* You know what, this reminds me of the fights I used to have with Riola when we were little. We'd use slingshots to hit each other in the head. Lucky I'm still alive, huh? Anyway, this gun... is my present for her.

options.content: This gun is... a present?

dialogues.content: Yeah, sort of... Had to come to Icelake for a mission, figured I might as well bring something.
And you've had way too many questions. Look, are you in or out? There's no shortage of Phoxhunters for the job, you know.

options.content: I can do the job. But if it's a gift for a friend, why don't you deliver it yourself?

dialogues.content: Deliver it myself? Forget it. If it weren't for orders from the top, I wouldn't bother coming back to Icelake.

options.content: Why is that?
What, gotten too used to the big city life to care about your humble hometown?

dialogues.content: Tsk, cut it out.

I did come back here before and had plans to catch up with the old gang. We used to climb trees and swipe veg together as kids. I wanted to chat with them, laugh about those silly pranks over a pint or two, and forget about life in the Legion for a while.
But word got out I was coming. They all lined up, saluted from a distance, yelling "Officer Lynn" so loud it scared the birds off the roofs.
I thought I'd let them do their thing. Get it out of their system. Then we'd all loosen up a bit reminiscing about tearing down the streets as kids.
But the old gang never gave me the chance. Everyone was too busy saluting, bowing like they owed me something. Couldn't even look me in the eye.

options.content: Do you think this is normal?

dialogues.content: Of course it's normal. I've seen my fair share of things to know why they're so afraid of me. If it weren't for my joining the Legion, I'd be the one who trembles at the sight of soldiers.
Icelake... No, it's the same for the whole of Hyperborea — the strong and rich walk all over the weak and poor... This has always been the way since I was a little girl. Nothing's changed.
Anyway, do you know what the gun and mask are for?
When we were kids, Riola and I were obsessed with this comic about Leblanc, a rogue who'd steal from wicked rich folks and give to the poor. They called him the "Masked Hero."

We made masks from scrap cardboard and used slingshots as our guns. We'd climb the town walls of Icelake, shouting Leblanc's lines from the comics. Silly, I know, but we didn't feel a bit embarrassed.
Those were the days when we felt we could... well... eventually become heroes ourselves.
Years later, I spotted a beautifully crafted Leblanc mask and toy gun in a Dismania store. I couldn't resist, so I bought them.
Back then, I thought, "I might have turned into a Charon-killing baddie, but at least Riola could still be a hero..."
The last time I saw her in Icelake, she trembled like a scared goose and called me "Officer Lynn." That's when I knew, we'd both changed. There's no going back to the good old days.
...Ugh, my head's hurting. Hit me with another!
These are the reasons why I avoid being back at Icelake. I don't even want to meet my own siblings. Just seeing them from afar, knowing they're alive and well, that's enough for me.

options.content: Is your family afraid of you?

dialogues.content: No, quite the opposite. They write all the time, saying how much they miss me and wish I'd visit.
But what could I tell them? About the latest horrors I've seen at the Academy? Or how many Charon prisoners I took?
...Forget it. Everyone's got their own burdens. It's all so damn normal these days.

options.content: I don't think any of this feels normal.

dialogues.content: This should be a world where you can return home whenever you want... Perhaps our generation should try to make it one.
Only outsiders like you would think this is weird and believe this can change.

Perhaps you also believe a day will come when Charons and Solas can live together in peace, and that people won't be judged for their strange-looking horns and spines, and the weird magic in their veins.
That could happen.
Even if you can't stop the snow in Icelake, you can at least shovel it away and make snowmen out of it, right?

You can at least go to your friend and tell her you remember your childhood dreams, even if they're broken now. You should be able to knock on the door of your family home and tell your folks that you'll always miss them no matter who you've become. That part of you never changes.
...Hah. To be honest, I like your way of thinking, even if it's a bit naive for my taste. It's way better than the usual crap like "Oh, that's the way it is, nobody can change the world."
And your words actually made this Icelake breeze a bit warmer, I must say. Hmm... Pour me another.
Let's see how far you can take this dream of changing the world. I'm curious if a naive fool can actually make a difference, even a little.
And if you ever need help, and I'm free, just ask — as long as it's nothing against the Legion. But not today — I've just changed my mind about something and will be busy later.
I'm cancelling the commission. Now, gimme back my mask and gun.

name: A Maid's Multiple Roles
desc: A maid's duties cover every aspect of life — including a few that might involve a bit of... bloodshed.
memoryDesc: Beneath petals lie thorns, and beneath the hem of a maid's dress? Bullets.

dialogues.content: I must say, I envy you for having the leisure to throw a little tea party.
I've just completed a grueling assignment up north and feel like I'm falling apart. I'll probably need a full night and day of sleep to recover.

options.content: Ah, why don't you go take a rest now? Our little tea party can wait.
That's a slight exaggeration, isn't it?

dialogues.content: It's fine. I'm already seated — might as well have a drink with you before heading to bed.
Perhaps you can handle a commission for me next time.
Mm, maybe I should just reject further commissions from this client. The pay is good but hardly worth the danger.
She had me deliver a rather colourful letter to her violence-prone relatives back home, designed to make them see red.

I had to bolt the second I delivered the letter; otherwise, the phrase "shoot the messenger" might have become more than just metaphorical — I bet those savages have never been on the receiving end of the kind words used in that letter.
Then it was a whole night's trekking through the snow to dodge ambushes. Sure, I could easily handle them, but there's no extra pay for that...
Hmm? You look astonished. What's wrong?

options.content: Are you really just a maid?
That sounds extremely dangerous.

dialogues.content: Of course, at least for now.
Not really. I've been through worse.
Before I was Miss Flora's maid, I briefly held a different position where I acquired many of the skills I use today, whether necessary or not.
Like how to swiftly dismantle firearms, extract poison from plants, or knock someone out in three seconds without serious harm...
Well, you are my long-term client, so I'll just be upfront with you — I used to be an agent.
Some called us spies. But the title doesn't matter. Essentially, we were a nameless group, always cloaked in disguise and shadow.
You might brush past one on the street, thinking they're just an ordinary passerby, when in reality, they could be on their way to create chaos or deliver secret messages.

options.content: Sounds like a wondrous adventure.
Sounds like a tough job.

dialogues.content: I once romanticised it as well, but reality is another story.
Indeed, it may sound exciting, but it's actually packed with challenges and risks.
Most agents are stuck with their legion, forced to follow orders — some even involve killing their own family.
I couldn't stand all those rules and restrictions, so I figured out a way to break free.
The escape was another heart-stopping story. This drink's not enough for me to share it, though.
I should go to bed now. I'll need to prepare breakfast for Miss Flora tomorrow. It's been days since she had my dessert.
And as a thank-you for this drink, I'll save a piece of cake for you.
Good night, then.

name: The Art of Fashion
desc: First impressions matter, and nothing speaks more directly than what you wear. Fashion, after all, is a timeless art.
memoryDesc: Disguises aren't magic but an art form — capable of transforming not just your appearance, but also your state of mind.

dialogues.content: I've finally got some free time today. I'm all yours if you're up for a few more drinks.
And after we're done here, I'm going to hit the shops — I've got some extra silver coins to squander from all those commissions I took.

options.content: Can I come with?
You'd go shopping?

dialogues.content: Sure, I can help pick out something that suits you.
Like I'd breathe, have meals, and sleep.
Shopping is my way to unwind. It's thoughtless, gets me some fresh air, and I can wear what I like — a rare opportunity for me.
At work, I'm typically in my maid's uniform or a bulky trench coat filled with pockets for various mission-essential gadgets.
And to keep a low profile during a mission, I'd tie up my hair. You know, red hair tends to draw unnecessary attention.
But when I'm out shopping, I can let loose a bit and wear lighter-coloured clothes.
Light colours really complement my hair. Though when I'm out with Miss Flora, I still tend to wear a hat.
I always wear dark red shoes. You know, like a red velvet cake needs to be topped with red berries.
I'd also dab on some fragrances and wear exotic accessories from the Starweavers — they really lift my spirits.
With your light silver hair, you'd look more vibrant in bright colours too.

options.content: Is it really that transformative?
It does sound quite stylish.

dialogues.content: Hmm? I thought it was pretty straightforward.
Right? You should try it too.
Actually, my fascination with this started during my career as an agent. We had to master the art of disguise, looking completely unlike ourselves.
I started with the basics: playing a street flower girl, a heavy-jewelled lady, an elderly woman teetering in the breeze, and even a "prince" or "princess" at times.

options.content: A prince?

dialogues.content: Mm-hmm, it was quite convincing as long as I remained silent. There were even a few noble ladies who gave me their handkerchiefs — it was adorable.
Over time, I realised that disguising myself as someone else could also change my mood. Even a dress or a piece of jewellery can be a factor in brightening my day.
So, after that, I fell in love with shopping for new outfits.
Well, I've finished my drink. Let's go hit the shops. I'll help you put together an outfit as a thank-you.

name: Pruning the Plants
desc: Snip, snip. Trim the flowers, and with them, trim away the woes.
memoryDesc: Be grateful the scissors in the maid's hand target only withered flowers.

dialogues.content: Thanks for inviting me... Mm, thank you.
After this drink, I'm off to trim the flowers.

options.content: Sounds like you're in a good mood.
That sounds like a typical maid's chore.

dialogues.content: Quite the opposite, actually. I want to pick up the shears precisely because I'm not in the best spirits.
It's not about work, actually; it's more about stress relief.
When I feel the pressure mounting, I find snipping away at dying flowers quite cathartic — as if I'm trimming away my own gloom.
I hope you wouldn't find that strange. It's just my way of blowing off steam. After all, the assignments I take normally require much more than making conversations.
Back when I was an agent, some of my colleagues had... let's say, darker ways of unwinding.
An assassination that lasts only seconds might require a month of planning, a week of prep, and a whole day of agonising wait — and failure could mean a lifetime behind bars.
Considering that kind of pressure, randomly cutting several flowers seems quite mild, doesn't it?

options.content: So what's bothering you?
Care to share more about your former colleagues?

dialogues.content: Well, it's not really a bother.
It seems you're missing the point of this conversation, aren't you?
I was just thinking of... um, someone important.
She was a fellow agent, but she always thought I wasn't cut out for the job. So I made so much effort trying to prove to her that I was not only competent but exceptional.
In the end, it turned out she was right.
I couldn't put missions above all else like she could.
Yet, there's a part of me that's relieved that I didn't end up walking her path.
We lost touch when I left the Legion. Now that I'm settling in here, I find myself... wondering how she's doing.

options.content: Why not go visit her then?

dialogues.content: Huh? Well...
You're right. Instead of trimming flowers here, perhaps I should just go see her in person.

name: A Belated Farewell
desc: No matter how well you hide, "growing up" always finds a way to catch up with you.
memoryDesc: A cup of flower tea, a maid's solemn vow.

dialogues.content: You approached me as soon as I returned, inviting me for a drink. Please be honest with me — have you picked up some of my old agent tricks and been keeping tabs on me?

options.content: Huh? It's just a coincidence.
Well, with hair as bright as yours, it's hard not to notice you.

dialogues.content: I was only teasing you. You came over because you're curious if I've met that lady who's important to me, aren't you?
Truth be told, no. She was reassigned away from the capital for certain reasons, so I've only caught snippets about her from others.
She's in a small town in the south — nothing like the icy grip here, but a place where she can enjoy bright sunlight and some music often.
To be honest, I was relieved. Because I wasn't sure how I would face her... But knowing she's doing well gives me some peace of mind.
This means the last ties between me, the Legion, and my past life as an agent have finally been severed.

options.content: Sounds like you've resolved some inner conflicts.
Would you have any regrets?

dialogues.content: Yes, finally.
The old me would, but no, not anymore.
She's actually a close family member of mine. She was the reason that I joined the Legion, and the reason I decided to leave.
She never wanted me to stay in such a dangerous profession, but I was desperate to show her that I could handle it — maybe even share some of her burdens.
It was the irony of fate that she and I received conflicting missions — hers to eliminate Miss Flora, mine to protect her.
While I was hesitating, she didn't think twice about fulfilling her task — even considering me as a potential obstacle to be removed if necessary.
So I took Miss Flora and fled before her assassination attempt could commence. At that time, I didn't have the leisure to dwell on my days in the Legion or anything related to her.

It's only because things have settled down recently, and you've been there for me to unload these old stories, that this whole thing had become a thorn in my heart, which led to my recent discomposure.

options.content: Do you still hate her?
Do you still love her?

dialogues.content: To be honest, I don't know. I just feel a bit indignant, aggrieved, and wistful. For agents like us, love and hate are luxuries we can't afford.
What I knew for sure was that eventually, I had to confront a complete farewell with her, which was something I had been trying to run away from.
Now that it's finally happened, it doesn't feel so bad. I'm even relieved that it'll no longer haunt me.
I've got so much I want to do now — trim flowers, bake a cake, shop for new outfits, maybe even dance a little.
But what I want to do most at the moment is thank you for helping me truly move on.

options.content: Hm? Did you just say "thank you"?
Come again?

dialogues.content: Thank you — is it so strange to hear that from me? I mean it sincerely.
But I must also remind you: now that you know my past, it means that one day when the Legion comes after me and Miss Flora, you won't be able to stay out of it.
I hope you're not too scared. Do you feel like I've handed you a sugar-coated poison?
Please rest assured that, I, Hilda, the all-capable maid, will always ensure your safety.

name: The Little Toy Vendor
desc: Everything he says circles back to explosions — that's one explosive way to make a first impression.
memoryDesc: The names may differ, but every toy on this list promises a spectacular explosion.

dialogues.content: H—Hello...
P—Please allow me to introduce myself. I... I'm Yale, from Scarletriver... I run a little shop called Snap 'n' Spark...
We sell, um... little toys that explode... in a fun way! The kids in Scarletriver love them...
Here's a catalogue of our products. If anything catches your eye, just drop us a note. We do home delivery as well...
Er... I should get going. It's not safe to stay out too late...

options.content: You're leaving already?
(This kid is painfully shy...)

dialogues.content: O—Okay... I can stay a little longer...
You look upset... I—I'm sorry... Did I say something wrong? I didn't mean to...
Oh, for crying out loud — move over. Didn't you swear you wouldn't chicken out this time? That you'd pitch our toys to Icelake?
And now look at you! Ugh, looks like I'll have to bail you out again.
I—I'm sorry... It's just... {性别：he|she}'s a really famous Phoxhunter in Icelake... I got nervous...
Don't be a chicken. {性别：He|She}'s not gonna eat you alive. Just talk to {性别：him|her} like you talk to the kids at our shop.

options.content: Awoo! I'm gonna eat you alive!
I'm a Phoxhunter of the heartwarming type. No need to be afraid.

dialogues.content: H...heartwarming type...? I've never heard of that type before, but you're definitely not what I pictured — you know, huge, louder than a bomb...
That wasn't scary at all. You were just trying to help me relax, right? Thank you...
Anyway, let me introduce my friend. This is Oliver. He, um, lives in this bomb. An alchemist sealed him inside...
We run Snap 'n' Spark together: I serve customers, and he comes up with new products.
Let's be real — Yale freezes halfway through his pitch more often than not, so I end up handling the talking too, like today.
He already mentioned we sell explosive little toys. Last month's top three sellers were: Boom-Blimp, Whizpop Firework, and Kaboom-Spinner.

options.content: Uh... why are you telling me all this?
Sounds fun. Where can I buy some?

dialogues.content: Tsk, hear me out first — I haven't even gotten to the real boom yet!
Heh... so you're interested, huh? Well, those were just the warm-up. What we really want to show you is this—
Looks like an ordinary alarm clock, right? But just one of these — and boom, all your troubles go up in smoke. Introducing: the Starshatterer.
Word about you's even made it to Scarletriver. Bet an awesome Phoxhunter like you could use a little extra firepower.

If the name's too hard to remember, you can just call them Tot Poppers. That's what I call them... it helps throw off Empire soldiers... makes them think it's just some kid's toy, so they drop their guard.
And the little drawings on the casings — they're also from me... This way the bombs look a bit less scary...
Ugh. How many times do I have to say it? People who buy bombs just want a good BOOM, not some cutesy nonsense.
But I think the drawings make our products stand out. And when I was sketching them, you were the one shouting all those tips about how to make them even cuter...
I... I only did that so you wouldn't botch it, all right? If the logo's ugly, no one's gonna buy them — duh!
Ahem. Anyway — that's our big sales pitch. If you'd like to place an order, just send us a note.
But make sure you write Tot Poppers on your order, not Starshatterers. Otherwise... we'll both be in hot water.
Our shop address is on the catalogue. We'll be waiting for your order...

Yale and Oliver — the unforgettable duo from Scarletriver. If you ever have the chance, why not pick up a few of their creations? Those Kaboom Spinners and Whizpop Fireworks sound like an absolute blast...

name: Return of the Mysterious Shopkeeper
desc: An unexpected visit, a conflicted conversation.
memoryDesc: A potent energy drink that sweeps away the fatigue of weary travellers. With a clear mind, the heart may finally see what it truly wants.

dialogues.content: Hello...
Do you remember me? I'm Yale, from Snap 'n' Spark...

options.content: Of course. I remember you were shy around strangers.
Yeah. And I remember your partner, Oliver, too.

dialogues.content: Th—That was because we barely knew each other then. It's better now.
Mm... He's always been much better at talking than I am.
I came by myself today, though.
It's not that we had a fight or anything — Oliver and I get along just fine. Which... might be exactly why there are things I can't quite say to him.
So... I thought maybe... I could tell you instead. N—No pressure — I'm not here asking for advice. I... just need someone to listen. And... you seemed like a good listener.
I never told you this, but Snap 'n' Spark wasn't ours to begin with. It belonged to a very, very grumpy old man.
He yelled a lot... always bossing me around. I messed up a lot of things at first... But after a while, even through all the shouting... I started to pick up how to run the place.
Then one day he simply announced he was off somewhere far away — and left the place to me.
After that, it was just me. Without him there... I didn't really know how to make new toys anymore. So I just kept selling whatever stock he'd left behind...

options.content: He just walked away? That's pretty irresponsible.
It's impressive you managed to keep the place running by yourself.

dialogues.content: I... I didn't understand it either. It all happened so suddenly.
Thank you... I really did try my best to learn everything I could back then.
Anyway... a few months passed. More parents came in with their kids, business was finally picking up...
Then one day a boy about my age showed up. I thought he was just another customer, so I started recommending toys.
But he just looked at me and said, in this cold voice, that Snap 'n' Spark wasn't the old man's shop at all — that he had stolen it from him.
I didn't believe him at first. But then he marched straight to the workbench, picked up the tools like he'd been using them forever...
I tried to warn him that the materials were dangerous and not to mess with them — but before I could even finish, he had already put together a bomb. Faster than the old man ever could.
He looked at me — and, in this really harsh, accusing voice — said the old man was a thief... and that I was one too.
I didn't want to believe him. But the way he handled everything... it felt like... he really belonged there. Like he was the real owner all along.
So... now I...

options.content: You want to find out the truth, right?
You're thinking of giving him the shop?

dialogues.content: Yes. If what he said is true... maybe I should give Snap 'n' Spark back.
If he really was the owner... then I think I should.
The truth is, I'm scared. B—but... if he really is the true owner of Snap 'n' Spark... what am I supposed to do?
I've grown so attached to the place... I worked really hard — learning how to greet customers, recommend toys, get better at talking to other kids... Could he do all that too?
And if it was his shop all along... how could I ever make it up to him? I don't know why he left in the first place, but... it just feels wrong.
Imagine losing your own shop, then coming back to find a stranger behind the counter... I can't even picture how awful that must feel...

options.content: Why not talk to Oliver about it?

dialogues.content: I know exactly what he'd say: yell at me, call me an idiot, insist I'm the rightful owner now — tell me to focus on running it better instead of handing it over.
He'd definitely try to stop me... But I know — underneath it all, he's actually really kind.
But... that boy was a good person too. And I don't think good people should always get the short end of the stick. Someone ought to do right by him as well.
Thanks for the tea. I think I know what I need to do now. Really — thank you. I'll head back to Scarletriver.
Oh! And if you still want to order something from Snap 'n' Spark, just send a letter. The shop's staying open either way.
Yale hurries off — clearly, he's made up his mind to return Snap 'n' Spark to its rightful owner.

name: Fireworks and Shadows
desc: They may be sworn enemies, but also inseparable halves of the same whole.
memoryDesc: A drink with a powerful calming effect, perfect for soothing the nerves of those left waiting. Only through patient waiting does the heart learn what it truly wants.

dialogues.content: Yo.
Got a minute?

options.content: What's with you today, Yale?
You're not Yale.

dialogues.content: Tch. I'm not that idiot.
Duh. I'm done playing "say hello to my talking bomb."
Name's Oliver. Oliver Kuzka. Not some fantastic creature holed up inside a bomb.

You probably haven't heard the name. Doesn't matter. Just remember it. If you ever swing by Dismania, head fifteen kilometres out from the north gate. You'll find a ruined fortress. My signature work.
As for why I'm here... That depends. Tell me — what did Yale say to you last time he was here?

options.content: I don't know what this is, but you don't sound like you're asking for a favour.
Tell me where Yale is, then we can talk.

dialogues.content: Hah. Tougher than you look — I like that. You only play along when asked nicely, huh? Guess we're the same type.
Fair enough. I like straight talk.
The truth, then. But fair warning — it's a long story.
Like I said — I'm Oliver Kuzka, the real owner of this body. And the best damn bomb maker you'll ever meet.

Back then, I was barely more than a kid myself. Thought I could blow the whole Empire sky-high with my little toys. Never even stopped to think what'd happen if I got caught... or maybe I just figured it wouldn't happen.
So when the Legion finally bagged me, I had no clue what was coming.
They hauled me off to some Spathatoi lab and sat me in front of this kindly looking old man called Jones.
Spoke real gentle, that one — kept saying crime was just "a mental hiccup" curable with right medication. Rubbish.

They didn't starve me, not really. Fed me fine, even. But they did force drugs down my throat and ran endless "check-ups." The stuff didn't taste bad, but after every dose, my thoughts would slow to a crawl... and little by little, my memories started slipping away.
At first, I still had enough fire left to cuss that shady codger out — but the more meds I swallowed, the harder it was to remember the curse words.
Someone once said: a man who never swears is a man who's lost his voice.
And that was only the beginning. Slowly, I forgot how to walk straight, how to grip things — even how to breathe.

I knew there was something wrong with those drugs. But every time they poured something down my throat, I couldn't even remember how to spit it out. All I could do was sit there and watch my memories dissolve. I'd have preferred being blown to bits.
In the end, all that was left of me was a shadow — watching some puppet called "Oliver Kuzka" move in the mirror, without a clue who the hell he was anymore.
Until one day, that old bastard walked in, stared at my body, and said: "Your name is Yale."
So he's Yale... then who the hell am I?

options.content: Sorry... you've lost me.
Jones did something really terrible to you...

dialogues.content: Figures. Took me a while, too. Jones... he created a new alter ego inside my body.
Too right. He created a new alter ego inside my body — meant to overwrite the Charon criminal named Oliver Kuzka.
But I'll give it to him — without Yale, I'd have lost control of my body forever. No matter how hard I fought, I couldn't move a finger.
But my thoughts could get through to him. Every time I so much as thought "You're a knock-off," he'd flinch like a startled quail — eyes darting, shoulders hunched.
You can imagine how much I hated him back then. I spent every waking second hurling every insult I could still remember at him.
To him, I must have been just a crazy voice in his head.
He tried to shut me out, of course. But how could he? That body was mine.
Then that old bastard caught on. He asked Yale if he'd ever heard the name "Oliver."
Yale denied it. But Jones just kept staring into his eyes... like he could see me hiding behind them.
After that, Jones wheeled in a record player. Each time the needle dropped and the music started, I blacked out— like someone snuffing a candle.
I knew the record player and the music was his new trick to wipe me out, so Yale could take the body for good.

Caught in that endless loop of blackouts and brief flashes of waking, I figured I'd lose everything — memories, thoughts, even the last scraps of who I was. But then, one day, I heard Yale's voice, telling me he didn't want to listen to the music any more.
That's when it hit me: the "knock-off" I kept abusing... was a real person. So we made a deal. Put together a plan. And broke out of that old bastard's lab for good.
We made it to Scarletriver and opened a toy shop. He named it Snap 'n' Spark — stupid name, if you ask me — and we never spoke of the lab again.

Couple days ago, I blacked out again — that same old, familiar feeling. Figured he must've dosed himself to shut me down. No idea what he got up to while I was under, so I asked around. Turns out he'd taken a trip to Icelake.
Thing is, I know him better than anyone — timid, shy... but too kind and soft for his own good. Definitely not the type to pull a stunt behind my back — not unless something was eating at him.
So I took the meds myself, knocked him out, and came here. I need to know what he said behind my back.

options.content: He told me a story... about the owner of Snap 'n' Spark.

dialogues.content: (You recount Yale's tale about Snap 'n' Spark and the mysterious former shopkeeper, which, in fact, is a metaphor of his very body and its true owner.)
So... he drugged me, came here, and decided to give the body back to me!?
That... that idiot... that hopeless, soft-hearted wimp!

options.content: Sounds like you really have forgotten how to swear.
It seems you two are actually getting along now.

dialogues.content: ...Hilarious. What I need to do now is wait for him to wake up, so that we can sort all this out.
Maybe. Maybe not. Either way, I'm staying put till he wakes, and we'll sort it out.
Thanks, by the way, for hearing me out. When Yale wakes up... if he turns out to be too stubborn, I might need you to back me up.
Oliver sits restlessly, one leg bouncing non-stop. It looks like it'll be a while before Yale wakes up...

name: Eternal Light in the Black Box
desc: Trapped in darkness, the warmth they share is the only light that dispels the gloom.
memoryDesc: Filled with Kaboom Spinners, Whizpop Fireworks, and Starshatterers, this giant toy chest marks a brand-new chapter for Snap 'n' Spark.

dialogues.content: Where am I...?
So bright... and warm... Not like the place in my dreams— lights always on, yet freezing cold.
Ah... {nickname}, it's you. Am I in Icelake? How did I—?

options.content: Oliver brought you here.

dialogues.content: Oliver? You must be mistaken. Oliver's my friend, but he's a bomb. He can't exactly take me anywhere...
Seriously? The jig's up — I already told {性别：him|her} everything, you idiot.
Oliver... you're here too...
Yeah. Been here the whole time.

options.content: Are you two fighting over the body right now?
If you've got something to say, spit it out.

dialogues.content: Nuh-uh!
I'm good. He's the one choking on words.
Don't be stupid!
I'm sorry... for thinking of handing the body back to you again.
...Just waiting for someone to say sorry, that's all.
I have a confession to make — the moment I learned it was yours, I'd already decided to do that.
But Jones was still around back then, and I knew what he meant to do to you. So I had to get us both out of that place — into the real world.
I didn't even know what the world looked like. The only place I'd ever been was that room — lights always on, and the air smelling like disinfectant.
Jones used to tell me the outside world was dangerous. Full of vicious Charons. He said I was better off locked up where it was "safe." But the books I read told a different story.

One of them was particularly interesting — it said when water gets cold enough, it turns to ice. I'd never seen ice... But it said there was a place called Icelake, where the whole city was covered in ice and snow.
It also mentioned a place called Scarletriver, where the river outside the city would glow beautifully red at sunset.
The only "red" I'd ever seen was blood. I couldn't understand how red could ever look beautiful...
So I wished — selfishly — to see those colours first: the white of snow in Icelake, the red of dusk in Scarletriver. And then... I'd give this body back to you.
Now, I've seen them both. They're clear in my mind now, so...
Alright, enough.
Can't believe someone wearing my face could say soppy stuff like that. Maybe that old bastard really was a genius after all.
I get it. I don't like owing people either. When you asked Jones to remove that damn record player, I figured you'd already paid me back half a life.
Then we busted out together — call it even.
But now you're back in my debt. While you were out these last few days, I had to deal with a mob of screeching brats in Snap 'n' Spark.
They all came asking for you. I had to pretend to be you — kept my voice down, smiled like an idiot, played nice until they left.
And after that, I had to come all the way to Icelake, and dig through a pile of painful memories just to bring {nickname} up to speed.
That doesn't vanish just because you hand the body over.
Most importantly — you never once asked how I felt.
To me, Yale's not just some guy who owes me. He's the idiot who saved my life. He's my best friend. And Snap 'n' Spark belongs to him just as much as it does to me.
So quit apologising. If you mean it, help me run the shop properly. You'll have plenty of chances to make it up to me.
...You're right. If I vanished now, Snap 'n' Spark would have to close.
Besides... I've read about other places that sound beautiful. Honestly... I kinda want to see them too.
Fine by me. We'll go together. But promise me — don't go getting soft again, saying you wanna hand the body over after every pretty view.
I won't. I promise. Let's go home. The kids are waiting for us to reopen.
Oh, and thank you, {nickname}. When we get back, we'll send over a big crate of Tot Poppers — on the house!

options.content: Thanks. Come visit again sometime — both of you.

dialogues.content:
A seemingly endless day draws to a close. 
And what follows is not a night just as long — but the faint glimmer of dawn, rising at the edge of the sky.

name: An Uninvited Guest
desc: A haunted house, a guest with secrets, and an amateur bartender.
memoryDesc: "Take good care of this guest."

dialogues.content: A quiet place indeed.
I'll have a drink, please.

options.content: Uh... are you sure you're in the right place?
Sorry, this isn't a tavern. If you want a proper drink, I know a good one in town.

dialogues.content: Up north in Icelake, there's a house with a piano, an anvil, and an hourglass. The lodger there entertains friends with homemade drinks — and is always happy to befriend strangers who mean no harm.
The Asphodel, you mean. Camilla Scarlet's establishment. Actually, she's the one who sent me here.
"A place where you can drink in peace. Unbothered."
Her drinks could rival those of the finest taverns in the capital — it's no wonder the place is always packed. But today, I seek peace. A place where I can lower my guard.

options.content: ...Have you anything to prove Ms Scarlet sent you?

dialogues.content: That's what Camilla Scarlet of the Asphodel told me. Was she lying?

options.content: ...Have you anything to prove Ms Scarlet sent you?

dialogues.content: Is it the colour of my skin or the weapon in my hand that unsettles you? Relax. She gave me this. It's for you.
"Take good care of this guest. Payment will be ready at The Asphodel tomorrow."
*sigh* ...Believe me, I've no wish to turn you away. Offending someone of your standing would do me no good at all.
I came without escort and kept my route quiet. If you recognised me regardless — then at the very least, I deserve a drink.
From the southern borders brushing Elysium to the Vidofnir Mountains in the far north — your name is known everywhere.
And every tale about you mentions your flame-red skin.
Icelake may be fading, but it's still the North's largest city. And I, madam, have run this tavern long enough to know a legend when she walks in.
How troublesome. I'd hoped to draw no more than a few curious glances — yet even in a near-empty bar, I am recognised at once.
Ma'am, you must've spent so long among convicts you've forgotten how the real world works. A tavern with just one patron at this hour would've gone under long ago.

Look beyond the door. You'll see them — folks loitering outside, too scared to step in. I'm not the only one who recognised you. I would gladly serve you alone, but if word gets out that a dignitary from the capital commandeered my bar for herself... Well, I doubt even I could sweep those rumours away.
You're not wrong. I had no intention of drawing attention. I appreciate the warning — though I doubt you're being helpful out of sheer goodwill.
(Hellfire's sharp gaze sweeps over the mechanical gears built into the tavern's hall. It's clear she senses the elaborate secrets hidden just beyond.)
There's something hidden behind that panelling. Bold, hiding your secret right in plain sight. I rather admire that.
Or perhaps you have more influence here than I assumed — enough to have people guard your secret, whether by a fine drink... or by offering them a way to survive in this city.
Heh... you flatter me, ma'am. I'm just a humble tavern keeper who'd never dare fall behind on her taxes. As for secrets — well, who doesn't have one or two?

Besides, not every secret's dangerous. Sometimes, it's just something harmless — like an old family recipe for smoked ham. I haven't served it yet... only because I wasn't sure it would suit your palate.
Amusing. One of my lieutenants — an expert in "thorough searches" — used to crack jokes like that.
Relax, Ms Scarlet.
This is your ground, not a courtroom — and certainly not the Royal Military Prison. No one here's going to jab a truth serum into your neck and drag a confession out of you.
I came to Icelake on my own business, and you have your way of keeping things running. Let's not waste time trading riddles about "ham recipes."
With that settled, I'll step away before my presence drives off the rest of your patrons.
Perhaps you wonder why I bothered to remark upon your little secret.
It wasn't meant as a threat. Call it a professional reflex — I find it hard to ignore lies and secrets that sit under my nose.
Pity I won't be able to enjoy a drink at Icelake's finest tavern. Farewell.
A moment, if you please.
Yes?
Up north in Icelake, there's a house with a piano, an anvil, and an hourglass. The lodger there entertains friends with homemade drinks — and is always happy to befriend strangers who mean no harm.
If ever you find yourself in need of someone to talk to, {性别：he|she} would be a good listener. Take this note — with it, you won't be turned away.
My thanks. With such discernment, I daresay you're capable of far more than running a border-town tavern.
Reality rarely turns out the way we expect, does it? Much like how I never imagined the Warden of the Royal Military Prison would turn out to be such a courteous guest.
For reasons I would rather not share, I won't be introducing myself. Just think of me as a weary traveller, laden with troubles, seeking a drink strong enough to drown them for an hour.

name: Bitters
desc: A strong spirit distilled from concentrated botanical extracts. Despite the name, its flavour is far from purely bitter — it's layered, evolving, and surprisingly complex.
memoryDesc: You never imagined the stuff was actually drinkable.

options.content: Sorry to keep you waiting. The bottle was hidden a little too well. Give me a second to let it breathe.

dialogues.content: Take your time. I've the whole night free.
Judging by the state of things, I'd wager you've been living here for some time — yet you still seem oddly unfamiliar with where everything is.
Even if you're only a tenant, I'd advise giving the place a proper sweep when you have the chance. Best to know what's tucked into every corner.

options.content: Is that really necessary...?
Are you saying there's something wrong with the house?

dialogues.content: Call it professional advice. I've toured more homes than I care to count with a trusted partner. And in those so-called "sweet" homes—

A flowerpot of rare blooms might be hiding a shaped charge; a child's diary, tucked in a drawer, could mask a smuggler's contact book; a bottle of wine offered as a gift might carry enough poison to kill a dozen men...

options.content: Forgive me, ma'am — what exactly is your line of work?

dialogues.content: No need for alarm. Just passing on a little field wisdom. Places like this — cheap, let to out-of-towners — often have a past. You'd do well to stay vigilant.
Landlords are always quick to take your silver. As for what might have happened inside these walls before you arrived, and why the rent is such a bargain... that part's rarely on the lease.

options.content: I... I'll keep that in mind.
First thing tomorrow I'm giving the place a full sweep!

dialogues.content: Here's a free bit of advice: Pay close attention to everything around you — or danger will find you before you're ready.
Easier said than done, of course. I'm not exactly a model of vigilance myself.

My partner was always sharper than me at spotting the hidden threads. Sharp eyes, deft hands — she spotted every clue the moment we walked in: shaped charges, smuggling ledgers, poisoned wine, you name it.
Nothing ever escaped her eyes.
She was my right hand — not just metaphorically. These hands of mine... they can melt glass, set books ablaze. Makes it hard to inspect evidence without destroying it.
So out in the field, she was my second pair of hands.

options.content: "Was"? Is she... no longer with you?

dialogues.content: ...In a manner of speaking, yes.
We were inseparable once — covering each other in firefights, cracking cyphers through sleepless nights, chasing half-dead leads down blind alleys.
Once, she even risked her life to retrieve a vital piece of intel — lived to tell it, but lost all hearing in her left ear — just so I could put a criminal on the scaffold.
I thought we'd always be the closest of comrades. But change never sends a warning before it comes.

Against my better judgment... I'll share a secret with you. I've come to Icelake to take custody of a mole — a traitor who sided with The Forsakens. She's responsible for the deaths of many Imperial soldiers who should never have fallen — some of them had served beside me for years.
I intended to cinch the noose myself — and watch her repent for it...

options.content: She killed your partner?
Your partner is the mole?

dialogues.content: It would have been an honour if she'd died for the Empire. But no — she chose treason. The mole is no one else, but her.
Yes. She betrayed me.
Before you can respond, the mysterious guest has already poured herself a drink — and downs it in one gulp.
Haa... Stronger than I expected. Bitter, too — bitter enough to make the judgment I'll have to pass seem mild.

options.content: You're sitting here drinking instead of dealing with it...
You're hesitating, aren't you?

dialogues.content: ...No. My intent hasn't wavered. Not for a second. I just haven't yet decided what words to throw back at her sophistry when we meet again.

"Commander, I've had enough — of you, of this filthy job. You like crawling through the gutter, living without sunlight — that's your choice. But I won't. Humans seek the light. Maybe you really are a monster."
By the time I noticed, that argument had played on repeat. Perhaps this ending was written long ago, and I was just too blind — too trusting — to see it.
When I face her... should I condemn her? Or mourn her? As her friend, her partner, her superior... or her executioner?
I have one night left to decide.
Until then... pour me another.

name: Sugar
desc: Craving sweetness is instinctual — people are drawn, often unconsciously, to memories of joy and warmth, even if overindulgence may take its toll on the body.
memoryDesc: A thick, luscious syrup whose sweetness clings to the palate long after the last drop.

dialogues.content:
"My dear little snowball, 
Nothing fills my heart with greater pride than seeing how you have grown!
By His Majesty's grace,
I have long feared you rarely allow yourself true happiness.
My little snowball, you work so hard, day and night,
as though a single idle minute were a crime.
But as your mother, all I wish is for you to live — truly, fully, without regret.
Life is short, and we only get to live it once.
So be gentle with yourself, my baby.
It is no sin to laugh, to rest, to let go once in a while."

"Boss,
Thanks for another year of hard graft — and happy birthday.
Now, enough of the formalities.
I mean it — stop working yourself into the bone.
And someone has to say it — using work as a coping mechanism is not healthy at all.
We've known each other nearly ten years, 
and even someone as good at digging up leads as I am still hasn't figured it out:
What exactly are you always fretting about?
Remember — unless the sky is actually falling, you can ease off.
So stop overthinking and actually live a little, would you?
—You may not need a holiday, but I certainly do!"

"Dear Madam Warden,
Thank you for your years of loyal service to the Empire. Our deepest respect and warmest birthday wishes to you.
May you enjoy this day to the full,
and may the year ahead bring you even more happiness.

Enclosed are your annual meal stipend, overtime bonus, and a voucher for a full medical examination.
Kindly acknowledge receipt at your earliest convenience."

"Your Honour,
Do excuse the anonymity — think of me as a quiet admirer, watching from a respectful distance~
You may not remember me, but I have never forgotten the way you stood against those thugs...
You fight for your ideals, for others, and maybe even for someone insignificant like me. (Teehee)
You shine so brightly, like a raging flame — true to your name.
Happy birthday!
I want you to know you deserve every honour, reward, and best wish that has come your way.
So please, enjoy them with all the peace of mind in the world."
From that night onwards, I ceased struggling to hold onto reality.

options.content: It wasn't your fault.
It was a dream too sweet to resist...

dialogues.content: I lived a full lifetime within that dream. When it ended, I passed peacefully — surrounded by family, comrades, all those I held dear. There could have been no finer ending.
A life without betrayal, loss, grief, or regret.
Then I opened my eyes. The peaceful death dissolved. Reality roared back — smoke, ash, searing pain, and bewilderment.
I summoned what strength remained and lifted my arm.
A red, trembling hand, smeared with blood and soot. But she took it in both of hers, unflinching. I think... I wept.
The heat could have blistered her skin, yet she would not let go. I had thought she would have fled long before.
It was Rebecca.

options.content: She reached out to you.
She was manipulating you.

dialogues.content: She said: "They call us monsters. But even monsters deserve the right to dream — and to chase those dreams until they are real."
She said: "They call us monsters. But even monsters deserve the right to dream — and to chase those dreams until they are real."
I wouldn't want to refute her. Perhaps that was why... I let her walk free.
Now, I see how hollow those dreams were. But at the time, I was caught in that fleeting sense of kinship — and I made a mistake I cannot undo.
I bear a duty — one I cannot forsake. Were I to falter, others would suffer for it. So, just this once, I surrendered my own dream... and gave it to her instead.
Still, I will not soften it with excuses. I acknowledge the desire within me — so it will never command me again.
I will not plead for forgiveness. I committed a fault, and I will not repeat it. The next time we meet... she will pay for what she has done.
Since then, the scent of dewiolet steadies my mind when it threatens to stray.
Perhaps, in time, the dream will fade and I shall break free of the illusion woven by The Destined One. For now... I still need the calm it brings.
One last matter.
Here is a wanted poster for Rebecca. Should you learn anything of her whereabouts, report it immediately to the nearest Escort post.

options.content: She's despicable! She won't get away this time!
(That dream sounds blissful... if only I could borrow it for a night.)

dialogues.content: Another drink, please — and this time, with a little dewiolet honey.
Another.

options.content: You've had enough.
Leave some for me.

dialogues.content: Do not underestimate me. Most of the alcohol boils off before it can reach my blood. I have yet to meet a brewer whose spirits can fell me.

options.content: ...Perhaps think of something brighter instead. Even someone as stone-faced as you must have at least one good memory.

dialogues.content: The fee I paid could buy ten more bottles of this.

options.content: ...Perhaps think of something brighter instead. Even someone as stone-faced as you must have at least one good memory.

dialogues.content: Perhaps.
You gather every piece of confectionery in the house and set them out before her.

options.content: Pick one — the taste that best recalls your fondest memory. Call it a small comfort.

dialogues.content: This will do.

options.content: Dewiolet honey? I wouldn't have guessed... does it bring back happier days?

dialogues.content: Happier? Heh...

It recalls only a master perfumer — a criminal, through and through. She distilled dewiolet nectar into her signature fragrance, The Destined One: a scent so sweet it could lull the unwary into eternal sleep.

options.content: Did you catch her?

dialogues.content: Silver-tongued, serpentine, and sly — a charming liar who spoke endlessly of "romance" and "love." But do not mistake her for some love-struck fool. Trust her, and you would find yourself a cold corpse, with venom seeping through your skin.
"Rebecca the Perfumer" — infamous across Luca, yet no more than a ghost in the Empire's records.
No one knows why she fled her homeland, nor when she drifted into Dismania. She was simply... there, as if conjured from the mist.
Any threat to Imperial security must be excised — all the more so when it comes from a Daimon of uncommon strength. I traced her movements, inferred her purpose — and misjudged her.
I overestimated her ambition — and fatally underestimated the chaos she would unleash.

She was not there to raid the Imperial Bank, nor to assassinate the Emperor at some parade. Fortress blueprints, top-secret dispatches smuggled out by agents at risk to their lives — to her, they were little more than scrap paper for jotting down perfume recipes.
Rebecca the Perfumer had one ludicrously simple ambition — to find the perfect lover. And she would stop at nothing to realise it.
To the vermin and gutter-rats skulking in Dismania's underbelly, she was the perfect pawn — a foreign Daimon, mistress of poisons, and, best of all, a dreamy-eyed romantic.
Naturally, she was swept into their schemes. A handful of lecherous aristocrats fell by her hand, and when she had outlived her usefulness, they cast her aside and consigned her to prison.
It fell to me to oversee the investigation.
During interrogation I told her: under the Hyperborean Criminal Code, her offences warranted fifty years of imprisonment. But if she cooperated, I would petition for a ten-year reduction.

options.content: Did she agree to cooperate?

dialogues.content: She accepted before I could finish the terms.

options.content: I suppose she was desperate to walk free.
Forty or fifty years — is there much difference?

dialogues.content: Few convicts ever cooperated as she did. It was as if — rather than bargaining for her freedom — she was pursuing some private, twisted ambition — methodical, relentless, unflinching.
I assumed it was revenge against the puppeteers who used her. She denied it.
"A perfumer's nose is keen," she told me. "And on you... I catch the scent of a kindred soul."

options.content: Hmm... that sounds rather unsettling.
Sounds like you were targeted!

dialogues.content: You're perceptive. Indeed — once the investigation neared the heart of it, we were ambushed by the true orchestrator. I was gravely wounded — left helpless.
She did not flee, nor finish me. Instead she bound my wounds — then, when I refused to black out, she misted me with her signature scent: The Destined One.
The dewiolet fragrance instantly drew me into a dream without end.
Tell me — have you ever wondered how different your life might be, had a single "accident" never occurred?
In that dream... I never awakened as a red-skinned Daimon. My kin never revered me as a divine figure. My mother could still cup my cheek gently, without being scorched.
For the first time in years, I remembered how pale my hands once were.

I was just an ordinary Charon. No shattered horn. No scorched skin to sear anyone who came too close.
I slept in a bed, not on stone floors for fear of fire. I turned over papers — evidence, reports — without worrying they might blacken and crumble at my touch.

I bore my family's duty as a warden of the Empire, as all my forebears had. A life still spent in shadow, yes — but without the legacy passed on to me by the first of our line, I found myself... somehow less alone.
At first I saw the seams — that suspiciously gentle world was a sugared mirage. Some unseen hand had to be pulling its strings.
Yet the quiet days stretched on. One year. Then two. Three. Ten. Whatever malice lay hidden behind the curtain never emerged. The dream endured — endless, unbroken.
Yes. That kind of "happiness"... stretched on without end.

It was, in its way, a quieter brand of torment. Not all torture is wrought by iron and flame. There is another cruelty — having to tear oneself away from a peace one had longed for. And that cuts far deeper.
In the end, I began to forget the truth: the peace, the warmth, the ordinary life were only a dream — spun by a perfumer's cunning hand.
When did I first yield to the illusion? Perhaps it was at that birthday celebration... when I opened each card, one by one.
Yes — even now, I can still recall the words written inside every single one.

name: Liquor
desc: It burns down the throat like a blade — and only the drinker knows what it cuts open inside.
memoryDesc: A cheap spirit — some drank it to feel alive, others to dull the ache. Yet whenever their glasses were raised, the same words rang out: "The Unyielding — to those who never yield."

dialogues.content: Thanks for the drink.
I understand now what Camilla meant about you — you have a way of lowering people's guard. Patience, perception, empathy: admirable traits in a bartender.
If you ever open a tavern of your own... I might just become a regular.

options.content: Just how friends treat each other, that's all.

dialogues.content: Heh. Friends...
That reminds me. I can't afford to linger forever. Once I finish this glass, it's time I paid an old friend a visit.

options.content: Want to try something new? Camilla says this one's all the rage in the capital—

dialogues.content: No need. Let's keep it simple.
The Unyielding — harsh upon the tongue, like swallowing a blade, and burning like fire once it hits the stomach. Thinking on it now... it truly is the drink for snowfields and frozen earth.
I'll have it. One moment.
Hellfire chips ice from the eaves, dropping it into the glass without letting her fingers touch the rim. She slides it across, then gestures for you to fill it to the brim with The Unyielding.
The ice melts fast. She drains the glass in one go. Then another. And another.

options.content: Are you all right? I told you not to drink so fast!
Please don't puke on the floor!

dialogues.content: Relax. With the glass half-full of ice, how much liquor could it possibly hold?
What I regret is how swiftly the ice dissolves in my hands. I do my best to preserve it, but it always turns to vapour and slips away — just like the liquor itself.
I do not care for florid metaphors — yet melting ice and fading ideals... they are too alike for comfort.
It takes me back — before I awakened, when my horns were whole, and my most trusted comrade had yet to betray me. We had just graduated, brimming with hope and unseasoned ambition.
Back then, we celebrated with cheap spirits, our roaring toasts drowning out the clink of glasses.
Every face flushed the same red as mine while we repeated the oath from induction day, again and again:
"To fight for Hyperborea's justice. To burn for her light. To stand for her endurance."
"The Unyielding — to those who never yield."
Of all those comrades, only two remain: myself... and that friend of mine named Artin.
And soon enough, there will be only one.

options.content: If you could... would you let her walk free?

dialogues.content: I will not repeat the same mistake.
We were comrades once, then officer and subordinate — now judge and criminal. Perhaps we both changed. But I will keep the vow I swore at any cost.
Even if it means I'll have to walk that path alone.

options.content: Have you decided what you'll say to her?

dialogues.content: Nothing.
The comrade I honoured was that unyielding young woman. I have nothing to say to a criminal.
Hellfire drains the last of the melted ice-water.
Whether from the Alchemy Academy or the Imperial Military College, whether once an ally or a lifelong enemy — I will judge them without distinction.
Such is the duty of a warden of the Royal Prison. It is the only path left to me.

name: The Scavenger's Work
desc: A good mood can work wonders on your efficiency, and the key to staying cheerful is knowing when to take care of yourself.
memoryDesc: After a long day's work scavenging Kossak's mansion, you and Margie have gathered a trove of treasures. Hopefully, they're worth the sore arms.

dialogues.content: The pieces of furniture inside? I brought them from the Imperial capital of Dismania thirty years ago. The rarity of the materials and the craftsmanship are beyond your wildest dreams.
Um, are you sure you want me to handle these valuable items, sir? If you change your mind all of a sudden, there's no way for a scavenger like me to...
You've already asked multiple times, and my answer remains: yes, these pieces are yours to handle. My true treasures are my music scores, and they have been well secured where they belong.
Well then, just to double-check before we start: about this huge pile of sheets — I collected them from the study. They look like music scores too...
Just burn them.
They're nothing but useless drafts, rubbish. Give them to someone struggling to stay warm to burn.
How laughable — if they were important to me, before you waste my time with these stupid questions, don't you think I'd have properly saved them already?
The distant sound of a train whistle echoes, as if hurrying the eccentric musician on his journey back to Dismania.
It's time I left. See you never, Charon.

options.content: You okay?
(Pats Margie on the shoulder)

dialogues.content: Oh, it's you. Excuse me for a minute!
(Margie takes a deep breath and begins to murmur to herself under her breath, though you can still hear her, even more clearly.)
Life's a dump, full of junk. They can't move but I can run, to keep my life safe and sound...
Don't get pissed, the jerks would win. Save your strength, unclench your fist, go soak up the sun with a grin...
Whew — Go to your happy place. Go to your happy place...
All set... I'm all good now! Just some barking noise. After all these years in Icelake, I'm so used to it.

options.content: Barking? Right. So who was that doggie?

dialogues.content: Doggie? Where? I wanna pet it... Oh, you mean Mr Kossak.
Well, I heard he's a famous composer from Dismania. That "Julius Anthem" he wrote — don't know if I got the name right — impressed even the Emperor. Those soldiers sing it every year on National Day.
But for some reason, he was thrown out of the capital at the height of his fame. Ended up in Icelake, banging on that beat-up gong at Galea Theatre for thirty years.
But I heard he recently wrote some symphonic works called "The Glory of Hyperborea," and some big shots in the capital liked them enough to bring him back.

He turned to Camilla to deal with all the stuff he left behind, and Camilla passed the big job on to me. I thought it was a stroke of luck at first, but it turned out the client was quite the character. Tough break...

options.content: A stroke of luck? Why's that?

dialogues.content: Uh-huh. Normally I'm just hustling between rubbish bins trying to collect anything useful to resell.

It's not often you find a rich guy who leaves behind a houseful of stuff without a second thought. His leftover belongings are worth a fortune — okay, maybe not a hundred bins worth, but definitely fifty at least!

Take those antique furniture pieces — the wood is top quality. You could turn them into beds or tables. I also checked with the tailor — those curtains, tablecloths, and rugs can be made into clothes after a few washes.
A few more families in the slums will get to sleep and dress better, and I'll make a tiny fortune. Plus, even though that musician was quite mean, he was pretty generous with the pay, hehe...
Can you believe it? I was totally upset just a moment ago, but now I'm not mad at all!
Anyway, Kossak's off to Dismania, and the folks in the slums get some good supplies. It doesn't matter that I got a little scolding — once I start to get busy, I'll forget all about it!

options.content: Mind if I lend a hand?
Finders keepers. I'd like a share of the finds too.

dialogues.content: Oh, that would be great! It's a bit of a chore hauling out his cabinets on my own. Feel free to pick anything you like while we're at it.
Sure thing! Consider it a thank you for putting up with my grumble. Come on, help me out here. You can pick whatever catches your eye.
You spent a productive day with Margie... Though your arms were sore from all the lifting by bedtime...

name: The Musician's Secret
desc: Even discarded or forgotten items can find a new purpose.
memoryDesc: A composition written for the Charon community, long-forgotten in the dark. It wasn't until Margie spread its melody through Icelake that it found its true purpose again.

dialogues.content: Oh! {nickname}, it's you! Come here — I've just stumbled upon something strange!
Found this wooden plank while I was taking apart a cabinet. Now, listen to how it sounds when I tap it.

options.content: Sounds like it's hollow inside.
It's got a nice ring to it. Quality wood.

dialogues.content: Exactly! The sound isn't right. There's definitely something stashed inside.
Oh, yeah. Kossak bragged that all his furniture was made from some fancy wood, though I can't remember the name. But what I'm trying to tell you is — it's hollow!

My detective instincts are telling me this piece of wood must have a breathtaking backstory! Ever since I started treasure hunting around the city's rubbish bins, secrets keep finding their way to me, whether I want them or not.

Like, if there's broken glass in the bin, it usually means the household just had a fight. If it's a huge bunch of old clothes, then they must've come into cash all of a sudden. And don't get me started on those torn-up love letters I found...

Anyway, back to this hollow plank. It was too dark in the room, so I brought it out here. I was just about to crack it open when you showed up. There's got to be something interesting hidden inside. Let's see...
Later, according to Camilla, "Demons Broken Loose" is indeed a brilliant piece, and quite a challenging one.
It took Margie three full days to master the song, and even then, she had to transpose it down an octave. Before long, echoes of the melody began to drift through the streets of Icelake.
Seems like Margie has accomplished her mission of bringing forgotten treasures back into the light.

Margie has taken up a room at Sanctuary to sort through the items left behind by the famous musician Kossak. The constant clatters and clanking from the room suggest she's busy turning waste into treasure.
You decide to check on her...

name: Old Martin
desc: The bond between father and daughter goes beyond habits, profession, bloodline, and worldview — it also includes sharing the moniker "idiot."
memoryDesc: A thoughtful birthday gift from a doting father. This multifunctional helmet comes with its own little surprise.

dialogues.content: Hmm...
Bitter and sweet at the same time... Ugh, this tastes like something my stupid old man would love! As for me, I think I'll need another ten... no, make that twenty years to appreciate this taste.

options.content: Even with sugar, our Margie still can't stomach coffee.
You're more of a fan of cool, refreshing drinks or something sweet, huh?

dialogues.content: I just don't get this drink! Why would anyone want to torture themselves with this bitter taste?

options.content: Who is your "stupid old man"?

dialogues.content: Exactly! Nothing beats a refreshing drink after a day's work — it's like a cool wave from head to toe!

options.content: Who is your "stupid old man"?

dialogues.content: Oh, that's my dad! They call him Old Martin. Before I took over, he was the one managing all the rubbish bins in Icelake.
If it weren't for his stupid title "King of the Bins," I wouldn't be stuck with that tacky, lame nickname "Princess Rubbish Bin"... Ugh, it's all that flashy old man's fault!
I mean, I was hoping for something cooler, smarter, and more reliable...

options.content: Understood! Miss Reticent Detective it is!
Understood! The coolest, smartest, most reliable Princess Rubbish Bin!

dialogues.content: That's right! Hehe, you totally get me!
Aaaah! Stop it! I'll whack you with my shovel if you say that again!
Ugh... ever since that stupid old man dumped all the work on me, I barely see him around. No idea what he's been doing. He better not be causing trouble for me and Ms Camilla!

options.content: I've never heard you talk about your dad before.

dialogues.content: Uh, well... if it weren't for this bitter taste, I guess I haven't really thought about him in a while...

options.content: Sounds like you're no better than him on this!
Like father, like daughter, huh?

dialogues.content: Well, in my defence, I've been swamped with work! His work, to be precise!
Ahem... Well, you know, when little animals grow up, they leave the nest to fend for themselves. It's totally normal.

Besides, that stupid old man has been fussing over me for more than ten years. Especially after we left our old home for Icelake — we spent a whole year trekking across the snowfields, just the two of us, not another living soul in sight.
I've had enough of his tales, his songs, and his tricks to last me a lifetime. So... I guess that's why I don't really miss him that much... probably.

Plus, soon after we arrived in Icelake, he jumped right into "staking out territories," "recruiting the local henchmen," "figuring out the protection racket," "making alliances with local powers," and "becoming the top dog." He seemed to enjoy himself just fine on his own.

options.content: ...Wait, what did you just say!? Should I report this?

dialogues.content: Oh, it's actually just mapping out the rubbish bin locations, recruiting the sanitation workers, setting rules for rubbish collection, finding buyers through Ms Camilla, and becoming the "King of the Bins."

Ugh, that stupid old man loves spouting off fancy talk — he sounds like a flashy character from a drama script! Bad habits from his rough-and-tumble days back home, I guess. He can't seem to shake them off. Gah!

options.content: But since Martin brought you away from your old home, maybe he didn't like it there either.

dialogues.content: It's hard to say! The old man always liked to brag about his "glorious past" back home. Stuff like...

"A scavenger's every mission is a matter of personal honour and family interest. From daily planning to personal grooming, everything must be meticulously prepared. And your father, my dear, was the finest scavenger of all."
Ugh, his bad influence is why, when I first got to Icelake, I talked exactly like a "Mini-Martin." Ms Camilla said it was really annoying, and it took her forever to help me lose that tone...

options.content: Really? How did you talk back then? Can you give me a demo?

dialogues.content: No way! That's too embarrassing!

options.content: Please, Miss Reticent Detective, I'll trade you your favourite drink for it!
If you won't, I'll just have to play dirty — Princess Rubbish Bin, Your Highness—

dialogues.content: Fine, just this once, okay? No encores!
Aaaahhhh!!! Okay, okay! I'll do it! Just stop already!
Uh… When Old Martin dropped me off at Ms Camilla's tavern before he went off to do who-knows-what, I'd say...
"Remember your mission, Father. Our future hinges on your every move, so I trust you've washed your face, brushed your teeth, and made a thorough plan."

options.content: (Holding back a laugh.)

dialogues.content: And then Old Martin would tip his hat and say, "As you command, ma'am! Should either of us fail, we'll inscribe that person's name with the modifier "idiot" on The Asphodel's door for all to see."

options.content: (It's increasingly hard to hold it back!)

dialogues.content: And I'd reply, "Oh, considering we share a last name, better to inscribe it on the bottom of a pot instead — saves me the shame and allows the stove fire to scorch your disgrace!"

options.content: (Can't hold it back anymore!)

dialogues.content: Ahahahahahahaha!
Now I see why you ended up with the title "Princess Rubbish Bin" — it's not all Old Martin's fault!
I don't care! It's totally his fault! Just thinking I almost turned into a pompous blowhard like him gives me the chills.
And I don't know if you figured this out — the stupid old man clearly misses and takes pride in his past. I don't think he left home just because he hated the chaos there.
But what could have happened that made him leave home and drag me across the snowfields?
He's definitely hiding something huge from me! But every time I ask, all he says is, "I won't tell you. If you do want to know, use your head and figure it out yourself."
So last year, I secretly investigated him for months. But the old man's so crafty and sneaky, he even hid the stuff he brought from our hometown. I couldn't find it no matter what.
After months of digging, I came up empty. And to top it off, he had the nerve to mock me—

options.content: Mock you? How?

dialogues.content: One day, out of nowhere, the old man actually showed up. He spent the whole day with me, and even forgot to take his suitcase with him when he left — the one he brought from our hometown!
I thought, "Ha! That old man slipped up at last!" So I opened the suitcase, and inside... was just a pot.
(Margie angrily taps on the pot she's wearing on her head, producing a hollow sound.)
This thing right here! And he left a note in the suitcase...
"Dear Miss Margie, I knew you'd snoop in this suitcase, so I've relocated the secret to a place you'd least expect."

"To make up for your disappointment, I've left you this — an all-purpose pot helmet! Worn normally, it protects your head; flip it over, and it's a perfect cooking pot. The attached lamp even works as a flashlight. Truly, the ultimate all-in-one tool."
"By the way, happy birthday. — Martin."

options.content: A pot helmet... Old Martin sure has a unique sense of style.
So it was a birthday gift... Looks like Old Martin really cares about you.

dialogues.content: ...I'm pretty sure he was mocking me!
Anyway, after that, I gave up caring about his stupid secret.
Speaking of secrets, I've got a hunch...
What is it?
Could his secret be hidden... inside this "all-purpose helmet"?
I mean, he did say it was at a place you'd least expect, so... maybe the most obvious place is the place you'd never expect.

Ah...!!! Come to think of it, I was so bummed back then I didn't even check this helmet carefully! You might be right — it's been modified, so it's possible that he had hidden something inside! Let's take it apart now!
Aha! A hidden compartment under the padding! I knew you had a detective's knack!
Gotcha, stupid old man! The jig's up!
(Margie skillfully manipulates the pot helmet — her experience with repurposing scrap obviously helps a lot. Her fingers move deftly, and soon the pot is fully disassembled.)
Ah, this is...
(Margie stares wide-eyed at the pot, speechless. You take the pot from her and see a small inscription on the bottom—)
"Dear Margie, my silly daughter,"
"Congratulations on failing yet again in the 'Find Old Martin's Secret' game. As punishment, I shall add the modifier 'Idiot' to your name."
"Considering we share a last name, I hereby inscribe it on the bottom of this pot instead, which saves me the shame, and allows the stove fire to scorch your disgrace."

name: Plumpytail and Margie
desc: Paths diverge between a human and a cat. Perhaps it's best to embrace farewells with a smile and look forward to a reunion.
memoryDesc: This grey furball, speckled with black spots, recalls the sight of a proud cat with a lush tail strutting across the snowfields.

dialogues.content: *sniffles* ...Detective Margie has cracked yet another groundbreaking case...

options.content: What's with the tears? Isn't that a good thing?

dialogues.content: Th—These are tears of joy!

options.content: Here, have some water. I'm here whenever you're ready to talk.

dialogues.content: (Margie gulps down a full glass of water, then gingerly pulls something from her pocket and presents it to you — it's a clump of fur, somewhat familiar in colour.)
I found Plumpytail!

options.content: Plumpytail? What's that?

dialogues.content: Plumpytail's the little cat I used to roam the snowfields with!
Then I came to Icelake, but she didn't want to come with me and stayed in the wilderness. I made a plushie that looks just like her to remember her!
I was just going to check the bins near the city gates today, but instead, I stumbled upon this clump of fur! Look!
The greyish colour with black spots, the soft yet coarse feel, and the fact that it was even a bit damp when I found it... It's definitely Plumpytail! She came back for me!
