Back in the day, when Plumpytail and I played "Tailing the Suspect," she would leave bits of furball from her grooming in different directions to throw me off. That was one of her signature tricks.

I was such a rookie detective back then, so I always walked straight into Plumpytail's traps. By the time I was worn out from running in circles, Plumpytail would prance around with her head held high, tail swaying like she was king of the world!

...It's all coming back to me — the irritation of being toyed with by the "Suspect Cat," the frustration of losing the trail, the panic of getting lost in the snowfields, and the bafflement of holding a handful of wet fur!

options.content: Aww, poor detective, completely at the mercy of Plumpytail!

dialogues.content: Hmph! Those days are long behind me! I'm no longer the rookie I once was! Plus, Icelake is my turf now, and this time, I'm definitely going to catch the "Suspect Cat"!

I've been mapping out the possible hiding spots based on the alley layouts and even bribed the local strays with fish treats. Anyone who can provide a lead on this outsider cat will be handsomely rewarded!

options.content: Meow meow! Miss Detective, I've got a major lead!
Not only do you know the bins' locations like the back of your hand, but you've even set up a kitten intel network. Bravo, Miss Reticent Detective of Icelake!

dialogues.content: Aha! Caught a white-furred big cat spreading false alarms! As punishment, no fish treats for half a month!
Hehe, even if you flatter me like that... hehe, I won't let it go to my head, hehe!
Ahem, as I was saying... my detailed deductions finally led me to a narrow alley full of cardboard boxes — it's like an irresistible paradise for a cat used to living in the wild!
And sure enough, there was the suspect, basking in the sun inside a cardboard box, casually flicking her tail at me as if she owned the place!
It's been so long, yet Plumpytail was still the same Plumpytail I knew... No, actually, she seemed a bit different this time.
When we last parted, Plumpytail had just grown up and didn't like being petted — one wrong move, and she'd vanish in a flash. But today, she seemed more mature, almost like an old cat.
Does "mellow with age" also apply to animals? Even without her favourite jerky, she let me pet her all over — belly rubs, paw squeezes, tail strokes and all.

This time, Plumpytail even brought a few kittens along. They're just as timid as Plumpytail used to be, peeking their little heads out from the box. But just from their fur, I could tell Plumpytail has been taking great care of them!
It's amazing... that clumsy cat who couldn't even catch a snowfield rat is now providing for a whole litter of kittens of her own!

options.content: You've also grown and no longer needed Old Martin's care, just like Plumpytail, looking after those in need.

dialogues.content: You're right... we've both grown since we first met. Hehe... it's kinda embarrassing to admit though...
Actually, when I first came to Icelake, I was such a crybaby — hey, don't you dare make fun of me!
I thought about leaving Icelake more than once. I figured I could just pretend I'd never come and wander the world with Plumpytail, which seemed pretty great.

options.content: What made you feel that way?

dialogues.content: Old Martin always said the city was a good place, so I believed it too. I imagined a "city" as a sanctuary where torch-bearing folks huddle together for warmth and protection.

But... Ugh! The things that go on in this "sanctuary" are just absurd. Charons are discriminated against for no reason; rich folks have more furs than they could wear in a lifetime, while the poor in the slums might not even survive the cold winter...
And I just missed Plumpytail so much! I figured, every place has its good and bad, so why not just stick with my favourite cat?

options.content: You chose Plumpytail over Old Martin? He'd cry if he knew.
But given how young you were, the snowfields wouldn't have been safe for you.

dialogues.content: Huh? He wouldn't... um, maybe... Anyway, I'm still here in Icelake, aren't I?
Yeah, now that I think about it, I was just a kid trying to run away from problems.
I actually did it once. One time, some Sola kids threw rocks at me, and I got so mad that I ran straight for the city gate. I just kept running, calling out for Plumpytail.
And then... I did run into Plumpytail. She was fighting a snow wolf over a silverback vole.
I figured Plumpytail must've been starving, so I threw her a piece of jerky. But she didn't even look at it. Her eyes were fixed only on her prey and her enemy.
In the end, Plumpytail won. She strutted over to me all proud-like, meowing — either showing off or maybe just happy to see me after so long.
I petted her fluffy head and said, "Plumpytail, I'll go with you. Let's live together in the snowfields."
But Plumpytail didn't take me to her home. She darted out of my arms and kept meowing in one direction — it was the direction of Icelake.
I guess she was trying to tell me the snowfields weren't my home, and I belonged to Icelake.
That's when I realised... Even with me feeding her, Plumpytail would still try her best to hunt, because that was her way of living.
And I had my way of living too, but I was too chicken to face my life in the city, always thinking of running back to Plumpytail — ugh, I was such a coward!

options.content: Plumpytail is really smart.
Kitty looked out for you, good kitty. Margie made kitty worried, bad Margie.

dialogues.content: Yeah. So I listened to her advice and went back. But there was a slight mishap...

Waaah, I know I messed up... I'm sorry! Not even Old Martin scolded me for that! Speaking of which, the old man was actually worried sick for once, because I ran into a little trouble on the way back...

I was so mad when I ran out that I didn't even pay attention to remembering the way! So after I said goodbye to Plumpytail, I got lost... And I just kept walking, feeling more and more tired, until I fell asleep in the snow...
I woke up to a bumpy ride — turned out that stupid old man was carrying me on his back. He's not tall, but his back is as sturdy as it was when I was little.
I felt very warm because he had bundled me up in a long scarf, wrapping me in layer after layer, covering even my mouth, like Solas do.
And that's how Margie's first adventure outside Icelake sloppily ended.
Since then, I've been learning how to make a life for myself in Icelake. But every time I run into trouble, that stupid old man still teases me, calling me "Can't-catch-anything Plumpytail Junior."
But he's wrong! Plumpytail had already become a skilled hunter, and I've learned to survive here too — just like you said, we've both grown.

options.content: Right, grown into an older crybaby who came to me all tearful today.

dialogues.content: Well, it's all Plumpytail's fault! Why did she have to leave so soon!? I must've begged her to stay a thousand times in my head, yet she still left before the sun even set...
...Alright, no more excuses! Next time Plumpytail and I meet again, I'll see her off with a smile!

name: The Meaning of Work
desc: She keeps reminding herself: turning a blind eye is the cruellest thing of all — so she must act, even if only in small ways.
memoryDesc: The "Daily Duties" column is always crammed with trifles, sometimes spilling onto a second page. Such was Rhythm's life in the Escort.

dialogues.content: (Rhythm appears to have arrived early.)
(You notice she's uncharacteristically taken off her gloves and is checking her reflection in the window, adjusting her hair.)

options.content: Surprise!
Rhythm, what are you doing?

dialogues.content: Ah!?
Oh, it's you... It was really windy on my way here, and my hair got all messy, so I thought I'd tidy up a bit.
(Your sudden appearance catches Rhythm off guard. It all happens so quickly — there's a flash of bright light, and you feel a strange twitch in your body.)
Wait a second, let me put my gloves back on — I'd hate to hurt you by accident.
{nickname}?! Are you alright?
Sorry I'm late.
I—I—I'm fine... just... felt an... e—e—electric...shock...
No, it's fine... I actually came too early.
Sorry, I failed to control my powers properly...

And thank you for having me here. After serving in the Escort for so long, I've become accustomed to a strict routine — getting up, patrolling, meals... But now that I've left the Legion, without that fixed schedule, I'm not quite sure what to do with myself anymore.
You must have never been late, right?
In the Escort, tardiness would get you written up... Plus, back then, I always thought that the earlier I arrived, the more I could accomplish compared to others.

In the Escort, we were responsible for pretty much everything in the city — patrols, dealing with Filthoids, resolving disputes, clearing out the sewers... Sometimes, we'd even assist with confidential tasks for the higher-ups in the Legion.

options.content: That sounds exhausting...
You've done so much for Icelake!

dialogues.content: I suppose so... At first, I took the job hoping that, as I worked my way towards the title of Laurelled Charon, I could also do something to help my fellow Charons.
But once I started, I realised that the situation many Charons face is far worse than I had imagined...
Some of them work themselves to the bone in back-alley shops run by Solas, taking menial jobs without proper contracts, just to save up for a travel permit to stay in Icelake.

However, before they could scrape together enough money for a travel permit, it only took one complaint letter for a Charon to be thrown in jail, while the shop owners would get away with not paying them.

Every time I came across these cases, all I could do was reprimand the unscrupulous shopkeepers and try my best to help those Charons clear their names. Most of the time, I couldn't even recover their wages.
In retrospect, I feel like I haven't really done anything useful. The best I did was go to work early every day and make sure my subordinates weren't rough with Charon citizens during their shifts.

It's ironic, isn't it? I spent so much time trying to fit in with the Legion, thinking I could make a difference. But in the end, I realised I couldn't change anything... and instead, the Legion changed me.
I still remember a few months ago, a young Charon man was shot dead in the street by one of the soldiers... I couldn't even get justice for him.

I tried to argue with my superiors about the soldier's punishment, but all I got was a warning to "mind my own business"... I knew right then that there was no point in pushing further, and the case was swept under the rug just like that.
In the end, all I could do was help bury the young man properly and leave some money for his father to live on... As for the source of the tragedy, I was completely powerless to do anything about it.

options.content: ...Actually, I was there when that happened.
You did the best you could with what you had.

dialogues.content: Huh?
Compared to other Legion members who turned a blind eye, you did more than most.
But I just stood by... totally in shock.

At least you still care. You saw injustice, you felt indignation, and you tried to make a difference. And now, your decision to leave the Legion shows that you haven't let them change you — you refused to become one of them.
...Thank you.
I thought I was the only one carrying this burden. Everyone else either became the Legion's accomplices or convinced themselves to follow orders blindly, never questioning anything.
Although... I guess, serving in the Legion, they had no other choice. After all, even a Laurelled Charon can end up in jail because of a complaint letter, just like those without a travel permit.

But... you're right. I don't have to worry about turning into one of them anymore. I'm free to be myself again. Though I still feel a bit lost without an official schedule, it's so much better than living by their rules.
Next time we meet, I won't come too early.

name: The Meaning of Moving Forward
desc: Sometimes, to see the road ahead — and go farther — you must stop and catch your breath.
memoryDesc: A tidy scrapbook filled with newspaper clippings — cleaner, kitchen hand, scribe, fisher, bartender, mason... and even an animal trainer?

dialogues.content: (This time, Rhythm arrives on time.)
(She's staring at the corner of the room, seemingly lost in thought.)

options.content: Surprise!
Hello, Rhythm.

dialogues.content: ...Please, don't spook me like that again. If I lose control of my powers, you might get hurt.
Ah, you came.
Too bad. I kinda miss that shock.
I just inspected your place again and noticed some cobwebs and hairballs hidden in the corners. I went ahead and cleaned them up for you.

options.content: You didn't have to do that...
Wow, thank you. I should pay you for the cleaning.

dialogues.content: I... don't really understand this quirk of yours.
It's fine. Once I start something, I like to follow through.
No... please don't. I just wanted to help, that's all.
What were you doing just now?
You're still as diligent as ever.
Diligent, huh... Maybe. It's become a habit. You know, I'm not really gifted at anything, so I've always had to make up for it with hard work.

options.content: Why do you push yourself so hard?
It's okay to take it easy sometimes.

dialogues.content: My former superiors used to say the Legion was the fairest place in the Empire, because "meritorious service never goes unnoticed, and hard work is always rewarded." As long as you're willing to put in the effort, even a Charon can earn recognition.
So I kept pushing myself, chasing the dream of becoming a "Laurelled Charon," but in the end, I realised the path I was on was taking me further away from what I truly wanted.
I can only comfort myself by thinking that, luckily, my lack of talent has kept me from going too far.
Were I more sophisticated, more tactful, I probably would have climbed higher. But then, I'd have lost track of who I truly am and eventually rotted from the inside.

options.content: No, I believe you'd stop before it was too late.
That's what sets you apart from the others.

dialogues.content: If you had to choose between helping others and climbing the ladder, you'd always choose the former.
You're gifted in your own way: you're capable of sticking to your principles better than anyone else.
Mmm... Thank you for your kind words...
(Rhythm looks at you as if she wants to say something but hesitates.)

options.content: If you have something on your mind, it's better to let it out. Now that you've left the Legion, there's no reason to hold back anymore.

dialogues.content: To be honest, I still haven't figured out what I'm supposed to be doing.
I've been doing odd jobs, but deep down, I know they're just work, not a real life purpose.
As for what my new purpose is... I still haven't found it. More accurately, I realised I'd been waiting for someone else to give me that purpose.
I took in all the doctrines the Legion taught me, swallowing them whole, because I needed something to hold onto. But once they were gone, my life suddenly felt empty and meaningless.
I don't know what to do anymore...

options.content: Then why not come work for me?
Then keep doing odd jobs for now. Things will work themselves out.

dialogues.content: Huh?
What do you mean?
I'm serious. The Noctoyagers could really use someone as calm and reliable as you.
Even if it's odd jobs, you'll give your best. So why not try different jobs for now? You'll surely find what you truly want to do someday.
In the meantime, you could help the Charon community like before, while observing the various jobs in Icelake to find something that truly speaks to you.
Right now, your life is a blank slate. You can become anyone. Rhythm Fischer — not just a Warrant Officer anymore, but someone with far more interesting and meaningful titles in the future.

Imagine this: Rhythm Fischer, the Bookstore Owner. Rhythm Fischer, the Fishing Enthusiast. Or even the Horse Whisperer, the Writer, the Pastry Chef... Anything's possible. Well, except, maybe, an electrician.
And before you find that new title that suits you best, it's okay to take a break. Just enjoy the time off.
You mean... it's okay to hit the pause button?
Of course. Even machines break down if they're running non-stop.

I think you should try to enjoy this little "pit stop." Maybe, in doing so, you'll naturally find what your true purpose is, and understand what it really means to move forward — not towards a goal someone else sets for you, but one that you set for yourself.
...Alright. I believe you.
Okay... it's settled then! Starting today, I'll follow your advice. I'll take it slow and try out all those jobs, one by one... alphabetically.
...That's not what "taking it slow" means!

name: The Meaning of "Rhythm"
desc: No more chasing notes scribbled by others — turn to a blank page, and begin your own movement.
memoryDesc: Each tricky passage is neatly marked, with careful notes in the margins. It clearly belongs to a diligent — if not yet seasoned — player. Look closer, and you'll spot a cute little lightning doodle in the corner.

dialogues.content: (It's the time you and Rhythm were supposed to meet, but she's nowhere in sight.)

(You check the time again and scan the surroundings, realising she's unusually late. Just as you begin to worry if something has happened to her, the sound of a harmonica drifts in through the window.)

options.content: Rhythm?

dialogues.content: Ah... yes. Sorry I'm late.
Were you playing the harmonica just now? That was a rare scene.
Well... remember when you told me to try and find "what I truly want to do"?
I thought it would be hard to just "find" something out of thin air, so I decided to start with something I'm familiar with... like playing the harmonica.
I'm not particularly good with music, but I want to understand it better. I picked a new song to learn. The owner of the second-hand bookstore said it's a piece about spring and hope.
I wanted to play it for you, but... I'm still a little unsure of myself. So, I thought I'd practice outside first...

options.content: I think you played it pretty well.
You can practice here. I'm here whenever you're ready.

dialogues.content: Thank you...
Did you notice that my brother's name and mine both have something to do with music?
My parents put a lot of thought into our names. I really like them. But the truth is, I'm not exactly good with music. I feel like I've wasted such a beautiful name...
The only piece I can play all the way through is Requiem for the Nameless. And the only reason I can do that is because Blues used to play it over and over in my ear.
Honestly, I don't even understand the sheet music. I just memorised the positions of the holes on the harmonica and how they should be played. It's all about muscle memory, really...

options.content: That's impressive in its own way...
Everyone learns in their own way. There's nothing wrong with that.

dialogues.content: Well, I'm a bit relieved hearing you say that.
While I have you, I have a favour to ask... Would you mind singing the melody while I play? That way, I'll know if I'm getting it right.

options.content: Sure!
I don't really know how to read music either...

dialogues.content: Thank you! Let's give it a try.
That's okay. We'll figure it out together.
(Under Rhythm's encouraging gaze, you start humming the melody of the song slowly, following the sheet music.)
(She raises the harmonica to her lips and, despite a slight clumsiness, tries to play along with you. After your duet ends, she plays the song once more on her own.)
Hmm... The pitch is okay, but the rhythm is all over the place. Once I focus on the pitch, it's hard to keep the rhythm steady. I guess I'll need more practice...
I thought it sounded pretty good, honestly.
It's okay if the rhythm's off. This is not an exam. Besides, music is supposed to be free of restrictions.
I think your name, "Rhythm," carries the same meaning. It's not about living your life according to some fixed "beat," but about finding your own rhythm.

So, you don't have to be so tense all the time, always keeping yourself busy. Live freely — decide for yourself when to move forward, and when to take a break. What is your own "rhythm," Rhythm? I think once you really get the hang of this piece, you'll see what I mean.

To master this song, you'll need to practice. To learn more songs, you may have to visit the bookstore again. And if you wish to share the spirit of spring and hope with others, you'll need to play it for them.
There's no set schedule for when to do these things. It's all up to you. You can do them whenever you feel like it. And what you feel like doing — or not doing — that's your "rhythm."
Of course, if you ever need someone to help you with the sheet music... I'm always here.
{nickname}...
Thank you. That's the most beautiful interpretation of my name I've ever heard.
I'll always remember your kind words.
If you don't mind bearing with my clumsiness and would like to witness my change... I promise you this: once I find my own "rhythm," I'll share it with you first, before anyone else.

name: Ulterior Motives
desc: When smart people speak, there's always an agenda behind their words. Efficiency is their craft, and in a way, that's its own form of honesty.
memoryDesc: Forget the grind and shake off your weariness — start your well-deserved break with a chilled, sweet indulgence!

dialogues.content: Nothing beats having a refreshing drink after a good rest. It's so wonderful to have a break from work!
Speaking of which, I got a package before I came here. Let me take a look.
This must be the pyjamas and incense my subordinate bought me as a sleep aid. Perfect, I'll go back home and take another rest.
Huh? "Proposal on the Optimisation of Ornamental Plants of the 13th Legion"? "Application for Purchasing Recreational Facilities to Enhance Soldiers' Morale"?
Urgh, it's always about work. Let's talk about this later. I won't let my holiday be spoiled by anything or anyone, except the Chief. But I doubt she'll show up here.

options.content: You're indeed a man of principles when it comes to this.
You're always slacking off, Randy.

dialogues.content: It's not easy to come up with such practical principles as these.
Whoa, how could you call this "slacking off"?
This is the "Howard High-Efficiency Energy-Saving Mode", created by yours truly, Randy Howard.
When you take a break, clear your mind of all work so that you can start working again in a good mood. That way, you won't dread getting back to work.
After years of practising and optimising this method, I've got it working perfectly.
This has helped me to figure out the most energy-saving solution to different problems in seconds.
Such as this conversation with an ulterior motive.
Huh? I'm not following.
A bit too late to play dumb, don't you think?
...Tell me, how's Berenica doing now?!
Hah, so that's No. 0's name — Berenica.
A bit late to play dumb too, I'd say.
Well, playing dumb is how smart people start a conversation.
But honestly, your question's moot. For starters, even if I did tell you something, there's no way you could verify it.
Secondly, in the principle of the "Howard High-Efficiency Energy-Saving Mode", I keep work and life separate.
Life might blend into work, but work must never intrude on my life. Right now, I'm technically on vacation, and that's the most "energy-efficient" way I operate.
So, this conversation and any future talks about No. 0 aren't gonna get anywhere; but if you want to chat about life and other fun stuff, I'm all ears.
Then it seems we're done here. You can leave.
While I can't disclose her whereabouts, I can assure you, she's safe.
There's no way I could verify that.
Hahaha, smart people are all quick learners.
*sigh* It's sad to see good intentions go unappreciated — so much so that I might not be able to rest properly tomorrow...

Oh, wait! Maybe I should try to extend my holiday by taking sick leave. Like, I need a prolonged holiday 'cause my illness had prevented me from getting proper rest. That makes perfect sense, doesn't it?!
And the reason I'll use will be... I feel achy all over, especially in my heart.
Because of a conflict during a public opinion survey... but it has been resolved through private negotiations. Maybe I'll even get compensation out of it. Today has been very fruitful.
You just extended my holiday in mere seconds. My friend, you're the best!
I'm looking forward to my next excuse for... Ahem... I mean, our next meeting.

name: The Making of a Gentleman
desc: A gentleman is not born but forged — shaped by education, refined by environment, and polished with a little family "guidance."
memoryDesc: A high-end drink aged for 20 years, "Triumph" has become a symbol of refinement and prestige among Hyperborea's elite. Yet, beneath the luxurious packaging, the bitterness is hard to mask.

dialogues.content: Looks like you're finally up for some casual chats, huh?
I'm still on a mission, so I couldn't meet up with you during working hours. I requested leave especially to grab a drink with you.
And my reason for this leave... I told them I was invited to a dance by a young lady of nobility.

Oh don't be surprised. It's quite common for young officers and noble ladies to have romantic affairs. The Legion turns a blind eye to them. After all, having relations with "the nobility" can bolster the Legion's influence.
As a gentleman, I had to take longer leave for this reason. I think it makes perfect sense.

options.content: A gentleman who lies to get off work?
Yeah, definitely. You're such a gentleman.

dialogues.content: Your words are like a dagger in my heart. I might have to extend my leave to recover from that burn.
Thank you, I'll take that as a compliment.
I'm aware by the way, that "gentleman" is often used sarcastically, not as praise.
When I was little, my sisters told me that being a gentleman is the ultimate goal for a man.

options.content: Your sisters? They must've been fair ladies.
I can't imagine what you were like as a boy.

dialogues.content: Maybe you're making that assumption based on your high opinion of me, but unfortunately, they're not lovely ladies, not at all.
I was just like any ordinary kid. Dumb and naive.
Look, I really don't feel like talking about my sisters. They tormented me during my childhood. But since you're my holiday buddy, I will tell you this.
I grew up with their "love". To survive their clutches... ahem, I mean love, I had to develop many skills.

options.content: Love? That doesn't sound so bad.
Tough love? That sounds as sarcastic as the word "gentleman". You must've had a bitter childhood.

dialogues.content: Yeah, love. Tough love.
Yeah, it was rather bitter.
Back then, they told me that a gentleman should kiss a lady's dress when they meet, and that one should adhere to principles and etiquette to conceal their true thoughts and feelings.
When I was five or six years old, I acted like a gentleman to every woman I met, even though I didn't want to.
You can imagine how my sisters watched me and laughed. Later on, they told me that gentlemen didn't really have to do that.
They should actually kiss the back of a lady's hand. Not her dress.
Anyway, let's not talk about this. Here's a toast to my miserable childhood.

name: Black Mist in White Snow
desc: Ah, Father!
memoryDesc: The pistol serves as both a symbol of responsibility, weighing heavily on a father's shoulders, and a badge of honour passed down through generations.

dialogues.content: I'm here. I couldn't stand you up now, could I?
Check this out. The Military Alloy Temperature Control Vessel - Ultimate Type. I've tried it, and it works like a charm... *yawn*
I'm feeling a bit drowsy at the moment, I need to find a place to get some shut-eye. I've nearly run out of annual leave, and I can't report to Chief Sibylle tomorrow with dark rings around my eyes.

options.content: Is something troubling you? You seem a bit off today.
Why are you hurrying to leave? Got another dance with a noble lady?

dialogues.content: You're very perceptive. Yes, there's something on my mind.
Of course not. You know how lazy I am. I turn most invitations down.
I won't keep it from you. Basically, I had a nightmare.

options.content: What kind of nightmare?

dialogues.content: To be honest, I had a nightmare last night, so I'm feeling a bit off today.

options.content: What kind of nightmare?

dialogues.content: Well, like many of my nightmares, this one was about my dad.

options.content: You've never mentioned him before.

dialogues.content: He used to be a soldier in the Empire, but... he's been bedridden for years now.
Back when I was tricked by my sisters into becoming a gentleman, he was a sergeant in the Legion. He spent more time on the front lines than at home, just like me now.
But the difference between us is that he was proud of being a soldier. He treated the Legion as his home and his actual home as nothing more than a hotel where he could complain as much as he liked.
Whenever he came home, he'd complain about something or other, like the Emperor's portrait not being hung up properly, or my sisters coming home too late.
And he'd always check up on me last.
He'd check how much taller I'd got, how many books I'd read, how many forts I'd learned the names of, and what new survival skills I'd acquired.
I tried talking to him about other things, but he wasn't interested in anything other than "being a soldier."
Once, to try to please him, I painstakingly carved a wooden pistol for him and eagerly awaited his praise.
But with a stren face he just snatched it from me, "Don't waste your time on things like this. Think about how you can become a better soldier from now on."
At that moment, I felt something change within me. Something cold, bitter, intangible and unstoppable, like the howling wind outside our home.
Later, I gradually realised that it was hatred. Although it was weak to begin with, it was still strong enough to make me feel that the person in front of me was nothing more than a stranger.
So after that, I stopped trying to be the son he wanted me to be. I ignored his check-ups on me, no matter how much he scolded me.
Years passed... He was shot in the head while protecting one of his subordinates. He was sent home with a purple heart. Although he was still alive, he had fallen into a coma.
When he came back, he had nothing but shiny medals, his slender savings, and a wooden pistol that was broken in two.
I thought he was disappointed in me because of that broken pistol, but his subordinates told me that he carried it with him at all times and that it broke when he fell on the battlefield.
It seems that he did love me after all. But his way of expressing it was unrecognisable. Maddening.
If he was proud of me, he should've told me. A few words of encouragement would've been enough, but instead, he just forced me to do things I didn't enjoy.
Although he'd never push me to do anything again, I still joined the army, just like he wanted.
I was curious about the Legion, the place that had turned my father into a detached man. I also wanted to prove that I could live a great life without his scolding.
Unfortunately for both of us, I found out that he was right all along. He was protecting me.
We're unlike most people in the Legion. We crawled out of piles of corpses on the battlefield, and kneel down to receive the medals they bestowed upon us like charity.
A decent job, a great life, and a means of survival. Everything about us is determined by those small medals. For the sake of our family, my dad devoted himself to them.
He obeyed, endured, suppressed his feelings, pushed back the tears, and turned himself into a husk of a man.
I can't do that, but I need money to support myself and maintain my family's decent lifestyle. So, I'm a happy loser now, as you can see.

options.content: Is that so?

dialogues.content: You have a keen eye. But to be frank, I have no idea what I want to do. After a long bout of depression, I've finally realised that —
Even though I haven't lived up to my dad's expectations, I'm happy with the life I have.

options.content: If your dad regains consciousness, he'll be very proud of you!
Let me make one more drink for you.

dialogues.content: I hope so. If that happens, my nightmares may finally end.
That tastes good. This will help me sleep without nightmares.
Thanks, holiday buddy, but I need some sleep now, or else I'll have to take more leave tomorrow.
Don't worry, I'll be the regular Randy you know the next time we meet. And if I have another nightmare, please make me one more cup of this delicious drink.

name: "Cinderella"
desc: One last dance before the clock strikes twelve.
memoryDesc: Sometimes, the best ideas strike while showering, sleeping, or sipping tea. The actions taken in pursuit of such inspiration might appear a little... eccentric to the outside world.

dialogues.content: A hot drink with extra sugar, please. I brought some desserts from the Imperial Capital. I queued up to buy them during my break. Want to try some?

options.content: Thanks, you seem to be in a good mood today.
What are you planning?

dialogues.content: I sure am. I'm in the mood for a sweet drink as a prelude to my invitation.
Ooh! I want to ask a small favour of you, but I wouldn't call it a "plan."
Ahem... Maybe this is a little sudden, but do you want to attend a dance with me?
Like I mentioned to you before, the Legion needs to maintain ties with local nobility. So, I need to attend annoying social balls in the inner city from time to time.
I really don't want to go. The trip is paid for, but dealing with nobility is such a headache.
So, I have a perfect solution. I can take a gorgeous lady with me as my partner.
That way, no one will try to introduce me to a female relative I've never met before.

options.content: But you need a gorgeous lady. Why did you come to me?
So, you're asking me to be your partner.

dialogues.content: Well... I was thinking... maybe... you could try to disguise yourself as a lady.

options.content: Why don't you disguise yourself?
Are you serious?

dialogues.content: Yes, you're my best dancing partner, after all. The question is, are you willing to do me this favour?

options.content: Are you going to arrest me at the ball?

dialogues.content: I can't. I'm the one who's been invited.
Sorry, but you're my last hope. I'm really clutching at straws here!
What?
We've had so many drinks together, and you're my closest friend. I'm even closer to you than my siblings, so I'm begging you for help.
Why on earth would you think that? If I really wanted to arrest you, I could've done that the first time we met.
If you help me in my time of need, I'll give you half of my salary for the next six months. And, if Chief Sibylle tries to arrest you next time, I'll come forward and protect you!
I don't see the point in using my precious leave to come here and organise something like a "secret arrest ball".
If that's not enough, I'll dress up like a lady and entertain you after the ball. What do you say?

options.content: ??? What the heck, bro?
You just want to dress up like a girl, don't you?

dialogues.content: And what if you turn me down? How would my plan work in that case?
No, no, no! You've got the wrong idea! What makes you think that?
You must be kidding. Do you seriously think I'm a scheming fool like that?

options.content: I'm just kidding. Of course I don't.
Maybe you're right.

dialogues.content: I mean, it's normal, right? Best buds do everything together — hang out, share meals, hit the restroom, try on dresses...

options.content: What's with the last two...?

dialogues.content: Alright then. If you really did misunderstand me and think I was a shameless jerk who'd betray his friends like that, I'd need a month's leave to recover from such heartbreak.
Hey, at least deny that I betrayed my friends for personal gain, or else you'll hurt my feelings!
Hey, don't laugh at me. I'm really in a bind here. Please just give me your answer. If you say "no," I'll have to find another solution.

options.content: Fine, I give up. I'll help you.
Let me think about it.

dialogues.content: But now there's one thing I'm sure of — You're not afraid of risk at all.
Just think about it...
Please give it plenty of consideration. After the ball, I'll find many creative ways to repay you, just like how I come up with excuses to take time off.
So, you were messing with me to see my reaction.

options.content: Sorry, I just wanted to see you panic. I couldn't help myself.
No, I'm really worried about being arrested!

dialogues.content: Huh? Really? That's fantastic! You're a lifesaver!
Take as much time as you need. I really need your help, and I'm certain that you'll come through for me.
I didn't know you love mean tricks like me. Where did you pick that up?
What?!
You've done me a huge favour. I'll repay you however I can.
I'll be awaiting your answer. See you later, my holiday buddy, break-time pal, and the target of my pursuits to this very day.
I panicked for a moment then. Although deep down I knew it was impossible, I was still worried. What if you really thought that way?
Okay, fine, you're right. I've been wanting to arrest you for ages. Every morning, I wake up and think about how to carry out my devious plan, but I procrastinate too much to actually do it.
But let's talk about this after the ball. I need to go home and prepare my outfit before you change your mind.
So, to make up for your trick, you must help me.

options.content: Okay, I'll help you.
Let me think about it.

dialogues.content: This time, I was hoping to fulfil my duty but failed. What do I do?
I'll see you later, my holiday buddy, break-time pal, and the target of my pursuits to this very day.
Maybe you can think twice before answering me...
One day, I'll be fired by the Legion and end up homeless and destitute on the cold streets of Icelake.
... Huh? Really? That's fantastic! You're my lifesaver!
Do you really want to see me turn into an ice sculpture on the street?

options.content: Okay, I'll help you.
Let me think about it.

dialogues.content: You've done me a huge favour. I'll repay you however I can.
But let's talk about this after the ball. I need to go home and prepare my outfit before you change your mind.
I'll see you later, my holiday buddy, break-time pal, and the target of my pursuits to this very day.

name: The Sword of Damocles
desc: The true test of loyalty lies in the ever-present sword, ready to fall.
memoryDesc: The 13th Legion stands as a symbol of authority, the vessel for the emperor's will and violence.

dialogues.content: That's certainly simple and efficient.
It's not that simple. The 13th Legion only takes orders from the Emperor. In the shadows, we are His Majesty's hidden blade, but in the light, we also serve as the messenger of his benevolence.
Executing a smuggler didn't close the case. We still needed to gather the alchemists together to deliver a message.
I bet they were too scared to even speak.
That was true. But what awaited them wasn't execution, but a speech announcing increased funding for the Spathatoi... With Willers's corpse nailed to the podium.

The Empire advances like a rumbling war chariot, and it cannot do without the academy as its engine. If we let a single act of smuggling impede the academy's research progress, that would be going against His Majesty's wishes.
So the rest of them just got off the hook just like that?
A spectacle of deterrence would suffice. All have witnessed the fate of those who betrayed the Empire.

The vermin and parasites like Willers would live in perpetual fear, dreading the knock at their doors every night. Those fence-sitters would breathe a sigh of relief, grateful for their prudence before making the wrong choice.
While the loyal — through the purge of the sinful and the commendation of the virtuous — will further cement their faith in His Majesty's justice.
Carrot and stick — the golden rule for commanding loyalty. We must tolerate some impurities, adjusting our grip as necessary.
Sounds too complicated for me to understand. I'm starting to think becoming a Major isn't all that great for me. Maybe I should stick to what I understand, like getting rid of this list.
Don't let the pressure overwhelm you. The 13th Legion spells death for our enemies but serves as a steadfast anchor for our allies. Take Randy — he'll help you navigate the minutiae.
Randy? He's tricked me more times than I can count.

His tricking you is also a lesson in disguise. He would never truly harm you. Though the smallest in number, the 13th Legion is composed of the forces' finest warriors. You need to learn how to blend in and build rapport with everyone.
Alright, I'll give it my best shot.
Chief Sibylle, I've cleaned up the office you were using before.
Consider it one of the perks of your promotion to Major. That's your workspace now.
His Majesty himself approves. Your achievements — capturing spies from the Elysian Church, suppressing The Forsakens, and neutralising large Filthoids — haven't gone unnoticed by His Majesty.
...I owe it all to your leadership, Chief.
Save it. We don't entertain sycophants in the 13th Legion. Use your head, be smart with what Randy taught you.
D**n it, he's duped me again.
Since you're here, it's clear you have uncertainties, even as a Major. Let's hear them.
Right, I've come across some of your personal items while clearing out the office, and I thought you might wanna have a look, Chief.
These documents have the Spathatoi crest on them. They seem quite old.
You've always dealt with matters related to the Spathatoi personally, so I didn't pry. How would you like to proceed with these documents, Chief?
These are... just some old lists of smuggled items from the Spathatoi that Randy put together for the case years ago. They can be discarded now.
Lists of smuggled items... Aren't these vital evidence?
The 13th Legion operates directly under His Majesty's command — our actions are guided by objectives, not by evidence.
Your confusion is understandable. Until now, your enemies have been external, and you've yet to witness the internal machinations. Let's take this chance to bring you up to speed.
When our missions intersect with other internal organisations, the "process" becomes irrelevant. The 13th Legion focuses solely on achieving the "results" His Majesty desires.
Mr Willers, you stand accused of smuggling alchemical equipment to the black market. Would you prefer to come quietly, or shall I assist you?
I'm a senior alchemist. Even with the Emperor backing the 13th Legion, you cannot simply do as you please!

Ssh, I'd advise you to think carefully before you speak. If this is just about smuggling, the lucky ones might still be spared. But if you slander and question His Majesty, then it would be considered treason.
Hmm, you know what, you might as well go on — it saves me the trouble of dragging you back — I could just shoot you on the spot. Come on, keep talking.

No, no... I am utterly loyal to His Majesty and the Empire... I harbour no ulterior motives... Those devices were faulty, so I thought it better to exchange them for money to buy new ones than to let them go to waste...
Those devices might be useless to the Academy, but if they end up in the hands of The Forsakens — or even worse, the Elysians — through the black market, have you considered the consequences?
They could reverse-engineer our tech through those rejects, which would lead to more casualties.
The money you've made through smuggling is tainted with the blood of our soldiers fighting at the front.
They won't accuse you, for they're fallen heroes, and you're just a vile vulture circling their corpses.
The Empire has no need for loyalty-chanting flies.
No, please... In Hyperborea, my smuggling amount wouldn't warrant a death sentence... You even said yourself I could live — I demand a fair trial!
Well, I said "the lucky ones."

name: Post-War "Trauma"
desc: War never truly ends — it merely changes form.
memoryDesc: Habit is a powerful thing. It makes us accept the abnormal and drift even further from the norm.

dialogues.content: Chief, the lists of smuggled items have been dealt with. All that's left is a broken recorder and an old photo for your review.
The recorder just keeps buzzing non-stop when it's on — I almost thought it was some kind of torture device.
Uh, that one. Just leave it here. Though I have many like it, one more won't hurt.
As for what's on it, it's no surprise you don't know — it's the sound of an airship engine model used over a decade ago.
Modern Empire airships prioritise stability and endurance, unlike during that war when speed and firepower were all that mattered.

You mean the "Divine Elegy" offensive against the Elysian Church more than 20 years ago, right? In that battle, the 13th Legion stormed their tower in prototype airships. That's a story even kids in the street can sing a verse or two about.
And it was your valour in that battle that made you the youngest chief in Empire history.
...Mm, we bypassed the hot zone at the border and struck directly at their normally untouchable tower, reaching the gods' lair for the first time. It's a tale worth retelling indeed.
But for the 13th Legion — or more precisely, for me — the campaign brought not only glory but also... anger and shame.
All 12 officers who attacked the tower were killed. Had I not been left to guard the airship outside, I might just be another number on the casualty list.
Behind the glory was our grievous defeat.
My last memory of that battle is piloting an out-of-control airship, weaving through relentless artillery fire and magical barrages across the border.
This recording takes me back to that airship... to that moment. It reminds me of the smell of blood in my nose and the weary roar of the engines in my ears.
That explains why you always choose the spot closest to the engine on flights.
This is war. It changes people.
I've seen too many soldiers in hospitals, still haunted by the war long after leaving the front. Sometimes, a ceremonial cannon or even a child's toy gun can trigger a breakdown.
War leaves its mark even on the toughest among us. Take the Chief of the 11th Legion stationed at the border, who sleeps with one eye open.
In that campaign, their forces held off the bulk of the Elysian army at the border, bearing just as much burden and bloodshed as we did.
Is that why you replay this recording over and over? Out of guilt over your comrades' deaths?
No, just to keep myself sharp. When I feel tired, it helps me focus.
Many dwell on past failures, lamenting their impotence, wallowing in guilt, and torturing themselves — this is the instinct and privilege of the weak.
But to me, failure is the scar of the past. It's a harsh reminder for me to keep pushing, to climb from all the pain and shame to victory.
I honour my comrades' sacrifices, which is precisely why I refuse to fall as they did. Pausing for breath or to mourn the fallen before claiming final victory would only squander their sacrifices.
Many call me cold-hearted, and some even cite my humble origins, claiming that cruelty is in my Charon blood.
But in the end, they'd forget the failures and even the names of the fallen, just buzzing like bugs before they perish.
All that remains is me, bearing the scars of defeat, continually climbing upward.
From my perspective, Chief, you've already reached heights many can't even dream of...
No, it's not enough. The 13th Legion bears a "true ideal" not yet known to the world.
Some of those born into privilege have long been drunk with fame, power, and glory. They only look downward, always plotting to shove those bearing true ideals off the cliff.
Nobles who can barely ride or understand the basics of command don't belong in this country.
I cannot afford to mark time like they do. I must climb higher, to the utmost power.
When that time comes, we shall lead the Hyperborean Empire — no, all of humanity, into a new tomorrow. Do you understand, Lynn?
Honestly, I didn't quite follow. You know, I'm just here for the cash — didn't have much choice.
But if you're saying big changes are coming... Then when they do, I'll definitely fight my hardest to protect my family — didn't have much choice on that either.
I appreciate your candour, Lynn. However modest, you have something worth fighting for — that's all that matters.

name: The Meaning of Alchemy
desc: Since humanity first roamed forests and plains, tools have ensured survival. Whether for creation or destruction, their purpose remains unchanged.
memoryDesc: Beneath the glory of this medal lies a path strewn with thorns.

dialogues.content: I've taken care of the recorder. As for the photo… it's of my teacher and that naive fellow pupil of mine, right?
Why do you call everybody naive, Chief?
Ha, yes, I've said the same about you. But her naivety was different to yours. She was another pupil of my teacher, with a remarkably pure heart.

Even within the Spathatoi, she held onto some rather fanciful ideas about alchemy. I remember the first time I met her, she asked me and our teacher: "Alchemy will make everyone's life better, right?"
So, what do you think of alchemy, Lynn?
Some fancy tech. I've never really used it myself.
Haha, our ancestors had long ago refined alchemy into the very foundation of the Empire's lifestyle. You've been using it all along. You just didn't realise it.
Take the bullets and firearms you use — they are one of the products of alchemical technology.
Really? Huh, well, I'd sure be lost without my guns. Those alchemists must be some talented scholars.
Most would agree. Alchemists might be a bit eccentric, but their inventions have been steadily transforming this country.
My teacher always said alchemy was a profound science that would change the future of the Empire. While my fellow pupil believed it was the key to peace and hope.
But for me, alchemy is something more pragmatic — a tool for climbing the ladder of power.
It was my alchemy skills, coupled with my loyalty and competence, that first got the Emperor's attention, making me a key player in the Divine Elegy offensive.
I aced every subject at the academy but never really poured my heart into any research. The deep theoretical knowledge just didn't resonate with me.

That infuriated my teacher. At the graduation ceremony, she even said that I would never grasp true knowledge. But riddle me this — how many have truly understood knowledge and truth through the ages?
And where are they now?
After all this time, if she were to ask me that question again, my answer would still be the same. Only now, there's no chance of that.
Right, I heard from Randy that the chief alchemist has passed away and that her relationship with her star pupil was... complicated.
Yes. Sadly, even when my teacher passed away, her favourite student — my fellow pupil — never showed up. It was just me there... along with a few ominous crows outside the hospital room.
What's sadder is that she never solved the formula that epitomized truth. Her monumental research ended up as indecipherable scribbles.
She entrusted her ideals and dreams to her, collapsing in her pursuit of truth. And what did she do?
She abandoned her prospects and resources, wasting her talents in a completely different field.
Didn't you say you don't dwell on the past?
I did, but that doesn't mean I'm devoid of feelings. Every time I look back, I'm overwhelmed by a mix of anger, confusion, regret, and even jealousy.
I always knew I wasn't one of her best students, who had their dreams, their ambitions, and limitless prospects.
But I know I'll be the one who makes it to the end.
By the way, though I know you wouldn't mention this conversation to anyone, I still have to remind you to keep it between us.
Understood! I don't really have anyone to talk to anyway. But I'm curious, Chief — if you don't want anyone to know, why share all this with me?
Because you're the right person for this. I know you don't care about nor understand those complex past events and emotions, and you're not one to offer empty sympathies, sincere or not.
I've never needed any sympathy or pity from anyone.
All we can truly rely on is what we wield. I think you understand that too.
That will be all for today. If you ever feel lost, you're welcome to talk to me.
While I may not offer comfort, I can guide you through resolving your doubts.

name: Life Runs on Meals
desc: Eating is the most basic of needs for all living creatures, but the art of eating is far from simple.
memoryDesc: This classic beverage was born from a mishap, yet became a staple across Atlasia for its versatile charm. After generations of refinement, it has transcended its original purpose of quenching thirst and staving off hunger, becoming a symbol of our pursuit of culinary delight.

dialogues.content: Mmm — this bread drink smells amazing! Did you make it yourself? You've really got a knack for this!
At one of our food drives, a kind-hearted lady brought along her homemade bread drink. She said it was quite the project!
You gotta chop up bread into bits, sprinkle on some sweet malt sugar, toast it till it's nice and warm, then soak it to let it ferment into a bubbly delight...
Mmm... this tastes just as good as the bread drink she made!

options.content: Wow, you know how to make this? It's not a common drink.

dialogues.content: Mm-hmm, I know everything about keeping bellies full!
I'm not bragging, you know — I'm like Elysium's walking encyclopedia of food! There's nothing about food that Commissary Truffle doesn't know!
So, any questions you've got about food — like where to find the best veggies in season right now, or what's in a certain dish — I've got all the answers!

options.content: Really? Can you guess which fruits are in this drink?

dialogues.content: Challenge accepted~ Lemme have another sip! ...Mmm, borealberries! Though they are a bit tart right now; they'd become sweeter and juicier a couple of days later.

options.content: You missed another berry, though.

dialogues.content: I know... Mmm, this taste is so familiar... just give me a moment...

options.content: Need a hint? It's—

dialogues.content: —Vermilion Teardrops! Freshly picked this morning from the wild, right?

options.content: Exactly right...

dialogues.content: Haha, why so surprised? It's no big deal. Filbert and I have tried EVERYTHING you can imagine — there's nothing unfamiliar to my taste buds.
Now, Vermilion Teardrops are a bit sour, like plums, so they go well with sweet berries; giant pine cones have tough shells, but the nuts inside are tender, crunchy, and sweet!
Creeping Tendrils taste just as awful as they look; insulating sealant looks like milk and smells fruity, but if you eat it, you'll get a tummy ache... so never try it!

options.content: ...Please tell me you've never tried Filthoid tentacles...
It's a miracle you've managed to stay healthy growing up...

dialogues.content: Nope, haven't gotten around to those. Wonder how they taste? Probably very slimy and chewy... Should Filbert and I try them out sometime...
Uh-huh. When I was little and wandering with Filbert, we occasionally nibbled on something poisonous and got sick.
Mm, pass! Though Filbert can knock over small Filthoids, those big ones are quite violent. I can't put Filbert in danger!

options.content: How come you've tried so many different "foods"?

dialogues.content: But don't worry! Now I'm quite the expert at identifying which plants are safe to munch on.

options.content: How come you've tried so many different "foods"?

dialogues.content: Because there was nothing much to eat. I started wandering alone at a very young age.
I've always been a big eater, so even though kind people sometimes gave me food, it was never enough — I was always hungry...
Aww, don't feel bad for me! I'm not upset about it, because I met Filbert soon after.
That day, I was super hungry, and so was Filbert. She was just a tiny piglet then, but she gave me the only piece of bread she had found in a bin.
I don't quite remember what I was thinking back then, just that I whispered into her ear, "Let's leave the city and find food in the wild together!"

options.content: Wow, a pig that understands human speech...

dialogues.content: Uh-huh, amazing, right? Filbert must be a gift from the gods.
Ever since that day, Filbert has carried me to fields and forests to find food... We never went hungry again, and we've even been able to share extra food with other starving people.
Ah... I wonder if Filbert's hungry out there on her own. Can I take the rest of this drink to share with her?

options.content: Of course.
I'd rather not share my drink with a pig...

dialogues.content: Aww, you're so kind-hearted! Some people frown upon me sharing treats with Filbert, just because she looks like a pig. But to me, Filbert is a dear friend...
Oh...Okay. Then I won't drink it either.
Anyway, thank you so much for not judging!
Filbert is my best friend; rejecting her is the same as rejecting me... it'd hurt her feelings, and mine too. But still, thank you for the bread drink.
I'm full now. See you around!

name: The Sin of "Waste"
desc: "Waste not, want not" — a simple maxim, harder to follow as we age.
memoryDesc: Ripened by time and cloaked in snowy white, Twisty Pods quietly await harvest, offering nature's bounty.

dialogues.content: Hmm... ugh...
*sigh*

options.content: You seem upset. What's wrong?

dialogues.content: Huh? Oh, I'm fine... Hehe, hehehe!

options.content: Come on, I could spot that pout from a mile away.

dialogues.content: Ah, you saw through me... Well, they say sharing bread is good and sharing troubles is bad, but since you asked... maybe you can help me figure this out!
A few days ago, I met a really obnoxious guy... He seemed to be a butler for some noble family, and he wanted to buy loads of nuts from us commissaries.
He and his men brought seven big bags, and the payment offered was all zeros and commas!
As a priestess in the church always says, "A coin not earned is a coin lost!" So, Filbert and I worked our tails off all day for this order.

options.content: Did he stiff you on the payment for those nuts?

dialogues.content: It was the opposite. He paid in full and even added a bonus for our quick service — it should've been a great deal.
But as they were leaving, I noticed the butler picking out some fresh Twisty Pods from the bags and throwing them away.
I stopped him right there and explained those were perfectly good nuts — the white stuff was their natural fuzz, not mould.
And guess what, he said he knew they weren't mouldy, but they weren't good for extracting oil, so he didn't want them!

options.content: Extracting oil...?

dialogues.content: Uh-huh! They didn't buy those nuts to eat! You won't believe this—
He said his master's family bathe in boiled milk every day! And they only use milk from the healthiest cows on the farm!
And that's not all — they'd add fresh perfume to the bath milk. They used to use tulip petals for the fragrance, and now they're switching to essential oil from nuts!
As for the nuts that couldn't be used for oil? Straight into the bin!

options.content: That's so wasteful...
Hmm, bathe in milk... must be nice...

dialogues.content: Exactly! And even if I could look the other way, Filbert wouldn't be okay with it!
Ah, don't say that! Our scriptures say wasting food is a huge sin! They'll get their comeuppance!
I threw his money right back at him and took back my nuts. I just couldn't watch them waste food like that! According to the divine teachings, the worst sin is waste!

options.content: You're absolutely right, Truffle. Wasting food is bad.
But if they've already paid, isn't it their right to do as they please with their own stuff?

dialogues.content: Right? Every bit of wasted food could have filled a hungry belly. I can't let food go to waste! Not even a little bit!
Huh? That's not what the gods teach... Though what you said does make sense... But something still doesn't feel right...
Anyway — in the end, I got a lecture from a priestess for losing that order, but I still gave all those nuts to people in need.
Ugh, so complicated. Well, if they have the right to waste their own food, then I have the right not to sell food to them!
I know what starving feels like — it's awful! I never want that again, and I don't want to see anyone else starve.

options.content: You have a kind heart, Truffle.

dialogues.content: If only those who never have to worry about food could see that there are still people starving out there...
*sigh*... It feels like there's still a loooong way to go before Filbert and I can achieve our dream of feeding everyone in the world.
Well, I guess I should try even harder! I'm off to gather food with Filbert now! See you around — and don't forget to eat well!

name: The "Not-So-Unique" Pig
desc: Filbert may seem like an ordinary pig to others, but to Truffle, she means the world.
memoryDesc: Freshly squeezed Borealberry juice, with the tartness filtered away, leaving only rich sweetness. The real magic in making it even tastier is sharing it with your best friend!

dialogues.content: Hehe, borealberry juice is just the best this season — so sweet and refreshing, not sour at all. Yum yum!

options.content: Glad you like it.

dialogues.content: Can I have the recipe? Filbert would love this too!

options.content: Sure.

dialogues.content: Thank you! You're so benevolent and phillan... phillan-thropic — did I get that right? Anyway, you're an angel!
Filbert and I used to pick borealberries very often. Just a little twist, and they'd fall into my hands. I'd fill baskets full of them, and Filbert was always so happy hauling them back.
One time, we ate so many our tongues and lips turned purple! We spent a lot of time washing our mouths by the stream, but the colour just wouldn't come off.

Filbert got so upset she jumped into the stream to wash up, and then a crab under the pebbles pinched her foot — it hurt so much she whimpered. So I jumped right in to save her, and guess what — there was another crab, a really big one...
We both ended up soaking wet, limping back with teary, purple-stained faces. Priestess McGuffin patched us up, all the while giving us a good scolding.
Since then, every time Filbert passes a berry bush, she just eyes those borealberries eagerly but never dares to nibble at one.

options.content: Are you two scared of Priestess McGuffin?

dialogues.content: I'm not. But Filbert shivers whenever she's around, probably because she threatened to kick her out when we first came.
When Priestess McGuffin first took me in, she was worried that Filbert would eat up all the food in the church and leave everyone else hungry.
But it didn't take long for them to realize that she didn't share a pig's voracious appetite and wouldn't devour large amounts of food.
Priestess McGuffin eventually agreed to keep Filbert, though she still complains Filbert isn't cool enough. She'd say things like—
"Little Truffle, have you read this Hyperborean novel about a hero who befriends a dragon? Why do they get such cool animal friends, and we just have a pig?"
"And here's another novel by a Huaxu writer — they have a pig too, but theirs is a celestial general who fights monsters! Does our pig have any special powers?"

options.content: Maybe she has a point. You should find a cooler companion.
She's wrong. Filbert is irreplaceable.
Don't listen to her — riding a pig is super cool!

dialogues.content: Nuh-uh! I would never leave Filbert!

options.content: You really like Filbert. She must be very special.

dialogues.content: Wow, you really think so? You're the best! May the Gods of Life, Bounty, Borealberry, Burrowing Botato — any gods there are — bless you!

options.content: You really like Filbert. She must be very special.

dialogues.content: Special? She sure is! But I'm curious — why would you think so, {nickname}?

options.content: Because Filbert runs very fast.
Because Filbert can find lots of food.

dialogues.content: Actually, all Geniemons are pretty fast. Many wild pigs can also do the same. And compared to them, Filbert isn't even close.
She uses her nose to sniff out food in the wild. Actually, all Geniemons have sharp noses. If you ask them nicely, they could help you find food too.
Actually, I've really thought about this after Priestess McGuffin asked me.
I once wondered, among all Geniemons out there, why must it be Filbert?
But I only thought about it for one night. The next morning, when Filbert nuzzled my face to wake me up, it suddenly all made sense.
Because only Filbert... is my Filbert! The one who helps me dig for mushrooms, carry bags of food handouts, and fight against bullies...
She's always been there for me — when I stumble through scriptures, when I get sick, and when I run around on errands.

options.content: So it's the many little moments you've shared together that make Filbert so special?

dialogues.content: Exactly! Even though many people think Filbert is not cool, and even though there are many Geniemons in this world that run faster, look cuter, and dig up more mushrooms than Filbert... even if Filbert is just an ordinary pig...
Filbert is still the one and only in the world — Commissary Truffle's best partner!

options.content: Right, I remember she's the Special Commissary.

dialogues.content: Right! Truffle and Filbert together, fighting hunger—
Ah! I almost forgot — I haven't divvied up today's food.
I have to go now, {nickname}. See you next time!

name: The Worries of Truffle
desc: Everyone defines happiness differently, but no matter what, a full stomach gives us the energy to chase it.
memoryDesc: One filbert per question — that's the deal you made with the girl. So when in doubt, why not ask the Magic Filbert?

dialogues.content: {nickname}! I... I have a really important question! Can you answer it right now?

options.content: Sure. What is it?

dialogues.content: I'm wondering — would you be happy if you get to fill yourself up every day?

options.content: Of course.
Mm, I don't know.

dialogues.content: Then I have another question — is just being able to fill yourself up every day enough to make you happy?

options.content: Uh-huh. What's there to be upset about when you're full?
Nah, there's plenty of stuff to worry about.

dialogues.content: Exactly! There's nothing more important than a full belly!
Huh? Really? We might be different then.
For me, as long as I get to fill my belly every day, I'm happy. But I have two friends who don't feel the same way at all, so I'm a bit confused.

One is a lady from a rich merchant family. She lives out in the suburbs, and has loads of shiny gems that can be traded for tons of silver coins; she can easily afford to hire lots of amazing chefs to make as much delicious food as she wants.
But she's still not happy. One priestess told me it's because she has to move far away to a city she doesn't like, to live with someone she doesn't even know.
And the other one's the most devout follower in our church. He traded all the food he saved up for a month for a new set of scriptures at the shrine.

I mean, isn't that crazy? Wouldn't he end up starving because of that? He's always been so thin — the wind can easily carry him away like a leaf! But he says that reading the scriptures "feeds his soul"!
I just don't get it... Why are they so different from me?
Why are some people still upset even when they're full? And why are some happy even when they're starving?
The scriptures say we should all try to make others happy... but how can I make EVERYONE happy?

options.content: Human hearts are quite complicated. Everyone feels different.
You can't make everyone happy; that's just nonsense in the scriptures.

dialogues.content: What do you mean? I don't get it...
People cry when they're sad, laugh when they're happy, yell when they're upset, and eat when they're hungry... What's so complicated about that?

options.content: Filbert loves coriander juice, right?

dialogues.content: Mm-hmm! The priestesses make fresh coriander juice for Filbert every day!

options.content: What about you, Truffle? Do you like coriander?

dialogues.content: Mmm, coriander tastes weird — bitter on the tongue but strangely fragrant... I can only eat it if I hold my nose... Ah, I get it now!
Some people love hazelnut milk, but others hate its smell; Filbert loves coriander, but I don't... Our happiness comes from different things...
I see... For the two friends of mine, there are things that make them much happier than a full belly makes them, so they don't mind starving.
Then... what can I do for everyone?

options.content: You're already doing an amazing thing by filling so many people's bellies.
You can't attend to everyone; just focus on making yourself happy.

dialogues.content: Really? Have I already made a lot of people happy?
Stuff that makes me happy? Hmm, let's see...
Yes. Being full might not necessarily mean happiness for everyone, but starving certainly means misery.

I feel happy when I see everyone well-fed, when some priestess pats my head and says I did a good job, when Filbert nuzzles me with her snout, and... oh! Sitting here chatting with you makes me happy too!
Thank you! You're so sweet! I fell from a tree picking plums today, but your nice words just made the pain go away!
So you're saying... I just keep doing what I'm already doing, and that's enough?
Well... you're smart, and I'm just silly. If even you don't know how to make everyone happy, then I certainly can't figure it out.
But I've made up my mind — I'll keep doing my best as a commissary!
Maybe I can't make everyone happy. But if filling their bellies makes them even a tiny bit happier, then I'm not failing the teachings of the gods, am I?

options.content: Right, it's a noble cause.

dialogues.content: Hehe... Thank you! There's so much in this world I don't understand. If I ever get confused about anything, can I still come to you?

options.content: Any time.
Then I want one filbert for one question.

dialogues.content: You're the best!
Ah, I can't do that. Filbert would be scared without me by her side...
It's a deal then. You'll be the official consultant for the great cause of Truffle and Filbert — pinky promise!
Oh, you meant the nut — sure! I'll bring you loads of filberts to fill you up!

name: Drinking Buddies
desc: True friends don't expect anything in return. A warm meal and a kind word — that's more than enough.
memoryDesc: No need for words — the drink says it all.

name: The Troublemakers
desc: Even the trickiest rules can be worked around. But people? The ones who stir up trouble — they never change. Get too used to them, and you'll find your life tied up in knots.
memoryDesc: After a long day, it's not the flavour that makes a good drink — it's the clean finish, and someone to talk it over with.

dialogues.content: Ah — half an hour late, huh? My bad. To make it up to you, I swear — even if today's drink tastes like bad fish in a dirty sock, I'll down it in one go!

options.content: It's rude to be late when someone invites you for a drink.
That's not an apology. You're just angling for more drinks.

dialogues.content: Remember that big job I mentioned the other day? Just wrapped it up with Wells. Took a bit longer than we thought.
Haha — sharp one. Saw right through me.
The job wasn't the problem — it was the people involved that made it a pain.

options.content: The Legion?

dialogues.content: Nah. The Legion's manageable — long as you know the rules, read the room, and steer clear of stepping on the Empire's toes, you can find ways around most of their messes.
They're like a drawn blade — sharp and deadly, sure, but at least you see it coming.
It's the other lot you need to watch out for. The ones with no rules, just chaos. Like a live bomb buried just out of sight—
The Forsakens. That mad bunch. Once they drag you in, everything gets ten times messier.

Take this job, for example — just your standard delivery gig, right? But Wells thought something felt off with the weight, so he quietly chiselled a hole in the crate and had a peek. And what do you know? It was packed with contraband weapons, all marked for the Forsakens.
If we'd hauled that through the city gates, the guards would've gunned us down before we got a word in.
Which was probably the plan. Maybe they wanted a few Phoxhunters dead. Maybe a little public chaos to slip into Icelake.
Or maybe it was all for show — a nice live performance, so their followers could watch exactly how cruel Solas are to Charons.
Point is, there's no guessing with them. Their motives don't make sense to normal folk — and their methods are even worse.
In the end, we had to smuggle the weapons in through the sewers just to finish the so-called "delivery."
Sounds simple when I say it, right? But Wells and I haven't had a proper night's sleep in days.

options.content: In that case, thirty minutes late doesn't sound so bad.
You should be getting rest, not drinking.

dialogues.content: Still — wrong's wrong. Doesn't matter how busy I was, I showed up late.
Nah. I'd never say no to a drinking buddy. Even if I were six feet under, I'd still claw my way up for a sip.
{空格}
But yeah, I do need sleep. Before I go — one last bit of advice. For your own safety, and for the sake of those who care about you... steer clear of the Forsakens.

options.content: You really hate them, don't you?

dialogues.content: ...Just survival instinct. Like most folk — I see danger, I walk the other way.
I've spent years scraping by between the grinding gears of clashing war machines. And if there's one thing I've learned, it's this: stay the hell away from the Forsakens.
This isn't some drunken ramble. This is life-or-death advice.

name: Secrets to the Grave
desc: Some secrets are fine to share — over a drink, with the right friend. It lightens the load, brings people closer. But others? They're meant to stay buried. Deep, dark, and untouched. Best if they never see the light of day.
memoryDesc: Steep those unbearable memories in the drink. Then down it in one go.

dialogues.content: Outsider shows up right on time. But after just one sip, he goes completely quiet.

options.content: Say something.
You okay?

dialogues.content: ...Ah... yeah. I'm fine. Good drink. Solid as ever.

options.content: Should I be getting you a handkerchief?
Are you gonna cry?

dialogues.content: Hah? Don't be ridiculous. Like I'd cry in front of people. Do I look like the soft-hearted type to you, buddy?
That said... lately, I've been thinking about the past more than I used to. Maybe I'm just getting old.
Don't give me that look. I'm not about to open up and bare my soul. You didn't seriously think a few drinks would buy my whole life story, did you?
Everyone's got things they'll take with them to the grave. They might not be buried in the coffin, but make no mistake — they're the most loyal companions we carry down there.
Could be something silly — like being weirdly fond of the smell of Phoxichor, or cracking a tooth on your favourite rock-hard gingersnap. Could be... a past you never talk about.

You won't see that stuff on the surface — they're called secrets for a reason. But truth is, it's that very stuff that drives a person. Not the whole reason, maybe — but close enough. You get the point.
When someone shares their secrets too easily, it's usually for one of a few reasons. Either those memories don't mean much to them anymore...
Or they're just spinning a tale to fish for sympathy.
Either way — spilling your guts to just anyone? That's reckless. You're handing over leverage. People might just see it as carelessness. Or worse... desperation.

options.content: I think it's totally normal to open up to friends.
That's a bit cynical. I still believe in people.

dialogues.content: Yeah, yeah, I get it. And you're not wrong. I say all this, but even I've let slip a secret or two at the tavern — like when I landed a juicy side gig or two.
But... let's just say, not all secrets weigh the same.

options.content: So what you're saying is, I'm not really your friend...

dialogues.content: Hey! How could you say that?
It's exactly because you're my friend that I can't tell you. I'm not trying to be cryptic or dramatic, alright? Think of it as a word of advice from someone who cares about you:
Digging up old graves doesn't always lead to treasure. Sometimes, all you find is rot. And I'd rather you never have to deal with the stench. Let me carry it.

It's fine. I've done a pretty good job of leaving the past behind. And if it ever comes knocking again — hey, I'll be the one answering the door. Not you. You just focus on the moment and let me handle the rest.
Alright then — another round, please! That last one went down so smooth, I barely tasted it.

options.content: I'm not running a soup kitchen here, you know.
Sure. Just try not to gulp this one down too.

dialogues.content: Hahaha! A stiff drink, a sharp-tongued friend, and a bit of banter — now this is the life.

options.content: Mhm. Good booze, good banter, and one very talkative mutt.

dialogues.content: What was that!?

name: A Name Left Behind
desc: It's not my real name — but I've grown to prefer "Outsider."
memoryDesc: Every problem has its fix. But the more you stew over it, the harder it is to see the road ahead.

dialogues.content: {空格}
Hm? What did you just call me?

options.content: I didn't say anything.

dialogues.content: Ah... must've been my imagination again. Been a bit on edge lately — sorry about that.
Truth is, I've been hearing voices calling my real name in my head for years. Some soft, some firm.
It's like tinnitus — you get used to it. Sometimes I even answer back, just for kicks. They're not real, after all.
But yesterday... something strange happened. I replied on reflex — just a little "hm?" — and this time, someone actually answered.
A rubbish bin tipped over near the street corner, and some shady character popped out from behind it and said hello.
Oof, I wanted to think it was just some brat messing around. But no — he called me by a name only the Forsakens would know. Not the name you know. Not Outsider.
I played dumb. Told him he had the wrong guy. No idea if he bought it... Ugh, should've let Wells handle that Forsakens' gig on his own.

options.content: You mean the delivery job from earlier?

dialogues.content: {空格}
Yeah. I suppose I owe you the truth. You deserve to know — wouldn't want you catching a blade in some back alley one day, just because you didn't know what I'd gotten tangled up in.
I've got... history with the Forsakens. Bad blood. They've been hunting me for a while now. That last gig? <H>Might've</> given 'em a whiff of my trail.
So now I've gotta cover my tracks in Icelake. Make sure nothing leads back to me.
Because if it does... my friends'll be the first to suffer. They'll go after them, one by one — until someone cracks and gives me up. And you? You wouldn't walk away, either.
But hey — if that day comes, just say I was some drinking buddy. That you don't know me well. Don't know a thing about any of this.

options.content: Got it. You should go.
You're not just a drinking buddy.

dialogues.content: Uh-uh. Hear me out. I'm just saying if. But if the worst does come...
I'll have to leave. Leave the city. Leave you lot behind. And Fina... take care of her for me, yeah?
If she asks, tell her I landed a big job. One that needs me gone a while. Here — these are letters I wrote. Give her one each month. That should buy you some time.
