Oh, right — there's some cash behind the third brick to the right of my fireplace. Take it if you need it. What else, what else...
Outsider, breathe. Calm down.
I am calm. Now repeat everything I just told you. If I'm not around, someone's gotta hold the line.
This really isn't like you. Is it because of the Forsakens?
"Like me," huh? Pretty sure the regular me wouldn't last five minutes against those lunatics with no moral scruples—
For a scrap of intel, they'd pull your fingernails out. One by one.
And that's just their idea of a warm-up. I'm not letting that happen... Not to anyone I care about.
But none of that's happened yet. You said your location <H>might've</> been compromised — not that it has.
Still. I've gotta start planning for the worst. Can't take any chances.
This isn't the first time, is it? Is this one really more dangerous than the others?
Hmm... Come to think of it, this one might not even crack the top five.
Right? And how did you get through those?
Well... some turned out to be false alarms. Others... bluffing, baiting, dragging the Legion into it, staging a few "cameos" in far-off cities — you know, the usual.

options.content: Talk about having no moral scruples... you'd almost rival the Forsakens.
So you've got no reason to run away this time either, right?

dialogues.content: {空格}
Yeah... you're right. What was I thinking? I've lived through worse. One little scare, and here I am — handing you my last words like it's the end of the world.
Maybe I've been spending too much time with you. Or maybe now that you're my Captain, some part of me thought I could lean a little. Or maybe... I've just gone soft.
No, no, no — can't be. Must be this drink. You spiked it, didn't you? I didn't say anything soppy just now, right? Be honest — I didn't, yeah?

options.content: Not at all. Want another drink?
You absolutely did. You owe me money for emotional damage.

dialogues.content: Anyway — rather than worry about what might happen, maybe we stay cool until it actually does. Who knows? By then, we might've already found a way through.
Hmm... good point. Cheers to that — here's to future me. May he be wiser and more put-together than current me. And to you — for being a good friend.
{空格}
Still... I owe you an apology. I've made peace with whatever's ahead — but my past? I still can't tell you everything. Not yet.
But I promise — someday, I'll show you the path that led me here. It won't be easy. And you might not like what you find.
But when that day comes... I believe you won't mind making me a drink like this one. Just like tonight, my friend.

name: If the Flower Must Wilt
desc: It is not the length of life that matters, but how we choose to live it.
memoryDesc: Children huddle together, dreaming of futures just beyond their reach.

dialogues.content: I'd never seen such a huge Filthoid before... My head was spinning, and I couldn't move my arms or legs. I knew I'd soon be returning to the Misty Sea and the bosom of Mother Embla, but I didn't expect that day to come so soon.
Then — {性别:he|she} suddenly charged forward. When I opened my eyes, {性别:he|she} was already shielding me from that Filthoid!
{性别:He|She} wasn't exactly strong, but {性别:he|she} bravely stared down the Filthoid, not backing down an inch...
And then that giant Filthoid leapt up, slammed down, and you both fell. Then you fought side by side and took it down. Then a man named Outsider popped up. And then—
Aw, Elisa! No spoilers, please!
You've told your Glevum Pit adventure three times already. I wish I had a coin for every time you told that story...
Well, I haven't told Fred yet, so... Um, right, that's what happened in the pit.
You must really like your new friend, Psyche.
Because you're especially talkative today, not that you're ever really quiet...
...Um, am I?
I've indeed never heard this story before. Let Psyche finish.
Alright! Now, where was I... Oh, Elisa already finished the second half for me.
Ooh! I just thought of something I haven't told you guys — that person isn't from around here but from a place far beyond Hyperborea — a small island to the south!
{性别:He|She} told me there's golden sand and white rosemary on that island... And the sea — it's as big as a hundred Lamenting Lakes put together!
There is also a giant Heaventree there — but unlike the one in Icelake, the breeze through the treetops is warm. Sailors use the Heaventree as a beacon at sea.
Sea, warm breezes, a Heaventree that's not just cold Phoxichor in factories, but a beacon for sailors...
Has that person ever stood under the Heaventree? From there, does the Heaventree look sparkling and magnificent — like in the songs by those wandering bards?
About the sand you mentioned just now...

I've heard that the sand by the sea is soft and smooth, and stepping on it feels like stepping on flour, not at all rough on the feet. And the sand is also very clean because of the waves, so it doesn't dirty your feet, right?
{性别:He|She} didn't mention any of this... I'll ask for you all next time!
What's the point in knowing all this, when we can't even leave Icelake?
...That's true.
No, it's not like that... Think of it this way:
Hunt shares tales of the Phoxhunters' adventures, and Mia tells us about all kinds of fish hiding beneath the ice of the Lamenting Lake...
Carolina gives us a fascinating glimpse into the novel lives of the ladies in the inner city, Elisa offers unique takes on old fairy tales, and Fred shares clever cleaning tricks...
Even if we don't get to experience all this first-hand, it's still wonderful to hear them from those who did.
Oh, it's really cool to learn so much when our lives are about to end — so we can take all this knowledge straight to the grave.
Don't you find that ironically cruel?
You do have a point...
But, um, I still feel there's more to it...
I know my days are numbered — there's no denying that. But if I just sit here doing nothing, simply waiting for "that day" to come...
Then I couldn't forgive myself, even in the grave.
So I tend flowers, read, go on adventures, and share stories with everyone... I always feel that I should busy myself with something, anything...
Perhaps then, when that day comes, I'll have fewer regrets.
But I didn't mean to upset you, Elisa — I'm sorry. I'll try to keep my mouth shut from now on.
Huh? But Psyche, you're the only one willing to talk to me ever since Hunt left...
Don't worry about it. I was just speaking off the cuff... I'd actually miss your chatter if it was gone.
Okay... I'm glad you're not upset, Elisa.
Next time you see that person, could you ask about the golden sand for me?
And about the Heaventree.
Sure! I'll keep all this in mind. I'll ask for you next time I see {性别:him|her}.

name: Remembered by Water and Wind
desc: Death is not the worst thing, as long as one is remembered.
memoryDesc: "Please see the world through your eyes for me."

dialogues.content: Elisa, I'm back.
I brought you some bread — I bet you've skipped the meals again. I'm not going anywhere until you finish it.
Why waste food... We're all going to leave the world soon anyway.
Don't say that... Do you see that plant over there? It'll eventually wither for sure, but we still water and take care of it so that it'll bloom one day.
But what if it never blooms?
Then, just watching it sprout and grow bigger is still wonderful, isn't it?
...Forget it. I don't have your green thumb.
By the way, why was that person here earlier? {性别:He|She} is not a Deteriorator, so why the frequent visits? Is {性别:he|she} a spy for the Security Bureau?
You mean {nickname}? {性别:He|She}'s not a local. {性别:He|She} now works as a Phoxhunter and has nothing to do with the Security Bureau. I think {性别:he|she} was here for a commission.
I heard {性别:he|she} found something Dr Henrik needs. If it helps, maybe we... um, never mind.
Didn't you say you went out of town with that person yesterday and got an earful from Dr Henrik?
Huh? Um, yes...
Then why still mix up with {性别:him|her}? Since {性别:he|she}'s not one of us and not with the Security Bureau, {性别:he|she} has nothing to do with us, right?
I... I just thought there might be something I could do—
Honestly, Psyche, I don't understand you sometimes.
{性别:He|She} is just a stranger, and might just leave Icelake tomorrow. {性别:He|She} doesn't even know... what will happen to you... You know it — everyone here is not long for this world.
Yet you're always out helping others, giving away flowers, making meals, telling stories, helping travellers with accommodations... What's the point?
Maybe you should stop meddling in other people's business and focus on yourself more.
...You have a point.
But you got one thing wrong — I'm not as selfless as you think.
To be more precise... I did all those things for myself.
I'm not afraid of dying — no, that's an overstatement... I am afraid.
But what terrifies me even more than death is... the idea of "disappearing." Once you're forgotten, it's like the very evidence of your existence just gets wiped away.
So you go out of your way to help as many people as possible, hoping they'll remember you for as long as they can — is that it?
Yes... I'm actually... very selfish. You're right, {性别:he|she} will leave one day.
{性别:He|She} doesn't belong here. I've always known that {性别:he|she} is different — unlike us, trapped in Icelake forever.
And that's exactly why I want to be friends with {性别:him|her} — so that {性别:he|she} will carry memories of me while going on wonderful adventures around the world.
I've read about the never-setting sun in Askard to the north, the cloud-capped tower of Elysium down the south, and further east, the star-bound ships of Huaxu...
But you'll be gone by then.
But I'll live on in {性别:his|her} memories. That way, it's like my life continues with {性别:him|her}.
How do you know for sure that {性别:he|she} will remember you?
I... I'm not sure. I'm not as smart as you. I don't understand many things, and I don't know how to make people remember me more.
So I just try my luck... like chatting with {性别:him|her}, listening to {性别:his|her} problems, and helping out with things...
Hopefully, that will leave more of an impression in {性别:his|her} memory — it's really just a shot in the dark though...
*Sigh*
You can be such a fool sometimes, Psyche.
...Maybe give {性别:him|her} a gift. But please, no more of your flowers.
Huh? Then what should I get {性别:him|her}...?
Something that won't break or go bad easily, that's for sure... It should be durable, special, and easy for {性别:him|her} to carry around at all times, ideally something practical.
That way... it might always remind {性别:him|her} of you.
That's a great idea!
I've got it... I have the perfect "treasure" to give {性别:him|her}!
Thanks, Elisa! You really are much smarter than me.
Alright, you need to eat the bread now.
And I'm going to water that plant... Hmm, where's the watering can... ah, there it is.
Ugh... why did I even say that...
Guess I'm also a fool...
Never mind...

name: New Wish Shall Sprout
desc: No one knows what tomorrow holds, yet even with life's uncertainties, we face the unknown, hoping for a better future.
memoryDesc: The coin has been tossed. No one can predict the outcome — heads or tails, death or rebirth.

dialogues.content: I should've come a bit later to give you more time to say goodbye.
Dr Henrik, do you mean...
I mean that kid, {nickname}. It was hard letting go of {性别:him|her} when {性别:he|she} grasped your hand, wasn't it?
Yeah... you always see right through me.
But I know that even though {性别:he|she} was right in front of me, {性别:he|she} was actually very far away, as far as Icelake is from the ocean.
So even though {性别:he|she} reached out, I couldn't really grasp {性别:his|her} hand, just as I tried so hard to look at {性别:him|her}, but couldn't see anything.
...Psyche, there's something I want you to know.
The development of anti-deterioration medication is finished.
Already? I thought the research would take longer...
I started the research years ago but put it aside after Hayley's death. I only picked it up again for you... for all of you.
Fortunately, all the previous theoretical data is still fresh in my mind, and with that piece of the Crystallo of Stella, I managed to replicate most of the experimental steps...
That's great! Your research succeeded! But... this is good news, right? Why do you still look so sad...?
*sigh* It's complicated...
Crystallo is highly unstable. Under specific medicinal catalysts, it can suppress the process of deterioration, or accelerate it... The conditions triggering each process are only minutely different.
Sadly, all the relevant pharmacological texts from Huaxu were lost in Hyperborea, and I can't verify each step of my work purely through theory.
The only option is clinical trials... but I can't bring myself to test an unverified new drug on you.
Perhaps your kindness is why the research on the anti-deterioration drug hasn't progressed further. Dr Henrik, please allow me to help you with the clinical trials.
Hypnos' House was founded to alleviate suffering... If I use you for experiments, how am I any different from the Legion!?
It's not like that... You've been taking care of us, going out of your way to ease our pain, but the pain hasn't disappeared — you've simply taken it upon yourself.
So, please let me share some of that burden.
It's more complicated than you might think... Do you realise what could happen if you take that medicine?
... I'm not sure if I get this right. Do you mean it might work, but also might not?
There's a fifty-fifty chance.
You could recover and gain a second chance at life, or...
Your condition could deteriorate rapidly... You might even be robbed of your last moments.
Dr Henrik, I've made up my mind.
The anti-deterioration drug is a chance to ease the pain of us all. Even if the chances of success are slim to none, I'd still like to help with your research. Besides...
I feel like I've changed... I'm not who I used to be.
What do you mean?
I've changed ever since I met someone and went on an adventure.
I've become much greedier... I now yearn for more time, more of everything...
I wish to hold someone's hand and escape Icelake, to travel to far-off lands...
I wish to grow older... so that one day I'll become a wrinkled old lady, sitting in the square, feeding birds and sharing stories of my youth with children...
I once thought that making the most of my last days was enough. But now, I want more...
I want to LIVE.
So, Dr Henrik, please allow me to help with the research.
"If fate decides I can't live like a person, then at least let me die like one..."
That was Hayley — my daughter's last wish. You and her are so alike, yet so different...
"To live like a person" — I understand your wish now.
Fate, grant me mercy just this once... allow me to help her fulfil this wish.

name: Before the White Grave
desc: Prolonged pain or instant death — I do not know which is crueller. But perhaps... we still have a chance to overcome the former.
memoryDesc: A bouquet of dew-kissed blooms, offered to a patient in goodwill. Yet true pain is not so easily eased by kind gestures.

dialogues.content: (That was six months ago. I'd gone to visit Roger Gaston — a wounded veteran of the war against the Elysian Church on the Southern Front.)
Emilia... you've come...
...Yes, Father. I've come to see you.
I brought you some pastries and honey — from Dismania's most famous bakery. I... hope you like them.
Come a little closer, Emilia... Let me have a good look at you...
You've gotten so tall... and so thin. Life at the Academy's still wearing you out, isn't it...?
It's all right — I've been doing fine. Everyone at the Academy's been kind, and they've really looked after me.
Every time Emilia talked about the Academy, she'd cry. She always regretted going there.
You're not Emilia! ...Who are you?
I'm sorry... Mr Gaston. My name is Daphne Theodore. I was... Emilia's friend. I came to visit on her behalf.
Ah... Forgive me, Miss Theodore. I can't even stand to greet you properly.
I've become so forgetful lately... I can barely tell dream from waking. And recently... I keep seeing Emilia. As if she were still alive.
She's so small... just like when she was little... jumping down the stairs into my arms, calling out, "Daddy!"
Mr Gaston... I'm —
No, child. Don't be. I remember now. Emilia was buried a month ago. A kind nurse wheeled me to the service. I left her old rubber duck on the grave — the one she always played with.
She often spoke of you, Miss Theodore. Said you were her closest friend. Please... be careful. The Academy is a dangerous place...
(I knew exactly what Mr Gaston meant. Emilia Gaston — my dear friend — had died in an accident at the Spathatoi.)
—Aargh!
...Mr Gaston!
Are you in pain? I'll get the doctor!
No... child...
My legs are done for. Too long in the trenches... One's been amputated. The other's rotted through.
Hurts like hell — but what of it? I'm still breathing. That's more than I can say for the others... right?
Ugh... aahhh...
(Mr Gaston's pain flared up again. His fists clenched the sheets, veins bulging. He wasn't clinging to life — he was clinging to dignity. The last thing a soldier has left.)
Aaaghhh—!
Miss Theodore — please. Just shoot me. I'm worthless now... I can't even get out of this bed. And now even my only daughter's...
I'll put it in my will — swear it was my choice. I've got no family left anyway. You can even take my old house!
Please, I'm begging you — put me out of my misery! Or at least... cut off the other leg!
No... Mr Gaston, I can't do that!
Please hang in there! Just a little longer! One year... no — six months! I swear, by the Emerald Order, I'll find a cure!
Please — don't give up. Emilia would never have wanted that.
Hngh...
(After the episode passed, the bed finally stilled. Mr Gaston drifted off, sobbing quietly. Whether it was the pain or Emilia's name, I couldn't tell — but something had soothed him.)
(For some, pain is a fate much crueller — and more humiliating — than death. Like a river stone worn smooth over time, it grinds down even the toughest — stripping away their pride and fire.)
(His comrades and daughter rest in the public cemetery. And this small white bed... is his grave.)
(That day, by his bedside, I finally made that decision.)

name: In the Prison of Honour
desc: Turn back — now! This isn't the tower I dreamed of. My dreams held no blood... no wails!
memoryDesc: A scalpel still tainted with blood, bearing silent witness to a tragedy labeled "accident." But she knows it was no accident. The true culprit wasn't any one person — or perhaps, it was everyone.

dialogues.content: We did it, Daphne! We finally synthesized the AG-1899 high-potency painkiller!
Well... I mean, you did it. You did most of the design and experiments, after all. I just helped out...
Don't say that! I never would've joined the project if you hadn't been so insistent.
Daphne... if our drug passes toxicity trials — if the Academy approves mass production...
If it makes it to every hospital — every battlefield—
Then maybe... those tormented by pain might suffer just a little less.
Daphne Theodore.
...Yes, Miss Mason. No... I suppose I should call you Chief now.
That's not what you used to call me at the Academy... Not that it matters anymore.
Now, explain what you have done, Daphne. How did you tick off Dean Silas?
There's nothing to explain. I lied — to Dean Silas, and to the Spathatoi.
I submitted a fake proposal and requested research funding. But I never worked on the intensification serum as Mr Silas required. Instead... I resumed our unfinished painkiller project.
Because I believe it holds far greater value.
I'll accept whatever punishment you see fit, but please — exercise your power as a chief to specially approve AG-1899 for mass production.
It's just a drug. It's done no wrong. And it could spare countless lives from agony.
I don't deny its value. But a drug like this — it could be developed by other alchemists. It would simply take more time.
As a researcher superior to others, you should have served where the Empire needs you most, to meet what the Academy expects.
Now that you've pulled this stunt, even if Silas doesn't punish you, all your research will now be conducted under direct oversight, given his temper.
No, Chief. I won't join the Intensification Project as the dean required. Because I refuse to become the next Emilia Gaston.
Emilia Gaston?
She was reassigned to the Intensification Project before we could finish our work. She didn't want it — not for anything — but she had no say. Because that was the Spathatoi's order.
Ah... the alchemist who died in that accident six months ago.
You're being paranoid. You've always been careful — not like her. She was reckless. Forgot to fasten the restraints... and ended up impaled by a berserk test subject.
...No, Chief. You never really knew Emilia Gaston.
I worked with her for a long time. She was far more meticulous than I ever was.
The report just said she died. What it didn't say was... there was blood everywhere. Still pouring from her chest... And... and even then... not once did she ask for help...
She just kept saying... "I'm sorry" over and over... to the test subject who was still cursing her.
She didn't forget the restraints. She released them... because she couldn't bear to see another human being suffer.
Had it been me... I might've done the same. The only thing that spared me from her fate — was a reassignment letter.
Those test subjects were just dregs of society. I thought Emilia's death might've at least taught you something.
Most Charons are cold, selfish, and cunning. Turn your back, and they'll sink their fangs into your heel without a second thought.
And I'm no different. Cold, selfish, cunning. If you stood above me, you'd crush me — just as easily as I could crush you now.
But you don't. Mercy is a privilege of the strong, Daphne.
...You're right. Emilia unshackled that test subject out of kindness — and he repaid her with a blade to the heart. Yes, they're cold and cunning.
But who made them that way?
Chief — no, Sibylle... I've made my choice. And I won't turn back.
"Alchemy exists to make life better." That's the <H>ideal</> I believed in when I entered the Academy.

I'm going back, Sibylle, to accept the punishment at the Academy... But I still want to beg you for one last time — if you would order the Alchemy to produce AG-1899, all those who are tortured by pain will be extremely grateful to you.
Since you're so set on it, I'll give you a few pieces of advice.
You have been at the Academy for so long and know so many core secrets, Silas will certainly not allow you to go wherever you please. So, you have three options now.
{空格}
A: Let them imprison you or commit you to an asylum, where you will spend the rest of your life.
B: Put this gun to your temple — and go straight to hell.
I've thought about both of these options. What's the third one?
C: File a transfer request to Fulvis. Head to the front lines — and die like a maggot.

The hail of bullets will shred your pride. The pain will rot your dignity. Watching your comrades fall — one by one — will grind your will to dust. And in the end, a meaningless death will devour what you once believed in.
But if, by some miracle, you survive... Then come back to me —
And tell me <H>if you still stay true to your ideals.</>

name: What Awaits Ahead
desc: As the long night nears its end, I too shall set forth. I believe what awaits me ahead is not meaningless death — but something beyond it. Something I must find.
memoryDesc: A small voice recorder, preserving her resolve at the moment of departure.

dialogues.content: This is why I left the Spathatoi. I chose to become a field medic — perhaps the last decision I'll ever get to make for myself.
Dear Mother... By the time you hear this recording, I'll be en route to the front lines. I may not return. I'm sorry to say goodbye this way.
There's a box of painkillers on my desk. Please pass it on to Mr Roger Gaston at Riverside Hospital. I've tested it on myself — it works.
Forgive me for failing to live up to your hopes, Mother. I'm the world's worst daughter... and the most disgraceful deserter.
But I don't regret my choice. Because I believe — someday, far in the future — we'll witness the dawn of a brighter age.
And maybe then, someone will stand at my grave... and say—
Daphne Theodore, you did the right thing.
Avar... look at your daughter. She's just like you — cut from the same cloth! How could she be so... foolish, so selfish, so impossibly stubborn!
Unbelievable! Doesn't she see it? A simple apology — a little compromise — or just asking for my help — and everything could've turned out differently!
...But now I remember.
It was that same naivety... that same foolish defiance... that made me choose you, all those years ago. In the end... the real fool was me.
You two... Please... Come back alive.
Thank goodness you're here! Hurry, come with—
Daphne... my leg's broken. I can't move...
Just leave me here... Go help the others...
No — we're still in range of enemy fire. If you stay, you'll die!
We'll stabilise the fracture now. I'll carry you to the temporary shelter. You're going to be all right!
Don't be afraid... Climb on my back.
The shelling... The Filthoid growls... I can't hear them anymore...
Miss... are we... going home?
...Yes. I gave you a strong painkiller. Just close your eyes and rest... We'll be home soon.
No... you're lying. There's no way back.
Dismania's too far... The rain's pouring. The roads are all mud. We'll never make it back...
Miss... please... Tell my mother...
Third drawer in the bookshelf... The perfume... It was for her birthday... I wanted to... surprise her...
...I promise. I'll get your message to her.
Look out! Hostile Magnetix Drones!
Feeling better now?
Yeah. Thanks for taking out the Magnetix Drones.

Are you out of your mind? Throwing yourself over a dying soldier like that!? He was clearly a goner — were you trying to get yourself killed too? If you'd died, what were the rest of the wounded supposed to do without you?
...Hehe.
What's so funny?
You remind me of my mother. And my senior, back when I was a student. If they were here... they'd have said the same thing.
They always hoped I'd learn. But I never did.
There are so many rational people in this world. They weigh cost against benefit — always choose the "least bad" option. They're born leaders. They steer the course of every era.
But I'm not one of them. I've never been calm enough to think that far ahead. All I can hear... are the cries right in front of me.
Still... I believe a better era should have room — even for short-sighted fools like me.
What are you talking about...
Sorry... I got a little carried away. Just remember this — if you're ever hurt, I won't leave you behind.
...Then you remember this — your life matters too. Don't act like it doesn't. The living can do far more than the dead.
"To carry your comrades' will and live — that's as noble as dying for them." That's what Commander Avar once told us.
He... said that?
I'll keep that in mind.
That's enough rest. Time to move on.
Where are you going?
To check for emergency supplies. And then...
To find Captain {nickname2}, and make sure {性别2:he|she}'s safe.
